<!-- remark-1: body_md -->
\label{rem:exist-points}
The points of Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-a} are critical points of $F_{\zeta^*}$ for an
order parameter $\zeta^*$ that depends on the point. They are not shown to be isolated, to be
strictly stable, or to be critical points of the fixed function $F_{\zeta_f}$. For convex $\xi$ with
at least two active degrees, Theorem~\ref{thm:stab}\ref{thm:stab-a} supplies critical points of $F_{\zeta_f}$
that are locally strongly concave, hence isolated, at rates arbitrarily close to $\Sigma(f)$.
<!-- end remark-1 -->
<!-- proposition-1: body_md -->
\label{prop:max-lower}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. For all $c,t>0$ and all large $N$,
\[
 \mathbb{P}\bigl(M_N<\logZ_N-tN\bigr)\le e^{-cN}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-2: body_md -->
\label{prop:max-upper}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. For all $c,t>0$ and all large $N$,
\[
 \mathbb{P}\bigl(M_N>\logZ_N+tN\bigr)\le e^{-cN}.
\]
<!-- end proposition-2 -->
<!-- proof-1: body_md -->
Attainment of $M_N$ was recalled above.

\ref{thm:max-a} By the two propositions, for every $c>0$,
$\mathbb{P}(|M_N-\logZ_N|>tN)\le2e^{-cN}$ for all large $N$.

\ref{thm:max-b} The case $\theta=0$ is trivial. Fix $\theta\ne0$ and $t>0$, let $C$ be as in
\eqref{eq:max-crude}, and put $G_t=\{|M_N-\logZ_N|\le tN\}$. By~\ref{thm:max-a},
$\mathbb{P}(G_t^c)\le e^{-(3C+2)N}$ for all large $N$. On $G_t$,
$e^{-|\theta|tN}Z_N^\theta\le e^{\thetaM_N}\le e^{|\theta|tN}Z_N^\theta$. Off $G_t$, the
Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and \eqref{eq:max-crude} give
\[
 \mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{\thetaM_N};G_t^c\bigr]\le\bigl(\mathbb{E} e^{2\thetaM_N}\bigr)^{1/2}\mathbb{P}(G_t^c)^{1/2}
 \le e^{-(C+1)N}\le e^{-N}\,\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta,
\]
and the same bound holds for $\mathbb{E}[Z_N^\theta;G_t^c]$. Hence, for all large $N$,
\[
 (1-e^{-N})\,e^{-|\theta|tN}\,\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ \le\ \mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}\ \le\
 \bigl(e^{|\theta|tN}+e^{-N}\bigr)\,\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta .
\]
So $\limsup_N N^{-1}\bigl|\log\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}-\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\bigr|\le|\theta|t$, and $t>0$ is
arbitrary.

\ref{thm:max-c} For $0<t<\varepsilon$ the inclusions
\[
 \bigl\{|N^{-1}\logZ_N-f|\le\varepsilon-t\bigr\}\cap G_t
 \subset\bigl\{|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon\bigr\}
 \subset\bigl\{|N^{-1}\logZ_N-f|\le\varepsilon+t\bigr\}\cup G_t^c
\]
and~\ref{thm:max-a} give the two displayed bounds. Since $c$ is arbitrary, the additive error
$e^{-cN}$ changes neither $\liminf_NN^{-1}\log$ nor $\limsup_NN^{-1}\log$ of the probabilities
involved. The lower bound with $t=\varepsilon/2$ shows that the local rates of $N^{-1}M_N$ at
window $\varepsilon$ are at least those of $N^{-1}\logZ_N$ at window $\varepsilon/2$. The upper
bound with $(\varepsilon,t)$ replaced by $(\varepsilon/2,\varepsilon/4)$ shows that the local rates of
$N^{-1}\logZ_N$ at window $\varepsilon$ are at least those of $N^{-1}M_N$ at window
$\varepsilon/2$. All of them are monotone in $\varepsilon$, so their limits as
$\varepsilon\downarrow0$ coincide. Finally,~\ref{thm:max-a} says that $N^{-1}M_N$ and
$N^{-1}\logZ_N$ are exponentially equivalent, and exponentially equivalent families satisfy the
same large deviation principles with good rate functions \cite[Section~4.2]{DZ}.
<!-- end proof-1 -->
<!-- corollary-1: body_md -->
\label{cor:max-tilt}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. For all $\theta>0$ and $t>0$,
\[
 \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{Q}_\theta\bigl(|M_N-\logZ_N|>tN\bigr)=-\infty .
\]
<!-- end corollary-1 -->
<!-- proof-2: body_md -->
By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and \eqref{eq:max-crude}, every event $A$ satisfies
\[
 \mathbb{Q}_\theta(A)\le\frac{(\mathbb{E}Z_N^{2\theta})^{1/2}\,\mathbb{P}(A)^{1/2}}{\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta}\le e^{2CN}\mathbb{P}(A)^{1/2}.
\]
Apply Theorem~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-a}.
<!-- end proof-2 -->
<!-- remark-2: body_md -->
\label{rem:max-fixedrate}
Every exponential rate is what transfers large deviations in both directions: in the proofs of
Theorem~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-b}--\ref{thm:max-c} the error event must be negligible against
moments and probabilities that are themselves exponentially large or small. For $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$
the upper band at every rate is already in \cite{CPS}, as their Theorem~1 combined with
\eqref{eq:max-band-le} below, and Boursier uses it in this way \cite[Proposition~3.12]{Bou26b}.
The gain is in the lower band.
<!-- end remark-2 -->
<!-- lemma-1: body_md -->
\label{lem:max-truncation}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. For all $c,t>0$ and $L\ge1$ there are $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ and an integer $n$
with $n\ge L$ and $n\ge L/\min(\varepsilon,\delta)$ such that, for all large $N$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:max-band-thm}
 \mathbb{P}^{*}\Bigl(\exists m\in[-1,1]^N:\
 \bigl|F^{\mathrm{band}}_n(m;\varepsilon,\delta)-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\bigr|\ge tN\Bigr)\le e^{-cN}.
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-1 -->
<!-- proof-3: body_md -->
Take $\varepsilon,\delta,n$ from Lemma~\ref{lem:max-truncation} with the given $c,t$ and $L=1$.
Outside the event in \eqref{eq:max-band-thm}, every $m\in[-1,1]^N$ satisfies
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)<F^{\mathrm{band}}_n(m)+tN\le\logZ_N+tN$ by \eqref{eq:max-band-le}. Hence
$M_N<\logZ_N+tN$ there.
<!-- end proof-3 -->
<!-- lemma-2: body_md -->
\label{lem:max-ramsey}
Let $J\ge1$ and $s\ge2$, let $[-1,1]=I_1\sqcup\dots\sqcup I_J$ be a partition into Borel sets, and
put $c_{J,s}=\bigl[J\binom{r_J(s)}{s}\bigr]^{-1}$. For every $N$ and every probability measure $G$
on $\{-1,1\}^N$,
\[
 \max_{k\le J}\ G^{\otimes s}\bigl(R(\sigma^i,\sigma^j)\in I_k\ \text{for all }
 1\le i<j\le s\bigr)\ \ge\ c_{J,s}.
\]
<!-- end lemma-2 -->
<!-- proof-4: body_md -->
Let $r=r_J(s)$ and sample $\sigma^1,\dots,\sigma^r$ independently from $G$. Color each pair
$\{i,j\}\subset\{1,\dots,r\}$ by the index $k$ with $R(\sigma^i,\sigma^j)\in I_k$; two equal
samples have overlap one and receive the color of the bin that contains one. By Ramsey's theorem,
for every outcome some $s$-element set $S\subset\{1,\dots,r\}$ is monochromatic, so
\[
 \sum_{|S|=s}\ \sum_{k\le J}\mathbf{1}\bigl\{\text{all pairs in } S \text{ have color } k\bigr\}\ge1
\]
pointwise. Take expectations. For each $S$ the samples $(\sigma^i)_{i\in S}$ are independent with
law $G$, so each of the $\binom rs$ sets contributes
$\sum_kG^{\otimes s}(R(\sigma^i,\sigma^j)\in I_k\ \forall i<j)$, and this sum is therefore at
least $\binom rs^{-1}$. The largest of its $J$ terms is at least the average.
<!-- end proof-4 -->
<!-- lemma-3: body_md -->
\label{lem:max-band}
Let $H$ be a real function on $[-1,1]^N$, $Z=2^{-N}\sum_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^N}e^{H(\sigma)}$ and
$G(\sigma)=2^{-N}e^{H(\sigma)}/Z$, and define $F^{\mathrm{band}}_n$ by \eqref{eq:max-band} with $H$
in place of $H_N$. Let $q\in[-1,1]$, $\varepsilon,\delta>0$, let $n\ge4/\min(\varepsilon,\delta)$ be
an integer and $\tau\in(0,\min(\varepsilon,\delta)/4]$. If $G^{\otimes2n}(A_{2n}(q,\tau))>0$, there
is $m\in[-1,1]^N$, the barycenter of $n$ points of $\{-1,1\}^N$, such that
$|q_m-q|<(1-q)/n+\tau$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:max-band-step}
 F^{\mathrm{band}}_n(m;\varepsilon,\delta)\ \ge\ \log Z+\frac1n\log G^{\otimes2n}\bigl(A_{2n}(q,\tau)\bigr).
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-3 -->
<!-- proof-5: body_md -->
\emph{An outer block.} Split a $2n$-tuple into an inner block $(\sigma^1,\dots,\sigma^n)$ and an
outer block $\bar\sigma=(\bar\sigma^{n+1},\dots,\bar\sigma^{2n})$. For an outer block whose pairwise
overlaps lie in $(q-\tau,q+\tau)$, let $A_n(\bar\sigma)$ be the set of inner blocks that complete
it to a point of $A_{2n}(q,\tau)$. Then
\[
 G^{\otimes2n}\bigl(A_{2n}(q,\tau)\bigr)=\sum_{\bar\sigma}G^{\otimes n}(\bar\sigma)\,
 G^{\otimes n}\bigl(A_n(\bar\sigma)\bigr),
\]
the sum running over such outer blocks. The weights $G^{\otimes n}(\bar\sigma)$ sum to at most
one, so some outer block $\bar\sigma$ in the sum has
$G^{\otimes n}(A_n(\bar\sigma))\ge G^{\otimes2n}(A_{2n}(q,\tau))$. Fix it.

\emph{Its barycenter.} Let $m=n^{-1}\sum_{k=n+1}^{2n}\bar\sigma^k\in[-1,1]^N$. Then
\[
 q_m=\frac1n+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k\ne k'}R(\bar\sigma^k,\bar\sigma^{k'}),\qquad
 q_m-q=\frac{1-q}n+\frac1{n^2}\sum_{k\ne k'}\bigl(R(\bar\sigma^k,\bar\sigma^{k'})-q\bigr),
\]
and the last sum has $n(n-1)$ terms of modulus less than $\tau$. Hence
$|q_m-q|<(1-q)/n+\tau\le2/n+\tau$. Now let $(\sigma^1,\dots,\sigma^n)\in A_n(\bar\sigma)$. Each
$R(\sigma^i,m)=n^{-1}\sum_kR(\sigma^i,\bar\sigma^k)$ lies in $(q-\tau,q+\tau)$, and so does
each $R(\sigma^i,\sigma^j)$ with $i\ne j$. Therefore $|R(\sigma^i,m)-q_m|$ and
$|R(\sigma^i,\sigma^j)-q_m|$ are less than $2\tau+2/n\le\min(\varepsilon,\delta)$, by the choice
of $n$ and $\tau$. So $A_n(\bar\sigma)\subsetB_n(m,\varepsilon,\delta)$.

\emph{The bound.} By \eqref{eq:max-band-gibbs} with $H$ in place of $H_N$,
\begin{align*}
 F^{\mathrm{band}}_n(m)=\log Z+\frac1n\log G^{\otimes n}\bigl(B_n(m,\varepsilon,\delta)\bigr)
 &\ge\log Z+\frac1n\log G^{\otimes n}\bigl(A_n(\bar\sigma)\bigr)\\
 &\ge\log Z+\frac1n\log G^{\otimes2n}\bigl(A_{2n}(q,\tau)\bigr).\qedhere
\end{align*}
<!-- end proof-5 -->
<!-- proof-6: body_md -->
Fix $c,t>0$. Lemma~\ref{lem:max-truncation} with $(c,t/2,L=4)$ gives $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ and an
integer $n\ge4/\min(\varepsilon,\delta)$ such that the event
\[
 \Omega_N^{\mathrm{bad}}=\bigl\{\exists m\in[-1,1]^N:\
 |F^{\mathrm{band}}_n(m;\varepsilon,\delta)-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)|\ge tN/2\bigr\}
\]
has outer probability at most $e^{-cN}$ for all large $N$. Put $\tau=\min(\varepsilon,\delta)/4$
and $J=\lceil2/\tau\rceil$, and cut $[-1,1]$ into the intervals
$I_k=[-1+2(k-1)/J,\,-1+2k/J)$ for $k<J$ and $I_J=[1-2/J,1]$, with midpoints $q_k$. An overlap in
$I_k$ lies within $1/J\le\tau/2$ of $q_k$, so the event that all pairwise overlaps lie in $I_k$ is
contained in $A_{2n}(q_k,\tau)$. Lemma~\ref{lem:max-ramsey} with $s=2n$ and $G=G_N$ gives, for
every $N$ and every realization, an index $k$ with
\[
 G_N^{\otimes2n}\bigl(A_{2n}(q_k,\tau)\bigr)\ge c_{J,2n}.
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:max-band} with $H=H_N$ then gives $m\in[-1,1]^N$ with
$F^{\mathrm{band}}_n(m)\ge\logZ_N-n^{-1}\log(1/c_{J,2n})$. Outside $\Omega_N^{\mathrm{bad}}$,
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)>F^{\mathrm{band}}_n(m)-tN/2$, so
\[
 M_N\geF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)>\logZ_N-\frac{tN}2-\frac1n\log\frac1{c_{J,2n}}\ge\logZ_N-tN
\]
as soon as $N\ge2\log(1/c_{J,2n})/(nt)$. Thus $\{M_N<\logZ_N-tN\}\subset\Omega_N^{\mathrm{bad}}$ for
all large $N$, and the claim follows from \eqref{eq:max-band-thm}.
<!-- end proof-6 -->
<!-- remark-3: body_md -->
\label{rem:max-witness}
The barycenter $m$ has self-overlap within $2/n+\tau$ of the bin midpoint $q_k$; the bin depends on
the realization, and nothing in the argument locates it. It may even be negative: positive
semidefiniteness of the overlap matrix of $2n$ replicas only forces $q_k>-1/(2n-1)-\tau$. For convex
$\xi$ the variational side locates the level: outside an event of outer probability at most
$e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c)}$, every $m$ with $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f-\delta)$ sits near the contact set $C_f$
(Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-i}), and for convex $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$ this holds conditionally
on an upper deviation of the free energy (Corollary~\ref{cor:title}). For every mixture,
Proposition~\ref{rem:max-overlap} in
Appendix~\ref{app:var-overlap} gives a cruder lower bound on its self-overlap.
<!-- end remark-3 -->
<!-- proposition-3: body_md -->
\label{prop:max-fm}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ and $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$, and let $\theta\in(0,1)$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{prop:max-fm-a} $\limsup_N N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le\Lambda(\theta)$.
\item\label{prop:max-fm-b} If $\theta\le\theta_*$, then
 $\liminf_N N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ge\Lambda(\theta)=\thetaf_{\mathrm{eq}}$.
\item\label{prop:max-fm-c} If $\xi$ is even, then $\liminf_N N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ge\Lambda(\theta)$.
\item\label{prop:max-fm-d} If $\xi$ is not even, then
 $\liminf_N N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ge\Lambda(\theta)$.
\end{thmlist}
In particular \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ holds.
<!-- end proposition-3 -->
<!-- remark-4: body_md -->
\label{rem:max-routes}
Boursier bounds $\limsup_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}\le\Lambda(\theta)$ directly, for
$\theta\in(0,1)$ and $\xi$ in her class \cite[Proposition~2.7]{Bou26b}; by
Theorem~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-b} this is equivalent to
Proposition~\ref{prop:max-fm}\ref{prop:max-fm-a}. For convex $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$ the lower half of
\hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ also has proofs that avoid \cite[Section~7]{Tal07}: with two active degrees the argument
for item~\ref{prop:max-fm-d} applies whether or not $\xi$ is even, and for $\xi(t)=\beta^2t^p$ with
$p$ even Appendix~\ref{app:moments-pure} perturbs $\xi$ by a second degree and transfers $M_N$
back (Proposition~\ref{prop:moments-pure}).
<!-- end remark-4 -->
<!-- proof-7: body_md -->
Parts~\ref{thm:exist-a} and~\ref{thm:exist-b} are
Lemmas~\ref{lem:gauss-interior}, \ref{lem:gauss-critical}, \ref{lem:var-basic} and
Proposition~\ref{prop:var-regular}, as discussed above.

\ref{thm:exist-c} If $\mathrm{FM}(\xi,\theta)$ holds, Theorem~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-b} gives
$\lim_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}=\lim_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta=\Lambda(\theta)$. At $\theta=1$ no
assumption is needed. Since $\operatorname{Var}H_N(\sigma)=N\xi(1)$ for $\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^N$, $\mathbb{E}Z_N=e^{N\xi(1)/2}$
exactly, and Theorem~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-b} gives $\lim_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{E} e^{M_N}=\xi(1)/2$.
Under \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}, Lemma~\ref{lem:var-dual} gives
$\overline{\Lambda}(1)=\lim_{\theta\uparrow1}\Lambda(\theta)=P_{\delta_0}=\xi(1)/2$.

\ref{thm:exist-d} Fix $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ and put $\theta=\theta_f\in(\theta_*,1)$. By~\ref{thm:exist-b},
$\Lambda'(\theta)=f$ and $\Sigma(f)=\Lambda(\theta)-\theta f$; by~\ref{thm:exist-c} and \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}},
$N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E} e^{sM_N}\to\Lambda(s)$ for every $s\in(0,1)$. Let $\varepsilon>0$.

\emph{Upper bound.} Chebyshev's inequality at $\theta$ gives
\[
 \mathbb{P}\bigl(|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon\bigr)\le\mathbb{P}\bigl(M_N\ge N(f-\varepsilon)\bigr)
 \le e^{-\theta N(f-\varepsilon)}\,\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N},
\]
so the $\limsup$ of $N^{-1}\log$ of both probabilities is at most
$\Lambda(\theta)-\theta f+\theta\varepsilon=\Sigma(f)+\theta\varepsilon$.

\emph{Lower bound.} Let $\tilde\mathbb{P}=e^{\thetaM_N}\,d\mathbb{P}/\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}$. Then
\[
 \mathbb{P}\bigl(|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon\bigr)
 \ge e^{-\theta N(f+\varepsilon)}\,\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}\,
 \tilde\mathbb{P}\bigl(|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon\bigr).
\]
For $0<\eta<\min(\theta,1-\theta)$, Chebyshev's inequality under $\tilde\mathbb{P}$ gives
\[
 \tilde\mathbb{P}\bigl(M_N>N(f+\varepsilon)\bigr)\le e^{-\eta N(f+\varepsilon)}
 \frac{\mathbb{E} e^{(\theta+\eta)M_N}}{\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}},\qquad
 \tilde\mathbb{P}\bigl(M_N<N(f-\varepsilon)\bigr)\le e^{\eta N(f-\varepsilon)}
 \frac{\mathbb{E} e^{(\theta-\eta)M_N}}{\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}} .
\]
After $N^{-1}\log$, the right-hand sides tend to
$\Lambda(\theta\pm\eta)-\Lambda(\theta)\mp\eta f-\eta\varepsilon$, which equals
$-\eta\varepsilon+o(\eta)$ because $\Lambda'(\theta)=f$. Fixing $\eta$ small, we get
$\tilde\mathbb{P}(|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon)\to1$, hence
$\liminf_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon)\ge\Lambda(\theta)-\theta(f+\varepsilon)
=\Sigma(f)-\theta\varepsilon$. Letting $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ proves the first claim.

\emph{The existence event.} If $|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon$, then by~\ref{thm:exist-a} every
maximizer $x^*$ and its order parameter $\zeta^*$ satisfy \eqref{eq:event-exist}. Since
$M_N\geF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)$ for every $x$, almost surely
\[
 \bigl\{|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon\bigr\}\subset\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)
 \subset\bigl\{M_N\ge N(f-\varepsilon)\bigr\}.
\]
The lower bound applies to the smaller event and the upper bound to the larger one, so the same
limits hold for $\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)$, for its inner and for its outer probability.

\ref{thm:exist-e} This is Proposition~\ref{prop:max-fm}.
<!-- end proof-7 -->
<!-- lemma-4: body_md -->
\label{lem:loc-obstacle}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ and let $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$.
\begin{thmlist}[beginpenalty=10000]
\item\label{lem:loc-obstacle-a} $\overline{\Lambda}$ is convex and lower semicontinuous on $[0,1]$, and
 $\overline{\Lambda}'_+(0)=f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. The function $\theta\mapsto\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta f$ has exactly one
 minimizer $\theta_f$ on $[0,1]$; it lies in $(0,1)$, and $\Sigma(f)=\Lambda(\theta_f)-\theta_f f$.
\item\label{lem:loc-obstacle-b} The infimum of $P_\zeta$ over
 $\{\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1]):\zeta(\{0\})\ge\theta_f\}$ is attained. Every minimizer $\zeta_f$ satisfies
 $\zeta_f(\{0\})=\theta_f$ and $\Sigma(f)=\theta_f(P_{\zeta_f}-f)$.
\item\label{lem:loc-obstacle-c} Let $\zeta_f$ be such a minimizer and $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}$. Then
 $\mathcal{O}\in C^1([0,1])$, $\mathcal{O}'(t)=-\frac12\xi''(t)(\Gamma_{\zeta_f}(t)-t)$ and $\mathcal{O}(1)=0$. The minimum
 $\mathcal{O}_{\min}$ of $\mathcal{O}$ over $(0,1]$ is attained, $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_{\min}$ on $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_f\cap(0,1]$, and
 \[
  \mathcal{O}(0)>\mathcal{O}_{\min},\qquad \mathcal{O}(1)>\mathcal{O}_{\min} .
 \]
 In particular $C_f=\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}$ is a nonempty compact subset of $(0,1)$ that
 contains $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_f\cap(0,1]$.
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end lemma-4 -->
<!-- proposition-4: body_md -->
\label{prop:glued-comparison}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}. Let $\theta\in(0,1)$, $Q\in[0,1)$ and $\rho\in[0,1-Q]$, with $\rho>0$ if
$Q=0$. Let the data be as follows.
\begin{itemize}[leftmargin=*,topsep=2pt,itemsep=1pt]
\item If $Q>0$: a step function $\mathsf{x}:[0,Q)\to(\theta,3]$ equal to $\mathsf{x}_\ell$ on
 $[q_{\ell-1},q_\ell)$ for $\ell=1,\dots,L$, where $0=q_0<q_1<\dots<q_L=Q$ and
 $\theta<\mathsf{x}_1<\dots<\mathsf{x}_L$; put $y=\mathsf{x}_L$. If $Q=0$ there is no $\mathsf{x}$, and $y=1$.
\item A measure $\eta\in\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$ whose distribution function $\bar{\eta}$ is a step
 function. No relation between $\mathsf{x}(Q-)$ and $\bar{\eta}(Q)$ is assumed.
\item A function $g_0\in C^2([-1,1])$ and $s\in\mathbb{R}$ with $|s|\,\|g_0''\|_\infty\le\frac12$.
\end{itemize}
Let $\Psi_s(z)=\sup_{|m|\le1}\{zm+\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q,m)+s\,g_0(m)\}$ for $z\in\mathbb{R}$; let $W_s$ be
the solution on $[0,Q]\times\mathbb{R}$ of
$\partial_tW+\frac{\xi''}2\bigl(\partial_x^2W+\mathsf{x}\,(\partial_xW)^2\bigr)=0$ with
$W(Q,\cdot)=\Psi_s$ (and $W_s(0,0)=\Psi_s(0)$ if $Q=0$); and let
\[
 P_s(\mathsf{x},\eta)=W_s(0,0)-\frac12\int_0^Qt\xi''(t)\mathsf{x}(t)\,dt
 -\frac12\int_Q^1t\xi''(t)\bar{\eta}(t)\,dt .
\]
Then for every $N\ge1$ there is a random variable $\mathcal T$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:loc-glued-pointwise}
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)+s\sum_{i=1}^Ng_0(m_i)\le N P_s(\mathsf{x},\eta)+\mathcal T
 \qquad\text{for every } m\in[-1,1]^N \text{ with } q_m\in[Q,Q+\rho],
\end{equation}
and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:loc-glued-moment}
 \mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T}\le
 \exp\Bigl\{\theta\Bigl(NC_R\rho+\mathbf{1}_{\rho>0}\,\frac{\log(N+1)}{y}\Bigr)\Bigr\},
 \qquad C_R=5\xi''(1).
\end{equation}
<!-- end proposition-4 -->
<!-- proposition-5: body_md -->
\label{prop:loc-gap}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ and let $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{prop:loc-gap-a} $p_Q\le P_{\zeta_f}$ for every $Q\in[0,1)$.
\item\label{prop:loc-gap-b} $p_Q=P_{\zeta_f}$ for every $Q\inC_f$.
\item\label{prop:loc-gap-c} For every $Q\in[0,1)\setminusC_f$ there are data
 $(\mathsf{x},\eta)\in\mathcal A_Q$ with
 \[
  P(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta))\le P_{\zeta_f}-\varphi\bigl(\mathcal{O}(Q)-\mathcal{O}_{\min}\bigr).
 \]
 In particular $p_Q\le P_{\zeta_f}-\varphi(\mathcal{O}(Q)-\mathcal{O}_{\min})$, a gap that depends on $Q$ only through
 $\mathcal{O}(Q)$.
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end proposition-5 -->
<!-- proof-8: body_md -->
We prove~\ref{prop:loc-gap-a}, \ref{prop:loc-gap-b}, and~\ref{prop:loc-gap-c} in full when
$C_f$ meets $[0,Q)$; the other case of~\ref{prop:loc-gap-c} is the same computation, sketched
here and written out in Appendix~\ref{app:var-gap}.

\ref{prop:loc-gap-a} Since $\bar{\zeta_f}\ge\zeta_f(\{0\})=\theta_f$, the pair
$(\bar{\zeta_f}|_{[0,Q)},\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta_f)$ lies in $\mathcal A_Q$, and its glued coefficient is
$\bar{\zeta_f}$.

\ref{prop:loc-gap-c}, \emph{direction (A)}. Suppose that $C_f$ contains a point $r<Q$. Let
$h=\mathbf{1}_{[r,Q)}$ and, for $0<\varepsilon\le\theta_f$, take $\mathsf{x}=\bar{\zeta_f}+\varepsilon h$ on
$[0,Q)$ and $\eta=\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta_f$. Then $\mathsf{x}$ is nondecreasing with values in
$[\theta_f,1+\theta_f]\subset[\theta_f,2]$, so $(\mathsf{x},\eta)\in\mathcal A_Q$, and
$\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)=\bar{\zeta_f}+\varepsilon h$. The first variation is
\[
 DP(\bar{\zeta_f})[h]=-\int_r^Q\mathcal{O}'(t)\,dt=\mathcal{O}(r)-\mathcal{O}(Q)=-d,\qquad d:=\mathcal{O}(Q)-\mathcal{O}_{\min} .
\]
As $\|h\|_{L^1}\le1$, \eqref{eq:loc-second-order} gives
$P(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta))\le P_{\zeta_f}-\varepsilon d+K\varepsilon^2$. If $d\le2K\theta_f$, the choice
$\varepsilon=d/(2K)$ gives $-\varepsilon d+K\varepsilon^2=-d^2/(4K)$. Otherwise take
$\varepsilon=\theta_f$; then $K\theta_f<d/2$ and $-\varepsilon d+K\varepsilon^2\le-\theta_f d/2$. In both
cases the gain is at least $\varphi(d)$.

\emph{Direction (B).} If $C_f$ has no point below $Q$ (this includes $Q=0$ and every
$Q<\minC_f$), it has a point $r\in(Q,1)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-c},
and one lowers the band distribution function by $\varepsilon$ on $[Q,r)$ instead: keep
$\mathsf{x}=\bar{\zeta_f}|_{[0,Q)}$ and take $\eta=\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta_f-\varepsilon\delta_Q+\varepsilon\delta_r$, a
probability measure for $\varepsilon\le\theta_f$ because $\bar{\zeta_f}(Q)\ge\zeta_f(\{0\})=\theta_f$. The
first variation is again $\mathcal{O}(r)-\mathcal{O}(Q)$, and the same choice of $\varepsilon$ applies;
Appendix~\ref{app:var-gap} gives the details.

\ref{prop:loc-gap-b} Let $Q\inC_f$ and $(\mathsf{x},\eta)\in\mathcal A_Q$. After a change of $\mathsf{x}$ on
a countable set, which does not change $P$, $\mathsf{x}(t)=\alpha([0,t])$ for a finite measure $\alpha$
on $[0,Q)$ with $\alpha(\{0\})\ge\theta_f$. By Fubini and $\mathcal{O}(1)=0$,
\[
 \int_0^1\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)\,(-\mathcal{O}')\,dt
 =\int_{[0,Q)}\bigl(\mathcal{O}(t)-\mathcal{O}(Q)\bigr)\,\alpha(dt)+\int_{[Q,1]}\mathcal{O}\,d\eta ,
\]
and the same computation with Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle} gives
$\int_0^1\bar{\zeta_f}(-\mathcal{O}')\,dt=\int\mathcal{O}\,d\zeta_f=\theta_f\mathcal{O}(0)+(1-\theta_f)\mathcal{O}_{\min}$. Since
$\mathcal{O}(Q)=\mathcal{O}_{\min}\le\mathcal{O}$ on $(0,1]$, $\mathcal{O}(0)>\mathcal{O}_{\min}$ and $\alpha(\{0\})\ge\theta_f$, the first integral
is at least $\theta_f(\mathcal{O}(0)-\mathcal{O}_{\min})$, and the second is at least $\mathcal{O}_{\min}$. Hence
\[
 DP(\bar{\zeta_f})\bigl[\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)-\bar{\zeta_f}\bigr]
 \ge\theta_f\bigl(\mathcal{O}(0)-\mathcal{O}_{\min}\bigr)+\mathcal{O}_{\min}-\theta_f\mathcal{O}(0)-(1-\theta_f)\mathcal{O}_{\min}=0,
\]
and~\eqref{eq:loc-first-order} gives $P(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta))\ge P_{\zeta_f}$. With~\ref{prop:loc-gap-a},
$p_Q=P_{\zeta_f}$.
<!-- end proof-8 -->
<!-- lemma-5: body_md -->
\label{lem:loc-monotone}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ and let $Q\in(0,1)$. If $(\mathsf{x},\eta)\in\mathcal A_Q$ and $\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)$ is
nondecreasing on $[0,1)$, then $P(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta))\ge P_{\zeta_f}$.
<!-- end lemma-5 -->
<!-- proof-9: body_md -->
Monotonicity across $Q$ forces $\mathsf{x}\le\bar{\eta}(Q)\le1$. So the glued coefficient agrees, off a
countable set, with a right-continuous nondecreasing function with values in $[\theta_f,1]$, that is,
with the distribution function of some $\mu\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$; and
$\mu(\{0\})=\mathsf{x}(0+)\ge\theta_f$. Since $P$ depends on a coefficient only through its class in $L^1$,
$P(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta))=P_\mu\ge\inf\{P_{\mu'}:\mu'(\{0\})\ge\theta_f\}=P_{\zeta_f}$.
<!-- end proof-9 -->
<!-- remark-5: body_md -->
\label{rem:loc-jump}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-monotone}, for $Q>0$ every gain in
Proposition~\ref{prop:loc-gap}\ref{prop:loc-gap-c} comes from a downward jump
$\mathsf{x}(Q-)>\bar{\eta}(Q)$ of the glued coefficient. Both directions create such a jump by moving
mass across $Q$ towards a point of $C_f$. In direction (A) the coefficient is raised by
$\varepsilon$ on $[r,Q)$ and then drops by $\varepsilon$ at $Q$, since $\zeta_f$ has no atom at
$Q\notinC_f$ (Figure~\ref{fig:obstacle}); in direction (B) the band distribution function is
lowered on $[Q,r)$. The size of the gain is governed by $\mathcal{O}(Q)-\mathcal{O}_{\min}$, which compares the
obstacle at $Q$ with its global minimum wherever that minimum is attained. This is why the
radii of near-maximizers localize on the set of global minimizers of $\mathcal{O}$, and not merely
near its stationary points (compare Remark~\ref{rem:loc-stationary}). Boursier's band comparison
already uses a strict obstacle gap of this kind, for competitors whose overlap with a given state
is a fixed value below the first contact \cite[Proposition~3.9 and Lemma~3.10,
(3.15)--(3.16)]{Bou26b}; here the gap
controls the self-overlaps of all near-maximizers, through the jump at the radius.
<!-- end remark-5 -->
<!-- proof-10: body_md -->
Fix $\kappa>0$ and write $\theta=\theta_f$, $\zeta=\zeta_f$, $\mathcal{O}=\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}$. Let
$\mathcal Q_\kappa=\{Q\in[0,1]:\operatorname{dist}(Q,C_f)\ge\kappa/2\}$. If $\mathcal Q_\kappa$ is empty, no $m$ has
$\operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_f)\ge\kappa$ and there is nothing to prove. Otherwise
\[
 \gamma_\kappa=\min_{Q\in \mathcal Q_\kappa}\bigl(\mathcal{O}(Q)-\mathcal{O}_{\min}\bigr)>0,
\]
because $\mathcal{O}$ is continuous on $[0,1]$, $\mathcal{O}>\mathcal{O}_{\min}$ on $(0,1]\setminusC_f$, and
$\mathcal{O}(0)>\mathcal{O}_{\min}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-c}). Put
$\varphi_\kappa=\varphi(\gamma_\kappa)$, choose $\rho\in(0,\kappa/2)$ with $C_R\rho\le\varphi_\kappa/8$, and
set $\delta=\varphi_\kappa/8$.

\emph{Shells.} Let $Q_j=j\rho$ and $I_j=[Q_j,\min(Q_j+\rho,1)]$ for the integers $j\ge0$ with
$Q_j<1$. If $\operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_f)\ge\kappa$, then $q_m\in I_j$ for some such $j$, and
$\operatorname{dist}(Q_j,C_f)\ge\kappa-\rho>\kappa/2$, so $Q_j\in \mathcal Q_\kappa$. Call such $j$ \emph{bad}.

\emph{One shell.} Let $j$ be bad. Proposition~\ref{prop:loc-gap}\ref{prop:loc-gap-c} gives data
in $\mathcal A_{Q_j}$ whose glued coefficient has
$P\le P_\zeta-\varphi(\mathcal{O}(Q_j)-\mathcal{O}_{\min})\le P_\zeta-\varphi_\kappa$, since $\varphi$ is
increasing. Then~\eqref{eq:loc-glued-general}, with $s=0$, shell width $\min(\rho,1-Q_j)$ and
$\varepsilon_A=\varphi_\kappa/2$, gives a random variable $\mathcal T_j$ with
\[
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\le N\Bigl(P_\zeta-\frac{\varphi_\kappa}2\Bigr)+\mathcal T_j\quad\text{for } q_m\in I_j,
 \qquad \mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T_j}\le(N+1)\,e^{N\theta C_R\rho}.
\]
Hence
$\{\exists m:q_m\in I_j,\ F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f-\delta)\}\subset
\{\mathcal T_j\ge N(f-\delta-P_\zeta+\varphi_\kappa/2)\}$, and Markov's inequality, together with
$\Sigma(f)=\theta(P_\zeta-f)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}\ref{lem:loc-obstacle-b}), bounds the
probability of the latter event by
\[
 (N+1)\exp N\Bigl[\theta(P_\zeta-f)-\frac{\theta\varphi_\kappa}2+\theta\delta+\theta C_R\rho\Bigr]
 \le(N+1)\,e^{N(\Sigma(f)-\theta\varphi_\kappa/4)} .
\]

\emph{Union bound.} There are at most $\lceil1/\rho\rceil+1$ shells. The event in
\ref{thm:struct-i} is therefore contained in a finite union of measurable events of total
probability at most $(\lceil1/\rho\rceil+1)(N+1)e^{N(\Sigma(f)-\theta\varphi_\kappa/4)}$, which is at
most $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-\theta\varphi_\kappa/8)}$ for all large $N$. This proves~\ref{thm:struct-i} with
\[
 \delta=\frac{\varphi(\gamma_\kappa)}8,\qquad c=\frac{\theta_f\,\varphi(\gamma_\kappa)}8 ,
\]
where $\varphi$ is the function~\eqref{eq:loc-gap-function}, whose constant $K$ depends only on
$\xi'(1)$ and $\xi''(1)$, and $\gamma_\kappa$ measures how far the obstacle rises above its
minimum at distance at least $\kappa/2$ from $C_f$.
<!-- end proof-10 -->
<!-- proof-11: body_md -->
Fix $\kappa>0$ and let $X$ be the Auffinger--Chen process of $\zeta_f$, so that
$L_{q}=\operatorname{Law}(\Phi_{\zeta_f,x}(q,X_q))$.

\emph{Finitely many test functions.} By Kantorovich--Rubinstein duality on $[-1,1]$, a net and a
mollification, there are smooth $g_1,\dots,g_J$ with $\|g_j'\|_\infty\le1$ such that, whenever
$W_1(\mu_m,L_{q_m})\ge\kappa$, some $j$ satisfies
\begin{equation}\label{eq:loc-field-bad}
 \frac1N\sum_{i=1}^Ng_j(m_i)\ge\int g_j\,dL_{q_m}+\frac\kappa2 .
\end{equation}
The maps $q\mapsto\int g_j\,dL_{q}$ are uniformly continuous on $[0,1]$, since
$q\mapsto\Phi_{\zeta_f,x}(q,X_q)$ is almost surely continuous and bounded
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}); let $\omega$ be a common modulus of continuity.

\emph{The tangent bound.} Fix a radius $Q$ and take the base data
$(\bar{\zeta_f}|_{[0,Q)},\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta_f)$, for which $P_0=P_{\zeta_f}$, with $g_0=g_j$. For these data (through step
approximants, Appendix~\ref{app:var-field}) the maximizer in the definition of $\Psi_0(z)$ is $m=\Phi_{\zeta_f,x}(Q,z)$, so
$\Psi_s(z)=\Psi_0(z)+s\,g_j(\Phi_{\zeta_f,x}(Q,z))+O(s^2)$ uniformly in $z$. The terminal sandwich
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-terminal}) and the stability of the Auffinger--Chen process under a change of
the terminal condition (Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-stability}) carry this expansion to the initial
value:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:loc-tangent}
 P_s\bigl(\bar{\zeta_f}|_{[0,Q)},\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta_f\bigr)
 \le P_{\zeta_f}+s\int g_j\,dL_{Q}+C_2s^2,
 \qquad 0\le s\le\bigl(2\|g_j''\|_\infty\bigr)^{-1},
\end{equation}
with $C_2$ depending only on $\xi'(1)$ and $\xi''(1)$, uniformly in $Q$ and $j$. So, to first
order in $s$, the perturbation $s\sum_ig_j(m_i)$ costs the bound no more than $s$ times the mean
of $g_j$ under the field law at the radius; a near-maximizer whose coordinates give $g_j$ a larger
mean gains more than the bound allows, and Markov's inequality detects this. The perturbation
follows the device by which \cite[Theorem~5]{CPS2} identifies the energy of near-maximizers on a
sphere whose radius lies in the support of the Parisi measure, there by convexity in the inverse
temperature.

\emph{Markov's inequality.} Let $I=[Q,Q+\rho]$ be a shell. If $q_m\in I$,
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f-\delta)$ and~\eqref{eq:loc-field-bad} holds, then
\[
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)+s\sum_{i=1}^Ng_j(m_i)\ge N\Bigl[f-\delta+s\Bigl(\int g_j\,dL_{Q}-\omega(\rho)
 +\frac\kappa2\Bigr)\Bigr],
\]
while by~\eqref{eq:loc-glued-general} and~\eqref{eq:loc-tangent} the left side is at most
$N[P_{\zeta_f}+s\int g_j\,dL_{Q}+C_2s^2+\varepsilon_A]+\mathcal T$. The terms
$s\int g_j\,dL_{Q}$ cancel, and Markov's inequality with $\Sigma(f)=\theta_f(P_{\zeta_f}-f)$ bounds the
probability of this event by
\[
 (N+1)\exp N\Bigl\{\Sigma(f)+\theta_f\Bigl[C_2s^2+\varepsilon_A+C_R\rho+\delta+s\,\omega(\rho)
 -\frac{s\kappa}2\Bigr]\Bigr\}.
\]
The gain $s\kappa/2$ is linear in $s$ and the cost $C_2s^2$ is quadratic. Appendix~\ref{app:var-field}
takes $s\le\kappa/(8C_2)$, and then $\rho$, $\delta$ and $\varepsilon_A$ small compared with
$s\kappa$, so that the bracket is at most $-\frac5{32}s\kappa$. A union over the finitely many
shells and test functions gives~\ref{thm:struct-ii}, with $c=\theta_f s\kappa/8$.
<!-- end proof-11 -->
<!-- remark-6: body_md -->
\label{rem:loc-stationary}
Since $t\mapsto t^2$ is $2$-Lipschitz on $[-1,1]$, $q_m=\int t^2\,\mu_m(dt)$ and
$\Gamma_{\zeta_f}(q)=\int t^2\,L_{q}(dt)$, one has $|q_m-\Gamma_{\zeta_f}(q_m)|\le2\,W_1(\mu_m,L_{q_m})$.
So~\ref{thm:struct-ii} alone places $q_m$ near the zero set of $\Gamma_{\zeta_f}(t)-t$, which consists of
$0$ and the points of $(0,1)$ where $\mathcal{O}'$ vanishes. Our proof excludes the stationary points that
are not global minimizers of $\mathcal{O}$ through~\ref{thm:struct-i}, that is, through the downward jump
of the glued coefficient (Remark~\ref{rem:loc-jump}).
<!-- end remark-6 -->
<!-- lemma-6: body_md -->
\label{lem:hess-pastur}
Let $a\ge0$ and $\rho\in\mathcal{P}([0,\infty))$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:hess-pastur-a} There is a unique probability measure $\nu=\nu[a,\rho]$ on
 $\mathbb{R}$ whose Cauchy transform $g(w)=\int\nu(d\lambda)/(w-\lambda)$ satisfies
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:hess-pastur}
  g(w)=\int\frac{\rho(dD)}{w+D-a\,g(w)}\qquad\text{for every } w\in\mathbb{C}^+ .
 \end{equation}
 For each $w\in\mathbb{C}^+$, equation~\eqref{eq:hess-pastur} has at most one solution $g(w)$ with
 $\operatorname{Im}g(w)<0$. If $D_N$ are real diagonal matrices with $\operatorname{ESD}(D_N)\to\rho$ weakly,
 then $\operatorname{ESD}(\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N)\to\nu$ weakly in probability, and the expected empirical spectral
 distribution converges weakly to $\nu$.
\item\label{lem:hess-pastur-b} $\nu((2\sqrt a,\infty))=0$, and
 $\nu((-\infty,-2\sqrt a-s))\le\rho([s,\infty))$ for every $s\ge0$.
\item\label{lem:hess-pastur-c} If $a_n\to a$ and $\rho_n\to\rho$ weakly, then
 $\nu[a_n,\rho_n]\to\nu[a,\rho]$ weakly. Hence, for $A,B>0$, the map
 $(a,\rho)\mapsto\nu[a,\rho]$ is uniformly continuous from $[0,A]\times\mathcal{P}([0,B])$,
 with the metric $|a-a'|+d_{\mathrm{L}}$, to $(\mathcal{P}(\mathbb{R}),d_{\mathrm{L}})$.
\item\label{lem:hess-pastur-d} Let $D,D'\ge0$ be random variables on one probability space, with
 laws $\rho$ and $\rho'$. If $|D-D'|\le\varepsilon$ almost surely, then
 $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\nu[a,\rho],\nu[a,\rho'])\le\varepsilon$. If $\mathbb{P}(D\ne D')\le p$, then
 $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\nu[a,\rho],\nu[a,\rho'])\le p$. Moreover
 $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\nu[a,\rho],\nu[a',\rho])\le2|\sqrt a-\sqrt{a'}|$.
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end lemma-6 -->
<!-- proposition-6: body_md -->
\label{prop:hess-bulk}
Let $\mathcal K$ be a compact subset of $[r_0,1-r_0]\times\mathcal{P}([-1,1])$, with the metric
$|Q-Q'|+W_1(\mu,\mu')$, such that $\mu(\{-1,1\})=0$ for every $(Q,\mu)\in\mathcal K$. For every
$\kappa>0$ there is $w\in(0,r_0/2]$, and for every $M>0$ there is $N_0$, such that for $N\ge N_0$,
outside an event of outer probability at most $e^{-MN}$, the following holds. For all
$(Q,\mu)\in\mathcal K$, $x\in(-1,1)^N$ and $\alpha\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ with
\[
 |q_x-Q|\le w,\qquad W_1(\mu_x,\mu)\le w,\qquad
 \int_{q_x}^1\bigl|\bar{\alpha}(t)-\bar{\zeta_f}(t)\bigr|\,dt\le w,
\]
both one-sided Hessians satisfy
$d_{\mathrm{L}}\bigl(\operatorname{ESD}(\nabla^2_{\pm} F_\alpha(x)),\nu[\xi''(Q),\rho_{Q,\mu}]\bigr)\le\kappa$.
<!-- end proposition-6 -->
<!-- lemma-7: body_md -->
\label{lem:hess-edge}
Assume~\eqref{eq:hess-fhyp}.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:hess-edge-a} The function $z$ is smooth and strictly convex on $(s_-,\infty)$,
 $z'(s)\to-\infty$ as $s\downarrow s_-$, and $z'(s)\to1$ as $s\to\infty$. Hence $z$ has a unique
 critical point $s^*$, and
 \[
  \lambda_+=z(s^*)=\min_{s>s_-}z(s).
 \]
\item\label{lem:hess-edge-b} \textup{(The edge identity.)} $z(-a\chi)=0$, $z'(-a\chi)=\Delta$ and
 $z''(-a\chi)=2a\mathbb{E} U^3$. Hence $\lambda_+\le0$, with equality if and only if $\Delta=0$.
\item\label{lem:hess-edge-c} \textup{(Quadratic vanishing.)} There are $c_0,C>0$ depending only on
 $a$ and $\mathbb{E} U^3$ such that $|\Delta|\le c_0$ implies
 $\bigl|\lambda_++\Delta^2/(4a\mathbb{E} U^3)\bigr|\le C|\Delta|^3$.
\item\label{lem:hess-edge-d} \textup{(Square-root edge.)} Put $C_2=z''(s^*)$,
 $c_2=z''(s^*+1)$ and $t_0=z(s^*+1)-\lambda_+$. There are $0<c\le C$ and $\kappa_0>0$, continuous
 functions of $(a,C_2,c_2,t_0)\in(0,\infty)^4$, such that
 \[
  c\,\kappa^{3/2}\le\nu([\lambda_+-\kappa,\lambda_+])\le C\kappa^{3/2}\qquad(0<\kappa\le\kappa_0).
 \]
\item\label{lem:hess-edge-e} \textup{(Dependence on the radius.)} For every $Q\in(0,1)$, the
 variable $U=U_Q$ with $a=a_Q$ satisfies~\eqref{eq:hess-fhyp}, and then $\nu=\nu_Q$,
 $\lambda_+=\lambda_+(Q)$ and $\Delta=\Delta(Q)$. The critical point $s^*_Q$, the edge $\lambda_+(Q)$ and the
 constants of~\ref{lem:hess-edge-d} depend continuously on $Q\in(0,1)$. For $Q\inC_f$,
 $\Delta(Q)=2\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''(Q)/\xi''(Q)\ge0$; hence $\lambda_+(Q)=0$ if and only if
 $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''(Q)=0$, and
 \[
  \lambda_+(Q)=-\frac{\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''(Q)^2}{\xi''(Q)^3\,\mathbb{E}U_Q^3}+O\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''(Q)^3\bigr),
 \]
 where the implied constant depends only on $\xi''(Q)$ and $\mathbb{E}U_Q^3$.
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end lemma-7 -->
<!-- proof-12: body_md -->
\emph{Shape of $z$.} For $s>s_-$ we have $s+D\ge s-s_->0$, so $z$ is smooth, with
\[
 z'(s)=1-a\mathbb{E}(s+D)^{-2},\qquad z''(s)=2a\mathbb{E}(s+D)^{-3}>0 .
\]
As $s\downarrow s_-$, $(s+D)^{-2}$ increases to $(D-\operatorname*{ess\,inf} D)^{-2}$, so $z'(s)\to-\infty$ by
monotone convergence and~\eqref{eq:hess-fhyp}; as $s\to\infty$, $z'(s)\to1$ by dominated
convergence. Hence $z'$ increases from $-\infty$ to $1$ and vanishes at exactly one point $s^*$,
which minimizes $z$. It remains to show that $\lambda_+=z(s^*)$; we prove the two inequalities
separately.

\emph{Upper bound: $\lambda_+\le z(s)$ for every $s>s_-$.} Let $D_N$ be the diagonal matrix whose
entries are the quantiles $d_i=\inf\{y:\rho((-\infty,y])\ge i/(N+1)\}$, $i\le N$. Then
$d_i\ge\operatorname*{ess\,inf} D$ and $\operatorname{ESD}(D_N)\to\rho$ weakly. Since $-s<\min_id_i$, the Gaussian comparison
inequality of Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-comparison} gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}\lambda_{\max}\bigl(\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N\bigr)\le s+\frac aN\sum_{i\le N}\frac1{d_i+s}
 \xrightarrow[N\to\infty]{}s+a\mathbb{E}(s+D)^{-1}=z(s),
\]
because $y\mapsto(y+s)^{-1}$ is bounded and continuous on $[\operatorname*{ess\,inf} D,\infty)$. The largest
eigenvalue is a $\sqrt{2a/N}$-Lipschitz function of the independent standard Gaussian variables
that define $W_N$, so for every $\eta>0$, $\lambda_{\max}(\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N)\le z(s)+\eta$ with
probability tending to one. By Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-a},
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\operatorname{ESD}(\sqrt a\,W_N-D_N),\nu)\le\eta$ with probability tending to one as well. On both
events, the left inequality of~\eqref{eq:hess-levy} with $t=z(s)+\eta$ gives
$\nu((z(s)+2\eta,\infty))\le\eta$. Letting $\eta\downarrow0$ yields $\nu((z(s),\infty))=0$.

\emph{Lower bound: $\lambda_+\ge z(s^*)$.} Let $g$ be the Cauchy transform of $\nu$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}\ref{lem:hess-pastur-b}, $\lambda_+\le2\sqrt a$. On $(\lambda_+,\infty)$ the
function $g$ is real analytic and positive, with $g'(w)=-\int\nu(d\lambda)(w-\lambda)^{-2}<0$. Put
$s(w)=w-ag(w)$. Then $s'(w)=1-ag'(w)\ge1$ and $s(w)\to\infty$ as $w\to\infty$. Let $w_0$ be the
infimum of the $w>\lambda_+$ such that $s>s_-$ on $(w,\infty)$. The function
$G(\sigma)=\mathbb{E}(\sigma+D)^{-1}$ is analytic off $-\operatorname{supp}\rho\subset(-\infty,s_-]$, so
$F(w)=g(w)-G(w-ag(w))$ is analytic on $\mathbb{C}^+$ and on a complex neighbourhood of $(w_0,\infty)$.
For $w\in\mathbb{C}^+$ we have $\operatorname{Im}(w-ag(w))>0$, and~\eqref{eq:hess-pastur} says that
$F(w)=0$. By the identity theorem $F=0$ on $(w_0,\infty)$, that is, $g(w)=G(s(w))$, and therefore
\[
 z(s(w))=s(w)+aG(s(w))=s(w)+ag(w)=w\qquad(w>w_0).
\]
Differentiating, $z'(s(w))\,s'(w)=1$, so $z'(s(w))>0$ and $s(w)>s^*$ for every $w>w_0$. If
$w_0>\lambda_+$, continuity of $s$ at $w_0$ would give $s(w_0)=s_-<s^*$, contradicting $s(w)>s^*$
for $w\downarrow w_0$. Hence $w_0=\lambda_+$, and every $w>\lambda_+$ satisfies $w=z(s(w))\ge z(s^*)$.
Letting $w\downarrow\lambda_+$ gives $\lambda_+\ge z(s^*)$.

\emph{The edge identity.} Since $-a\chi-s_-=u_{\max}^{-1}\ge1$, the point $-a\chi$ lies in
$(s_-,\infty)$, and $(-a\chi+D)^{-1}=U$. Hence
\[
 z(-a\chi)=-a\chi+a\mathbb{E} U=0,\qquad z'(-a\chi)=1-a\mathbb{E} U^2=\Delta,\qquad z''(-a\chi)=2a\mathbb{E} U^3 .
\]
Thus $\lambda_+=\min z\le z(-a\chi)=0$. If $\Delta=0$, then $-a\chi$ is the critical point $s^*$ and
$\lambda_+=0$. If $\Delta\ne0$, then $s^*\ne-a\chi$, and strict convexity gives
$\lambda_+=z(s^*)<z(-a\chi)=0$.
<!-- end proof-12 -->
<!-- remark-7: body_md -->
\label{rem:hess-sign}
By Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge}\ref{lem:hess-edge-b}, $\lambda_+<0$ for both signs of $\Delta\ne0$. At a
contact the sign is fixed, $\Delta\ge0$, because a contact minimizes the obstacle. By the formulas
for $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}'$ and $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''$ in Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}, the identity
$\Delta=2\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''/\xi''$ holds at every critical point of the obstacle in $(0,1)$, so
$\Delta\le0$ at a local maximum of the obstacle, and the edge is again negative there unless
$\Delta=0$. Since $\lambda_+(Q)\le0$ for every $Q\in(0,1)$, the Hessian bulk never rules out a radius:
near-maximizers at radii away from $C_f$ are excluded by the localization of
Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-i}, not by the spectrum.
<!-- end remark-7 -->
<!-- proposition-7: body_md -->
\label{prop:hess-own}
For every $\kappa>0$ there are $\varepsilon,c>0$ such that, for all large $N$, outside an event of
outer probability at most $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c)}$, every $x\in[-1,1]^N$ and $\alpha\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$
with
\[
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon)\qquad\text{and}\qquad F_\alpha(x)\leF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)+2\varepsilon N
\]
satisfy
\[
 \operatorname{dist}(q_x,C_f)<\kappa,\qquad W_1(\mu_x,L_{q_x})<\kappa,\qquad
 \int_{q_x}^1\bigl|\bar{\alpha}(t)-\bar{\zeta_f}(t)\bigr|\,dt<\kappa .
\]
<!-- end proposition-7 -->
<!-- proof-13: body_md -->
Fix $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_f)$. The set $\mathcal K=\{(Q,L_{Q}):Q\in[r_0,1-r_0]\}$ is compact,
because $Q\mapstoL_{Q}$ is $W_1$-continuous (Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}), and
$L_{Q}(\{-1,1\})=0$ because $M_Q\in(-1,1)$. Let $w\in(0,r_0/2]$ be given by
Proposition~\ref{prop:hess-bulk} for this $\mathcal K$ and accuracy $\kappa/2$, and use that
proposition with the exponent $M'=1-\Sigma(f)>0$ in place of $M$. Put $\kappa_1=\min(\kappa,w,r_0)$, and let $\varepsilon,c>0$ be
given by Proposition~\ref{prop:hess-own} at accuracy $\kappa_1$. For large $N$ the union of the two
exceptional events has outer probability at most
$e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c)}+e^{N(\Sigma(f)-1)}\le e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c')}$, with $c'=\min(c,1)/2$.

Outside this union, let $x\in(-1,1)^N$ with $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon)$. Since $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)$ is an
infimum over order parameters, some $\alpha$ satisfies $F_\alpha(x)\leF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)+2\varepsilon N$, and
Proposition~\ref{prop:hess-own} gives $\operatorname{dist}(q_x,C_f)<\kappa_1$ and
$W_1(\mu_x,L_{q_x})<\kappa_1$. As $\kappa_1\le r_0$ and $C_f\subset[2r_0,1-2r_0]$, we get
$q_x\in(r_0,1-r_0)$, so $(q_x,L_{q_x})\in\mathcal K$. Apply Proposition~\ref{prop:hess-bulk} with
$(Q,\mu)=(q_x,L_{q_x})$. The first two window conditions hold because $\kappa_1\le w$. The third
is void for $\alpha=\zeta_f$, and for $\alpha$ with $F_\alpha(x)\leF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)+2\varepsilon N$ it holds by
Proposition~\ref{prop:hess-own}, again because $\kappa_1\le w$. Since
$\nu[\xi''(q_x),\rho_{q_x,L_{q_x}}]=\nu_{q_x}$, every one-sided Hessian in
$\mathcal H_\varepsilon(x)$ has $\operatorname{ESD}$ within L\'evy distance $\kappa/2$ of $\nu_{q_x}$. By
\eqref{eq:hess-interlace}, the compressions are within $\kappa/2+1/(N-1)\le\kappa$ for large $N$.
Finally $\operatorname{dist}(q_x,C_f)<\kappa_1\le\kappa$.
<!-- end proof-13 -->
<!-- proof-14: body_md -->
Let $Q\in(0,1)$. Then $a_Q>0$, the variable $U_Q$ takes values in $(0,1]$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge}\ref{lem:hess-edge-e} identifies $\nu_Q$, $\lambda_+(Q)$ and $\Delta(Q)$ with
the objects of Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge} for $U=U_Q$ and $a=a_Q$, for which~\eqref{eq:hess-fhyp}
holds. Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-edge}\ref{lem:hess-edge-b} gives $\lambda_+(Q)\le0$, with equality if and
only if $\Delta(Q)=0$. On $C_f$, $\Delta=2\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''/\xi''\ge0$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}), so a contact $Q$ has $\lambda_+(Q)=0$ if and only if
$\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''(Q)=0$.
<!-- end proof-14 -->
<!-- proposition-8: body_md -->
\label{prop:hess-index}
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{prop:hess-index-a} $\kappa'(\kappa)>0$ for every $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_*]$, and there are
 $c_{\mathrm{ix}},C_{\mathrm{ix}},\kappa_{\mathrm{ix}}>0$ such that
 $c_{\mathrm{ix}}\kappa^{3/2}\le\kappa'(\kappa)\le C_{\mathrm{ix}}\kappa^{3/2}$ for
 $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_{\mathrm{ix}}]$.
\item\label{prop:hess-index-b} For every $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_*]$ there are $\varepsilon,c>0$ such
 that, for all large $N$, outside an event of outer probability at most $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c)}$,
 every $x\in(-1,1)^N$ with $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon)$ has $q_x\inC_f^\kappa$, and every
 $H\in\mathcal H_\varepsilon(x)$ satisfies, with $\kappa'=\kappa'(\kappa)$,
 \[
  \lambda_{\lceil\kappa'N\rceil}(H)\in\bigl[\lambda_+(q_x)-\kappa,\lambda_+(q_x)+\kappa\bigr],\qquad
  \#\bigl\{i:\lambda_i(H)>\lambda_+(q_x)+\kappa\bigr\}<\kappa'N .
 \]
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end proposition-8 -->
<!-- remark-8: body_md -->
\label{rem:stab-window}
Assume the hypotheses of Theorem~\ref{thm:stab}\ref{thm:stab-a} and let $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$. There is
$\kappa_{\mathrm w}>0$ with the following property. For every $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_{\mathrm w}]$ and every $\delta>0$,
let $\mathcal B_N(\kappa,\delta)$ be the event that some critical point $x\in(-1,1)^N$ of $F_{\zeta_f}$ with
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\delta)$ has $\lambda_{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}(H)<\lambda_+(q_x)-\kappa$ for each $H$
among $\nabla^2_{\pm} F_{\zeta_f}(x)$ and their compressions to the orthogonal complement of $x$. Then, for
every $c'>0$ and all large $N$, $\mathcal B_N(\kappa,\delta)$ contains an event of probability at
least $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c')}$. Consequently, for no $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_{\mathrm w}]$ are there $\delta,c>0$
such that, for all large $N$, outside an event of outer probability at most $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c)}$,
every $m\in(-1,1)^N$ with $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f-\delta)$ has
$\lambda_{\lfloor\kappa N\rfloor}(H)\ge\lambda_+(q_m)-\kappa$ for some $H$ among $\nabla^2_{\pm} F_{\zeta_f}(m)$ and
their compressions. The witnesses are the retained points of Section~\ref{sec:stab-kr}. The proof
is in Appendix~\ref{app:matrix-index} (Proposition~\ref{prop:matrix-window}).
<!-- end remark-8 -->
<!-- corollary-2: body_md -->
\label{cor:hess-marg}
For every $\kappa\in(0,\kappa_*]$ there are $\kappa',\varepsilon,c>0$ such that, for all large $N$,
outside an event of outer probability at most $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c)}$, every $x\in(-1,1)^N$ with
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon)$ admits $Q\inC_f$ such that every $H\in\mathcal H_\varepsilon(x)$
satisfies
\[
 \lambda_{\lceil\kappa'N\rceil}(H)\in\bigl[\lambda_+(Q)-\kappa,\lambda_+(Q)+\kappa\bigr],\qquad
 \#\bigl\{i:\lambda_i(H)>\lambda_+(Q)+\kappa\bigr\}<\kappa'N .
\]
Here $\lambda_+(Q)=0$ if $\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''(Q)=0$; otherwise $\lambda_+(Q)<0$, and
$\lambda_+(Q)=-\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''(Q)^2/(\xi''(Q)^3\mathbb{E}U_Q^3)+O(\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''(Q)^3)$.
<!-- end corollary-2 -->
<!-- remark-9: body_md -->
\label{rem:hess-plefka}
For $x\in(-1,1)^N$ with $q_x\in(0,1)$ let $\Delta_N(x)=1-\xi''(q_x)N^{-1}\sum_iu(q_x,x_i)^2$ be the
Plefka factor computed from the susceptibilities of $x$ itself. For every $\kappa>0$ there are
$\varepsilon,c>0$ such that, for all large $N$, outside an event of outer probability at most
$e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c)}$, every $x\in(-1,1)^N$ with $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon)$ satisfies
$\Delta_N(x)\ge-\kappa$ and $|\Delta_N(x)-\Delta(Q)|\le\kappa$ for some $Q\inC_f$. Indeed,
$\Delta_N(x)$ and $\Delta(q_x)$ are the integrals of $1-\xi''(q_x)u(q_x,\cdot)^2$ against $\mu_x$ and
$L_{q_x}$, because $u(q_x,\cdot)$ maps $L_{q_x}$ to the law of $U_{q_x}$; $u^2$ is bounded and
uniformly continuous on $[r_0/2,1-r_0/2]\times[-1,1]$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}), and $\Delta$
is uniformly continuous on $C_f^{r_0}$. So the joint form of Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-i}--\ref{thm:struct-ii} (end of Section~\ref{sec:loc-field})
at a small enough accuracy $\kappa_2\le r_0$ gives $Q\inC_f$ with $|q_x-Q|<\kappa_2$ and
$|\Delta_N(x)-\Delta(q_x)|+|\Delta(q_x)-\Delta(Q)|<\kappa$, by coupling $\mu_x$ with $L_{q_x}$; and
$\Delta(Q)\ge0$ gives $\Delta_N(x)\ge-\kappa$. This transfers to every near-maximizer, up to
$\kappa$, the non-strict Plefka inequality that Boursier notes for the first contact
\cite[Remark~1.2]{Bou26b}.
<!-- end remark-9 -->
<!-- proof-15: body_md -->
\emph{Step 0: reduction and the bad events.} Every conclusion of the corollary becomes weaker when
$\kappa$ increases: this is clear for $\operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_f)<\kappa$, $W_1(\mu_m,L_{q_m})<\kappa$ and
$d_{\mathrm{L}}\le\kappa$, and at most $\kappa N$ eigenvalues are larger than $\kappa$ if at most
$\kappa_2N$ eigenvalues are larger than $\kappa_2\le\kappa$. So we may assume $\kappa<\kappa_f$.
The joint form of Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-i}--\ref{thm:struct-ii} (end of
Section~\ref{sec:loc-field}) at accuracy $\kappa$ gives $\delta_1,c_1>0$, and
Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-iii} at accuracy $\kappa$ gives $\varepsilon_2,c_2>0$. Put
$\delta=\min(\delta_1,\varepsilon_2)$ and $c_{\mathrm s}=\min(c_1,c_2)$. Let $B_1$ be the event that some
$m\in[-1,1]^N$ with $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f-\delta)$ has $\operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_f)\ge\kappa$ or
$W_1(\mu_m,L_{q_m})\ge\kappa$. Let $B_2$ be the event that some $m\in(-1,1)^N$ with
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f-\delta)$ fails the following: $\operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_f)<\kappa$, and
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\operatorname{ESD}(H),\nu_{q_m})\le\kappa$ for every $H\in\mathcal H_\delta(m)$. When
$\operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_f)<\kappa<\kappa_f$ we have $q_m\in(0,1)$, so every object in this condition is
defined. Since $\delta\le\delta_1$, the event $B_1$ is contained in the exceptional event of that
joint form. Since
$\delta\le\varepsilon_2$ and $\mathcal H_\delta(m)\subset\mathcal H_{\varepsilon_2}(m)$, the event
$B_2$ is contained in the exceptional event of Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-iii}.
Hence, for $N\ge N_1(\kappa)$,
\[
 \mathbb{P}^{*}(B_1\cup B_2)\le2e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_{\mathrm s})} .
\]
Outside $B_2$, every $H\in\mathcal H_\delta(m)$ also has at most $\kappa N$ eigenvalues larger than
$\kappa$. Indeed, $\nu_{q_m}$ is carried by $(-\infty,\lambda_+(q_m)]\subset(-\infty,0]$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-iv}, so the right inequality of~\eqref{eq:hess-levy} gives
$\operatorname{ESD}(H)((\kappa+s,\infty))\le\nu_{q_m}([s,\infty))+\kappa=\kappa$ for every $s>0$; letting
$s\downarrow0$, $\operatorname{ESD}(H)((\kappa,\infty))\le\kappa$. (For a compression the normalization is $N-1$,
and $\kappa(N-1)\le\kappa N$.)

\emph{Step 1(a): the conditioning event in (a).} The rate $\Sigma$ is concave, as an infimum of
affine functions of $f$, and finite on $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ by
Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-b}; hence it is continuous there. Choose
$\eta\in(0,(f_1-f)/2)$ with $\Sigma(f+2\eta)\ge\Sigma(f)-c_{\mathrm s}/8$, and put
$f'=f+2\eta\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$. By Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-e}, \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ holds, so
Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-d} applies at $f'$. Since
$\mathbb{P}(|N^{-1}M_N-f'|\le\varepsilon)$ is nondecreasing in $\varepsilon$,
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(|N^{-1}M_N-f'|\le\eta\bigr)\ge\Sigma(f')
 \ge\Sigma(f)-c_{\mathrm s}/8 .
\]
On $\{|N^{-1}M_N-f'|\le\eta\}\cap\{|M_N-\logZ_N|\le\eta N/2\}$ we have
$N^{-1}\logZ_N\ge f'-3\eta/2=f+\eta/2\ge f$. Theorem~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-a} at $t=\eta/2$
allows every exponential rate, in particular the rate $c_{\mathrm s}-\Sigma(f)>0$:
$\mathbb{P}(|M_N-\logZ_N|>\eta N/2)\le e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_{\mathrm s})}$ for large $N$. Hence, for
$N\ge N_2(\kappa)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:hess-cond}
 \mathbb{P}\bigl(N^{-1}\logZ_N\ge f\bigr)\ge e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_{\mathrm s}/4)}-e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_{\mathrm s})}
 \ge e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_{\mathrm s}/2)} .
\end{equation}
In particular this probability is positive.

\emph{Step 1(b): the conditioning event in (b).} By Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-d} at
$f$ and the same monotonicity,
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(M_N\ge N(f-\delta)\bigr)
 \ge\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\delta\bigr)\ge\Sigma(f),
\]
so $\mathbb{P}(M_N\ge N(f-\delta))\ge e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_{\mathrm s}/2)}$ for $N\ge N_2'(\kappa)$.

\emph{Step 2: conditional bounds.} Put $c=c_{\mathrm s}/4$ and $A=\{N^{-1}\logZ_N\ge f\}$. By Step 0
and~\eqref{eq:hess-cond},
\[
 \mathbb{P}^{*}(B_1\cup B_2\mid A)\le\frac{2e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_{\mathrm s})}}{e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_{\mathrm s}/2)}}=2e^{-c_{\mathrm s}N/2}.
\]
Given $t>0$, Theorem~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-a} gives
$\mathbb{P}(|M_N-\logZ_N|>tN)\le e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_{\mathrm s})}$ for $N\ge N_3(t,\kappa)$, so its conditional
probability given $A$ is at most $e^{-c_{\mathrm s}N/2}$. The conclusions of
Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-a} fail only on a null set. Hence, for
$N\ge N_0(t,\kappa)=\max(N_1,N_2,N_3,\lceil4\log3/c_{\mathrm s}\rceil)$, the conditional outer probability
that one of items~\ref{cor:title-1}--\ref{cor:title-3} fails is at most
$3e^{-c_{\mathrm s}N/2}\le e^{-cN}$. Indeed, outside the three exceptional sets, item~\ref{cor:title-1}
holds by Theorems~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-a} and~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-a},
item~\ref{cor:title-2} holds off $B_1$, and item~\ref{cor:title-3} holds off $B_2$, with the
eigenvalue count of Step~0.

For the last assertion of (a), let $t\le\delta$. On the good event, every maximizer $x^*$ lies in
$(-1,1)^N$ and satisfies $F_{\zeta^*}(x^*)=F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x^*)=M_N\ge\logZ_N-tN\ge N(f-\delta)$. So
items~\ref{cor:title-2} and~\ref{cor:title-3} apply to $x^*$, and $\alpha=\zeta^*$ is admissible in
item~\ref{cor:title-3} because $F_{\zeta^*}(x^*)=F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x^*)$.

For (b), Step~1(b) bounds the probability of the conditioning event from below by
$e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_{\mathrm s}/2)}$. So the conditional outer probability of $B_1\cup B_2$ is at most
\[
 2e^{-c_{\mathrm s}N/2}\le e^{-cN}\qquad\text{for } N\ge\max\bigl(N_1,N_2',\lceil4\log2/c_{\mathrm s}\rceil\bigr),
\]
and outside $B_1\cup B_2$ items~\ref{cor:title-2} and~\ref{cor:title-3} hold.
<!-- end proof-15 -->
<!-- proof-16: body_md -->
Fix $g>0$, and recall that $\kappa_f=\operatorname{dist}(C_f,\{0,1\})>0$.

\emph{Step 1: mass near the edge.} By \hyperref[hyp:Hmarg]{\textup{(H-marg)}}\ and
Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-iv}, $\lambda_+(Q)=\sup\operatorname{supp}\nu_Q=0$ for every $Q\inC_f$. The
open set $(-g/4,\infty)$ contains a point of $\operatorname{supp}\nu_Q$, so $\nu_Q((-g/4,\infty))>0$ for $Q\inC_f$.
The map $Q\mapsto\nu_Q$ is weakly continuous on $(0,1)$, by the continuity of reflected Pastur laws
in their data (Lemma~\ref{lem:hess-pastur}) and the continuity of $Q\mapsto\operatorname{Law}(U_Q)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}). By the portmanteau theorem, $Q\mapsto\nu_Q((-g/4,\infty))$ is lower
semicontinuous on $(0,1)$. The contact set $C_f$ is a compact subset of $(0,1)$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}), and a lower semicontinuous function attains its minimum on a
compact set, so
\[
 p:=\min_{Q\inC_f}\nu_Q\bigl((-g/4,\infty)\bigr)>0 .
\]
The set $\{Q\in(0,1):\nu_Q((-g/4,\infty))>p/2\}$ is open and contains $C_f$, so it contains
$\{Q:\operatorname{dist}(Q,C_f)<\kappa_0\}$ for some $\kappa_0\in(0,\kappa_f)$.

\emph{Step 2: transfer to the Hessians.} Put $\kappa:=\min\{\kappa_0,g/4,p/4\}\in(0,\kappa_f)$.
Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-iii} with this $\kappa$ gives $\varepsilon,c>0$ and, for all
large $N$, an event $B_N$ with $\mathbb{P}^{*}(B_N)\le e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c)}$ outside of which every
$x\in(-1,1)^N$ with $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon)$ satisfies $\operatorname{dist}(q_x,C_f)<\kappa$ and
$d_{\mathrm{L}}(\operatorname{ESD}(H),\nu_{q_x})\le\kappa$ for each of the matrices $H=\nabla^2_{\pm} F_{\zeta_f}(x)$ and
$H=\nabla^2_{\pm} F_\alpha(x)$, $\alpha\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ with $F_\alpha(x)\leF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)+2\varepsilon N$.

\emph{Step 3: no margin.} Outside $B_N$, let $x$ and $H$ be as in Step~2. If $d_{\mathrm{L}}(\mu,\mu')\le\kappa$,
then $\mu((t,\infty))\ge\mu'((t+\kappa,\infty))-\kappa$ for every $t\in\mathbb{R}$. We apply this with
$t=-g/2$. Since $\kappa\le g/4$, $\operatorname{dist}(q_x,C_f)<\kappa_0$ and $\kappa\le p/4$,
\[
 \operatorname{ESD}(H)\bigl((-g/2,\infty)\bigr)\ge\nu_{q_x}\bigl((-g/4,\infty)\bigr)-\kappa
 \ge\frac p2-\frac p4=\frac p4 .
\]
So at least $pN/4$ eigenvalues of $H$ exceed $-g/2$, and $\lambda_{\max}(H)>-g$. This holds for
both one-sided Hessians, so $\min_\pm\lambda_{\max}(\nabla^2_{\pm} F_\alpha(x))>-g$, both for $\alpha=\zeta_f$ and
for every $\alpha$ with $F_\alpha(x)\leF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)+2\varepsilon N$. The two events of
part~\ref{thm:stab-b} are therefore contained in $B_N$, which proves the bound on their outer
probability.

For the last assertion, let $\varepsilon'\in(0,\varepsilon]$ and let $(\zeta,x)$ witness
$\mathcal{E}^{g}_{N,\varepsilon'}(f)$, with $\nabla^2_\sigma F_\zeta(x)\preceq-gI$. Then $x$ lies in $(-1,1)^N$,
\begin{gather*}
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon'),\qquad
 F_\zeta(x)\le N(f+\varepsilon')\leF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)+2\varepsilon' N,\\
 \min_\pm\lambda_{\max}\bigl(\nabla^2_{\pm} F_\zeta(x)\bigr)\le\lambda_{\max}\bigl(\nabla^2_\sigma F_\zeta(x)\bigr)\le-g .
\end{gather*}
Hence $\mathcal{E}^{g}_{N,\varepsilon'}(f)\subset B_N$, and
$\mathbb{P}^{*}(\mathcal{E}^{g}_{N,\varepsilon'}(f))\le e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c)}$ for all large $N$.
<!-- end proof-16 -->
<!-- proof-17: body_md -->
Fix $\varepsilon>0$. Choose an admissible $\eta$ with $\varepsilon_1(\eta)\le\varepsilon/3$ and
$\varepsilon_3(\eta)\le\varepsilon/4$; if $\Delta(q_f)>0$ this is $\eta=0$. Put $g=g_\eta$ and
$\rho=\rho_\eta$. Choose $\delta\in(0,q/2)$ with $\frac12\log(1-\delta/q)\ge-\varepsilon/4$. By
\ref{step:stab-k3} there is $w_2>0$ such that
$\liminf_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(\widehat C_N(\eta,\delta,w)\ge1)\ge\Sigma(f)-\varepsilon$ for every
$w\in(0,w_2]$; fix such a $w$ with $\varepsilon_2(w)\le\varepsilon/3$. For $N^{-2}\le\varepsilon/6$,
\ref{step:stab-k1} and \ref{step:stab-k2} show that every retained point $x$ satisfies
\eqref{eq:event-exist} with $\zeta=\zeta_f$, and \eqref{eq:event-fix}. Hence
$\{\widehat C_N\ge1\}\subset\mathcal{E}^{g,\rho}_{N,\varepsilon,\mathrm{fix}}(f)$ for all large $N$, which gives the first
display of part~\ref{thm:stab-a}.

If $\Delta(q_f)>0$, then $\eta=0$ for every $\varepsilon$, and $(g,\rho)=(g_0,\rho_0)$ does not
depend on $\varepsilon$. The lower bound $\Sigma(f)-\varepsilon$ then holds at this fixed margin for
every $\varepsilon>0$. Since $\mathcal{E}^{g,\rho}_{N,\varepsilon,\mathrm{fix}}(f)\subset\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)$,
Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-d}--\ref{thm:exist-e} gives the matching upper bound
$\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\limsup_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}^{*}(\mathcal{E}^{g,\rho}_{N,\varepsilon,\mathrm{fix}}(f))\le\Sigma(f)$.
The lower bound comes from the measurable subevent $\{\widehat C_N\ge1\}$, so the equality holds
for the inner and for the outer probability.
<!-- end proof-17 -->
<!-- remark-10: body_md -->
\label{rem:stab-margin}
Assume $\Delta(q_f)=0$. For every admissible $\eta>0$, every margin $g_\eta$ as in
\ref{step:stab-k1} satisfies $g_\eta\le-\lambda_+^{(\eta)}$, and, as $\eta\downarrow0$,
\[
 -\lambda_+^{(\eta)}=\frac{\Delta_\eta^2}{4a\mathbb{E}_{\pi_\eta}U^3}+O(\eta^3)
 =\frac{a(\mathbb{E}_{\pi_0}\mathcal R^2)^2}{4\mathbb{E}_{\pi_0}U^3}\,\eta^2+O(\eta^3).
\]
So the margins of the construction are $O(\eta^2)$. In the $2+4$ family of
Theorem~\ref{thm:stab}\ref{thm:stab-c} some such vanishing is unavoidable, by
item~\ref{thm:stab-c2} there. The remark is proved in Appendix~\ref{app:kr-susy}.
<!-- end remark-10 -->
<!-- definition-1: body_md -->
\label{def:stab-susy}
Let $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$, and let $M$, $\pi_0$ and $\pi_x$ be as above. For $\varepsilon>0$, an
\emph{$\varepsilon$-SUSY state at level $f$} is a critical point $x\in(-1,1)^N$ of $F_{\zeta_f}$ such that
\[
 |q_x-q_f|\le\varepsilon,\qquad
 \bigl|N^{-1}F_{\zeta_f}(x)-f\bigr|\le\varepsilon,\qquad
 \bigl|N^{-1}F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)-f\bigr|\le\varepsilon,\qquad
 W_2(\pi_x,\pi_0)\le\varepsilon .
\]
Let $\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}$ be the number of $\varepsilon$-SUSY states.
<!-- end definition-1 -->
<!-- proposition-9: body_md -->
\label{prop:stab-susy}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}, $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$ and that $\xi$ has at least two active degrees, and let
$f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$.
\begin{romanlist}
\item\label{prop:stab-susy-i} For every $\varepsilon>0$,
 $\liminf_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}\ge\Sigma(f)$, and
 \[
  \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{E}\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}\le\Sigma(f).
 \]
 Consequently both $\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\liminf_N$ and
 $\lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\limsup_N$ of $N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}$ equal
 \[
  \Sigma(f)=\theta_f(P_{\zeta_f}-f).
 \]
\item\label{prop:stab-susy-ii} For every $\varepsilon>0$,
 $\liminf_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}\ge1)\ge\Sigma(f)$, and
 \[
  \lim_{\varepsilon\downarrow0}\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
  \log\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}\bigm|\mathsf N_{N,\varepsilon}\ge1\bigr]=0 .
 \]
\end{romanlist}
No strict Plefka condition is imposed: $\Delta(q_f)=0$ is allowed.
<!-- end proposition-9 -->
<!-- lemma-8: body_md -->
\label{lem:stab-family}
Let $\xi$ and $\theta_0$ be as above, let $\theta\in(0,\theta_0)$ and $\zeta=\zeta_\theta$, and put
$h(t)=\Gamma_{\zeta}(t)-t$. Then
\[
 h>0\ \text{ on }(0,q_\theta),\qquad h=0\ \text{ on }[q_\theta,v_\theta],\qquad
 h<0\ \text{ on }(v_\theta,1].
\]
Consequently $\mathcal{O}_\zeta$ is strictly decreasing on $[0,q_\theta]$, constant on
$[q_\theta,v_\theta]$ and strictly increasing on $[v_\theta,1]$, so that
$\operatorname*{arg\,min}_{(0,1]}\mathcal{O}_\zeta=[q_\theta,v_\theta]=\operatorname{supp}\zeta\cap(0,1]$, and
$\mathcal{O}_\zeta''=\frac12\xi''(1-\Gamma_{\zeta}')=0$ on $[q_\theta,v_\theta]$.
<!-- end lemma-8 -->
<!-- proof-18: body_md -->
Let $\xi$ be in the family and $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_0)$. The covariance is a polynomial with
$\xi''(t)=2b+12et^2>0$, so $\xi$ satisfies \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}, $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$, and $\xi$ has two active
degrees. Since $\theta_f\in(0,\theta_0)$, Lemma~\ref{lem:stab-family} applies to $\zeta_f=\zeta_{\theta_f}$.

\emph{Item~\ref{thm:stab-c1}.} By Lemma~\ref{lem:stab-family},
$C_f=\operatorname{supp}\zeta_f\cap(0,1]=[q_{\theta_f},v_{\theta_f}]$, an interval of positive length, and
$\mathcal{O}_{\zeta_f}''=0$ on $C_f$, which is \hyperref[hyp:Hmarg]{\textup{(H-marg)}}.

\emph{Item~\ref{thm:stab-c2}.} Suppose that $g(\varepsilon_n)\ge g_0>0$ along a sequence
$\varepsilon_n\downarrow0$. Part~\ref{thm:stab-b} at the margin $g_0$, which applies by
item~\ref{thm:stab-c1}, gives $\varepsilon(g_0),c(g_0)>0$ such that
$\limsup_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(\mathcal{E}^{g_0}_{N,\varepsilon'}(f))\le\Sigma(f)-c(g_0)$ for every
$\varepsilon'\in(0,\varepsilon(g_0)]$. A point in $\mathcal{E}^{g,\rho}_{N,\varepsilon,\mathrm{fix}}(f)$ witnesses
$\mathcal{E}^{g}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)$ with $\zeta=\zeta_f$, and $\mathcal{E}^{g}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)\subset
\mathcal{E}^{g_0}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)$ for $g\ge g_0$. For $n$ with
$\varepsilon_n<\min\{\varepsilon(g_0),c(g_0)\}$, part~\ref{thm:stab-a} therefore gives
\[
 \Sigma(f)-\varepsilon_n\le\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N
 \log\mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathcal{E}^{g(\varepsilon_n),\rho(\varepsilon_n)}_{N,\varepsilon_n,\mathrm{fix}}(f)\bigr)
 \le\limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(\mathcal{E}^{g_0}_{N,\varepsilon_n}(f)\bigr)
 \le\Sigma(f)-c(g_0),
\]
a contradiction. Hence $g(\varepsilon)\to0$.

\emph{Item~\ref{thm:stab-c3}.} By item~\ref{thm:stab-c1} and
Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-iv}, $\lambda_+(Q)=0$ for every $Q\inC_f$. Let $\kappa>0$ be
small enough for Corollary~\ref{cor:hess-marg}. It gives $\kappa',\varepsilon_4,c_4>0$ such that, for
all large $N$, outside an event of outer probability at most $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_4)}$, every
$x\in(-1,1)^N$ with $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon_4)$ admits $Q\inC_f$ for which each of the matrices
$\nabla^2_{\pm} F_{\zeta_f}(x)$, $\nabla^2_{\pm} F_\alpha(x)$ with $F_\alpha(x)\leF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)+2\varepsilon_4N$, and their
compressions to the orthogonal complement of $x$, has its $\lceil\kappa'N\rceil$-th largest
eigenvalue in $[\lambda_+(Q)-\kappa,\lambda_+(Q)+\kappa]=[-\kappa,\kappa]$ and fewer than $\kappa'N$
eigenvalues larger than $\lambda_+(Q)+\kappa=\kappa$. Theorem~\ref{thm:struct}\ref{thm:struct-i}--\ref{thm:struct-ii}
with this $\kappa$ give $\delta_2,c_2>0$ such that, outside an event of outer probability at most
$2e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_2)}$, every $m\in[-1,1]^N$ with $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f-\delta_2)$ satisfies
$\operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_f)<\kappa$ and $W_1(\mu_m,L_{q_m})<\kappa$. Put
$\varepsilon=\min\{\varepsilon_4,\delta_2\}$ and $c_3=\min\{c_4,c_2\}$, and let $B_N$ be the union of
the two exceptional events, so that $\mathbb{P}^{*}(B_N)\le3e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_3)}$.

Let $(\alpha,x)$ satisfy \eqref{eq:event-exist}. Then $x\in(-1,1)^N$, $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-\varepsilon)$ and
$F_\alpha(x)\le N(f+\varepsilon)\leF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)+2\varepsilon N$, so outside $B_N$ the pair $(\alpha,x)$
has all the properties listed in item~\ref{thm:stab-c3}. It remains to condition. By
Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-d}--\ref{thm:exist-e} and the monotonicity of
$\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)$ in $\varepsilon$ (for the inner probability, Section~\ref{sec:max-existence}),
$\liminf_NN^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}_{*}(\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f))\ge\Sigma(f)$. Hence
$\mathbb{P}_{*}(\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f))\ge e^{N(\Sigma(f)-c_3/4)}$ for all large $N$, and
\[
 \mathbb{P}^{*}\bigl(B_N\bigm|\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f)\bigr)
 \le\frac{\mathbb{P}^{*}(B_N)}{\mathbb{P}_{*}(\mathcal{E}_{N,\varepsilon}(f))}\le3e^{-3c_3N/4}\le e^{-c_3N/2}
\]
for all large $N$. This proves item~\ref{thm:stab-c3} with $c=c_3/2$.
<!-- end proof-18 -->
<!-- lemma-9: body_md -->
\label{lem:eq-obstacle}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ and let $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$ be a Parisi measure.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:eq-obstacle-a} $\int\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\,d\mu\ge\int\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\,d\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$ for every
 $\mu\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$. Consequently $\int\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\,d\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}=\min_{[0,1]}\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}$, and
 $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}\subsetC_{\mathrm{P}}$.
\item\label{lem:eq-obstacle-b} $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}'(1)=\frac12\xi''(1)\bigl(1-\mathbb{E}\tanh^2X_1\bigr)>0$.
 Consequently $\min_{[0,1]}\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}<0=\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(1)$, and $C_{\mathrm{P}}$ is a nonempty compact subset of $[0,1)$.
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end lemma-9 -->
<!-- proof-19: body_md -->
\ref{lem:eq-obstacle-a} Let $\mu\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ and $\lambda\in(0,1]$. The measure
$(1-\lambda)\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}+\lambda\mu$ is admissible, and its distribution function is
$\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}+\lambda h$ with $h=\bar{\mu}-\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}$, which has $\|h\|_{L^1}\le1$. Minimality of
$\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$ and \eqref{eq:eq-second} give
$0\le P_{(1-\lambda)\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}+\lambda\mu}-f_{\mathrm{eq}}\le\lambda\,DP(\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}})[h]+K\lambda^2$. Dividing by
$\lambda$ and letting $\lambda\downarrow0$, then applying \eqref{eq:eq-firstvar} and
\eqref{eq:eq-fubini} to $\mu$ and to $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$,
\[
 0\le DP(\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}})[\bar{\mu}-\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}]=\int\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\,d\mu-\int\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\,d\zeta_{\mathrm{P}} .
\]
With $\mu=\delta_t$ this reads $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(t)\ge\int\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\,d\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$ for every $t\in[0,1]$, so
$\int\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\,d\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}=\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}$. Hence $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}=\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}$ holds $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$-almost everywhere; the set where it
holds is closed, so it contains $\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$.

\ref{lem:eq-obstacle-b} Since $\Phi_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(1,x)=\log\cosh x$, we have $u(1,x)=\tanh x$,
so $\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(1)=\mathbb{E}\tanh^2X_1<1$ and
$\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}'(1)=-\frac12\xi''(1)(\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(1)-1)>0$, since $\xi''(1)>0$. As $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(1)=0$, the
obstacle is negative just below $1$, so $\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}<0$ and $1\notinC_{\mathrm{P}}$. The set $C_{\mathrm{P}}$ is closed
in $[0,1]$ by continuity of $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}$, and nonempty.
<!-- end proof-19 -->
<!-- lemma-10: body_md -->
\label{lem:eq-zero}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}. For every Parisi measure $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$, $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(0)=\min_{[0,1]}\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}$; that is,
$0\inC_{\mathrm{P}}$.
<!-- end lemma-10 -->
<!-- proof-20: body_md -->
Let $\underline q=\min\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$. If $\underline q=0$, then $0\inC_{\mathrm{P}}$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-obstacle}\ref{lem:eq-obstacle-a}. Suppose $\underline q>0$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-obstacle}, $\underline q\inC_{\mathrm{P}}$ and $\underline q<1$, so $\underline q$ is an
interior minimum point of the $C^1$ function $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}$. Hence $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}'(\underline q)=0$, and since
$\xi''(\underline q)>0$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-gap-end}
 \Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(\underline q)=\underline q .
\end{equation}

\emph{The gap.} We have $\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}=0$ on $[0,\underline q)$. Approximate $\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}$ in $L^1$ by
step distribution functions that also vanish on $[0,\underline q)$ (for instance, those of the
measures obtained by rounding $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$ up to a finite grid). On $[0,\underline q)$ each
approximating Parisi equation has coefficient $0$, so its solution is a Gaussian convolution of
its value at time $\underline q$, and so is its space derivative. Passing to the uniform limit
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}) gives, with $\varphi:=u(\underline q,\cdot)$,
\[
 u(t,x)=\mathbb{E}\,\varphi(x+\sigma_tZ),\qquad
 \sigma_t^2=\xi'(\underline q)-\xi'(t)>0,\qquad 0\le t<\underline q,
\]
where $Z$ is a standard Gaussian variable. By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}, $\varphi$ is odd,
nondecreasing and $1$-Lipschitz. The drift of $X$ vanishes on $[0,\underline q)$, so
$X_t=\int_0^t\sqrt{\xi''(r)}\,dB_r$ there: a Gaussian martingale whose increment
$X_{\underline q}-X_t\sim N(0,\sigma_t^2)$ is independent of $\mathcal F_t$, and
$X_{\underline q}$ has a density because $\xi'(\underline q)>0$. Hence, for $t<\underline q$,
\[
 Y_t:=u(t,X_t)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\varphi(X_{\underline q})\bigm|\mathcal F_t\bigr],
 \qquad
 Y'_t:=\partial_xu(t,X_t)=\mathbb{E}\bigl[\varphi'(X_{\underline q})\bigm|\mathcal F_t\bigr],
\]
where we differentiated under the Gaussian integral ($\varphi$ is Lipschitz, so $\varphi'$ exists
almost everywhere and is bounded by $1$). Both are bounded martingales, so
$t\mapsto\mathbb{E}(Y'_t)^2$ is nondecreasing on $[0,\underline q)$.

\emph{Convexity of $\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}$ on the gap.} On $[0,\underline q)\times\mathbb{R}$ the function $u$ is
smooth and solves $\partial_tu+\frac12\xi''\partial_{xx}u=0$, so It\^o's formula gives
$dY_t=\sqrt{\xi''(t)}\,Y'_t\,dB_t$. Since $Y_0=u(0,0)=0$ by oddness, the It\^o isometry yields
\[
 \Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(t)=\mathbb{E} Y_t^2=\int_0^t\xi''(r)\,\mathbb{E}(Y'_r)^2\,dr,\qquad 0\le t<\underline q .
\]
The integrand is the product of two nonnegative nondecreasing functions, because
$\xi'''\ge0$ on $[0,1]$ (the coefficients of $\xi$ are nonnegative). So $\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}$ is
convex on $[0,\underline q)$, and on $[0,\underline q]$ by continuity, with
$\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(0)=0$ and $\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(\underline q)=\underline q$ by \eqref{eq:eq-gap-end}.
Therefore $\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(t)\le t$ on $[0,\underline q]$, that is,
$\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}'(t)=-\frac12\xi''(t)(\Gamma_{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}(t)-t)\ge0$ there, and
$\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(0)\le\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(\underline q)=\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}$.
<!-- end proof-20 -->
<!-- lemma-11: body_md -->
\label{lem:eq-gap}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}. Let $Q\in(0,1)\setminusC_{\mathrm{P}}$ and $\varepsilon\in(0,1]$, and take the glued data
\[
 \mathsf{x}=\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}+\varepsilon\ \text{ on }[0,Q),\qquad \eta=\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}\in\mathcal{P}([Q,1]).
\]
Then $\mathsf{x}$ is nondecreasing with values in $[\varepsilon,2]$, and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-gap}
 P\bigl(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)\bigr)\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}-\varepsilon\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(Q)-\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\bigr)+K\varepsilon^2 .
\end{equation}
<!-- end lemma-11 -->
<!-- proof-21: body_md -->
The measure $\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}=\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}|_{(Q,1]}+\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}([0,Q])\delta_Q$ has distribution function
$\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}$ on $[Q,1]$, so $\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)=\bar{\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}}+\varepsilon h$ with
$h=\mathbf{1}_{[0,Q)}$. Here $\|h\|_{L^1}=Q\le1$ and the glued coefficient takes values in
$[0,2]$. By \eqref{eq:eq-second}, \eqref{eq:eq-firstvar} and Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-zero},
\[
 P\bigl(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)\bigr)\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}+\varepsilon\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(0)-\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(Q)\bigr)+K\varepsilon^2
 =f_{\mathrm{eq}}-\varepsilon\bigl(\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(Q)-\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\bigr)+K\varepsilon^2 .
\]
The claims about $\mathsf{x}$ are clear.
<!-- end proof-21 -->
<!-- proof-22: body_md -->
The containment $\{0\}\cup\operatorname{supp}\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}\subsetC_{\mathrm{P}}$ was proved in Section~\ref{sec:eq-obstacle}. The
probability bound has a localization part and a field-law part. We prove them in Steps~1 and~2
by the shell argument of Section~\ref{sec:loc-proof} and Appendix~\ref{app:var-field}, with
Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-gap} as the source of the gain. Step~3 combines them, and Step~4 deduces the
fixed-radius statement. Convexity of $\xi$ on $[-1,1]$ enters only through the Slepian step of
Proposition~\ref{prop:glued-comparison}; the toolbox of Appendix~\ref{app:pde-toolbox} and
the proofs of Lemmas~\ref{lem:eq-obstacle} and~\ref{lem:eq-zero} use only \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}.

\emph{Shells and the comparison.} For $\rho\in(0,1]$ let $Q_j=j\rho$ and
$I_j=[Q_j,\min(Q_j+\rho,1)]$ for the integers $j\ge0$ with $Q_j<1$. There are at most
$\lceil1/\rho\rceil+1$ such shells, and they cover $[0,1]$. We use \eqref{eq:loc-glued-general}
with $s=0$ (Proposition~\ref{prop:glued-comparison} with the approximation of
Corollary~\ref{cor:pde-majorant}): if $\theta\in(0,1)$, $Q\in[0,1)$, $\rho'\in(0,1-Q]$,
$\mathsf{x}:[0,Q)\to[\theta,2]$ is nondecreasing (there is no cascade part if $Q=0$) and
$\eta\in\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$, then for every $\varepsilon_A>0$ there is a random
variable $\mathcal T$ such that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-majorant}
\begin{aligned}
 \sup\bigl\{F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m):\ m\in[-1,1]^N,\ q_m\in[Q,Q+\rho']\bigr\}
 &\le N P\bigl(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)\bigr)+N\varepsilon_A+\mathcal T,\\
 \mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T}&\le(N+1)\,e^{N\theta C_R\rho'},
\end{aligned}
\end{equation}
with $C_R=5\xi''(1)$. The events below that involve all $m$ in the cube are contained in finite
unions of events $\{\mathcal T\ge a\}$, which is how their outer probabilities are bounded.

\emph{Step 1: localization.} Fix $\kappa>0$ and let
$A_\kappa=\{Q\in[0,1]:\operatorname{dist}(Q,C_{\mathrm{P}})\ge\kappa/2\}$. If $A_\kappa$ is empty, no $m$ has $\operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_{\mathrm{P}})\ge\kappa$, so the event of
\eqref{eq:eq-step1} is empty and there is nothing to prove; set $c_1:=c_2$ in Step~3. Otherwise $A_\kappa$ is compact and disjoint from $C_{\mathrm{P}}$, and
$\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}$ is continuous, so
\[
 \gamma:=\min\bigl\{\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(Q)-\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}:\ Q\in A_\kappa\bigr\}>0 .
\]
Put $\varepsilon=\min\{1,\gamma/(2K)\}$ and $\theta=\varepsilon/2$, choose $\rho\in(0,\kappa/2)$
with $C_R\rho\le\varepsilon\gamma/16$, and put $\varepsilon_A=\varepsilon\gamma/16$ and
$t=\varepsilon\gamma/8$.

If $\operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_{\mathrm{P}})\ge\kappa$, then $q_m\in I_j$ for some $j$ with
$\operatorname{dist}(Q_j,C_{\mathrm{P}})\ge\kappa-\rho>\kappa/2$. Such an anchor lies in $A_\kappa$; it satisfies
$Q_j>\kappa/2>0$ because $0\inC_{\mathrm{P}}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-zero}), and $Q_j<1$. So
Lemma~\ref{lem:eq-gap} applies at $Q=Q_j$, and since $\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}(Q_j)-\min\mathcal{O}_{\mathrm{P}}\ge\gamma$ and
$K\varepsilon\le\gamma/2$, its data satisfy
\[
 P\bigl(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta)\bigr)\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}-\varepsilon\gamma+K\varepsilon^2\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}-\varepsilon\gamma/2 .
\]
The cascade coefficient takes values in $[\varepsilon,2]\subset[\theta,2]$, so
\eqref{eq:eq-majorant} applies on $I_j$ and gives a random variable $\mathcal T_j$ with
$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T_j}\le(N+1)e^{N\theta C_R\rho}$ and
\[
 \bigl\{\exists m:\ q_m\in I_j,\ F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-t)\bigr\}
 \subset\bigl\{\mathcal T_j\ge N(\varepsilon\gamma/2-\varepsilon_A-t)\bigr\}
 =\bigl\{\mathcal T_j\ge\tfrac5{16}N\varepsilon\gamma\bigr\}.
\]
By Markov's inequality applied to $e^{\theta\mathcal T_j}$, this event has probability at most
\[
 (N+1)\exp\Bigl\{N\theta\Bigl(C_R\rho-\frac5{16}\varepsilon\gamma\Bigr)\Bigr\}
 \le(N+1)\,e^{-N\theta\varepsilon\gamma/4}.
\]
A union bound over the at most $\lceil1/\rho\rceil+1$ shells gives, for all large $N$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-step1}
 \mathbb{P}^{*}\bigl(\exists m\in[-1,1]^N:\ F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}-t),\ \operatorname{dist}(q_m,C_{\mathrm{P}})\ge\kappa\bigr)
 \le e^{-c_1N},
\end{equation}
where $c_1:=\theta\varepsilon\gamma/8=\varepsilon^2\gamma/16\le t$.

\emph{Step 2: field law.} Fix $\kappa>0$. Let $\tilde g_1,\dots,\tilde g_J$ be the smooth test
functions of Lemma~\ref{lem:var-net} for the accuracy $\kappa$: they satisfy
$\|\tilde g_j'\|_\infty\le1$, $\|\tilde g_j''\|_\infty<\infty$, and for probability measures
$\mu,\mu'$ on $[-1,1]$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-net}
 W_1(\mu,\mu')\ge\kappa\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \int\tilde g_j\,d(\mu-\mu')\ge\kappa/2\ \text{ for some } j .
\end{equation}
The map $q\mapsto\int\tilde g_j\,dL^{\mathrm{P}}_{q}$ is uniformly continuous on $[0,1]$, because
$q\mapsto u(q,X_q)$ is almost surely continuous and bounded by $1$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}); let $\omega_{\mathrm P}$ be a common modulus of continuity for
$j=1,\dots,J$.

We need the perturbed comparison at a base point other than a minimizer. Let
$\zeta'\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ and $\theta\in(0,1)$ with $\zeta'(\{0\})\ge\theta$,
let $L'_Q=\operatorname{Law}(\partial_x\Phi_{\zeta'}(Q,X'_Q))$ be the field law of $\zeta'$ ($X'$ its
Auffinger--Chen process), and let $Q\in[0,1)$, $\rho'\in(0,1-Q]$,
$0<s\le(2\max_j\|\tilde g_j''\|_\infty)^{-1}$ and $\varepsilon_A>0$. Then for each $j$ there is a
random variable $\mathcal T$ with $\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T}\le(N+1)e^{N\theta C_R\rho'}$ and
\begin{equation}\label{eq:eq-perturbed}
 \sup\Bigl\{F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)+s\sum_{i=1}^N\tilde g_j(m_i):\ q_m\in[Q,Q+\rho']\Bigr\}
 \le N\bigl[P_{\zeta'}+s\int\tilde g_j\,dL'_Q+C_2s^2+\varepsilon_A\bigr]+\mathcal T,
\end{equation}
where $C_2=1+L_\psi$, with $L_\psi$ as in~\eqref{eq:pde-constants}, depends only on $\xi'(1)$
and $\xi''(1)$. This is
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-tangent}\ref{lem:var-tangent-b} with $g=\tilde g_j$: the comparison of
Proposition~\ref{prop:glued-comparison} at the base point $(\bar{\zeta'}|_{[0,Q)},\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta')$,
with the terminal condition perturbed by $s\tilde g_j$. Its proof uses only
$\zeta'(\{0\})\ge\theta$, which makes this base point admissible, and not any minimality of
