$\alpha$, almost surely. Therefore
\[
 \bigl(u_{\pi(\alpha)}+Y(q,\pi(\alpha))-A(q)\bigr)_\alpha
 =\operatorname{Leaf}\bigl(\operatorname{Sort}(\lambda)\bigr)
 \overset{d}{=}\operatorname{Leaf}(u)=(u_\alpha)_\alpha .
\]
The supremum of a family indexed by $\mathbb{N}^L$ is a Borel function of the family, and the set of
families whose supremum is attained is Borel; neither changes when the index set is permuted by
$\pi$. This gives the last assertion of (a).

\emph{Step 4: proof of (b).} Let $\mathsf Y=(Y(\cdot,\alpha))_\alpha$, a random element of
$C([0,r_L])^{\mathbb{N}^L}$. The map
$\mathsf V(s,\mathsf u,\mathsf y)
=\sup_\alpha\bigl(\sum_{\ell}\mathsf u_{\alpha|\ell}+\mathsf y_\alpha(s)-A(s)\bigr)$ is Borel on
$[0,r_L]\times\mathbb{R}^{\mathcal V}\times C([0,r_L])^{\mathbb{N}^L}$, because evaluation $(s,y)\mapsto y(s)$ is
continuous, $A$ is continuous and the supremum is countable. Let $h:(-\infty,\infty]\to\mathbb{R}$ be
bounded and Borel and let $H\in\mathcal H$. Since $(\mathsf q,\mathbf{1}_H)$ is independent of
$(u,\mathsf Y)$, $V=\mathsf V(\mathsf q,u,\mathsf Y)$ and Fubini's theorem give
$\mathbb{E}[h(V)\mathbf{1}_H]=\mathbb{E}[\varphi(\mathsf q)\mathbf{1}_H]$ with $\varphi(s)=\mathbb{E} h(\mathsf V(s,u,\mathsf Y))$. By
(a), $\varphi(s)=\mathbb{E} h(U)$ for every $s$, so $\mathbb{E}[h(V)\mathbf{1}_H]=\mathbb{E} h(U)\,\mathbb{P}(H)$.

\emph{Step 5: proof of (c).} The $\sigma$-fields $\mathcal G$ and $\sigma(u^b,Y^b)$, $b\ge1$, are
mutually independent. Fix $b$ and apply (b) to $(u^b,Y^b)$ with
$\mathcal H_b=\mathcal G\vee\sigma\bigl((u^{b'},Y^{b'}):b'\ne b\bigr)$: $V_b$ has the law of $U$ and
is independent of $\mathcal H_b$, which contains $\mathcal G$ and every $V_{b'}$ with $b'\ne b$.
For distinct $b_1,\dots,b_k$, Borel sets $D_1,\dots,D_k$ and $\Omega_0\in\mathcal G$, applying
this successively to $b_1,b_2,\dots$ gives
$\mathbb{P}\bigl(\Omega_0\cap\bigcap_{i\le k}\{V_{b_i}\in D_i\}\bigr)
=\mathbb{P}(\Omega_0)\prod_{i\le k}\mathbb{P}(U\in D_i)$.
<!-- end proof-39 -->
<!-- lemma-24: body_md -->
\label{lem:cascade-domination}
Assume $0<\mathsf{x}_1<\dots<\mathsf{x}_L$. For $1\le\ell\le L$ and every vertex $w$ of depth $\ell$ let
$\delta_\ell(w)$ be a measurable function of the path of $w$, and let $c_\ell\in\mathbb{R}$ be
deterministic with
\[
 \mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{\mathsf{x}_\ell\delta_\ell(vn)}\bigm|\mathcal G_{\ell-1}\bigr]\le e^{\mathsf{x}_\ell c_\ell}
 \quad\text{almost surely, for every vertex $v$ of depth $\ell-1$ and every $n$.}
\]
Then, for every $\lambda\in(0,\mathsf{x}_1)$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}\exp\Bigl(\lambda\sup_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^L}\Bigl(u_\alpha+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\delta_\ell(\alpha|\ell)\Bigr)\Bigr)
 \le e^{\lambda\sum_\ell c_\ell}\,\mathbb{E} e^{\lambda U}<\infty .
\]
<!-- end lemma-24 -->
<!-- proof-40: body_md -->
For a vertex $w$ of depth $\ell<L$ let
$R_w=\sup_{\alpha:\,\alpha|\ell=w}\sum_{k>\ell}\bigl(u_{\alpha|k}+\delta_k(\alpha|k)\bigr)$, and
$R_w=0$ for leaves; $R_\varnothing$ is the supremum in the statement. For $0\le\ell\le L$ let
$U^{(\ell)}$ be the supremum of the leaf labels of a cascade with the levels $\ell+1,\dots,L$ and
parameters $\mathsf{x}_{\ell+1},\dots,\mathsf{x}_L$, so that $U^{(L)}=0$ and $U^{(0)}=U$, and put
$c_{>\ell}=\sum_{k>\ell}c_k$ and $\mathsf{x}_{L+1}=\infty$. We show by downward induction on $\ell$ that,
for every $\lambda\in(0,\mathsf{x}_{\ell+1})$, $\mathbb{E} e^{\lambda U^{(\ell)}}<\infty$ and
\[
 \mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{\lambda R_w}\bigm|\mathcal G_\ell\bigr]\le e^{\lambda c_{>\ell}}\,\mathbb{E} e^{\lambda U^{(\ell)}}
 \qquad\text{for every vertex $w$ of depth $\ell$.}
\]
For $\ell=L$ there is nothing to prove. Let $1\le\ell\le L$, assume the statement at $\ell$, and fix
a vertex $v$ of depth $\ell-1$. Then $R_v=\sup_n(u_{vn}+Y_n)$ with $Y_n=\delta_\ell(vn)+R_{vn}$. By
the independence structure of the construction, conditionally on $\mathcal G_{\ell-1}$ the $Y_n$
are i.i.d.\ and independent of the labels $(u_{vn})_n$, which form a Poisson point process with
intensity $\mathsf{x}_\ell e^{-\mathsf{x}_\ell u}\,du$. By the induction hypothesis at $\lambda=\mathsf{x}_\ell<\mathsf{x}_{\ell+1}$
and the assumption on $\delta_\ell$,
\[
 \mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{\mathsf{x}_\ell Y_n}\bigm|\mathcal G_{\ell-1}\bigr]
 =\mathbb{E}\Bigl[e^{\mathsf{x}_\ell\delta_\ell(vn)}\,\mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{\mathsf{x}_\ell R_{vn}}\bigm|\mathcal G_\ell\bigr]\Bigm|\mathcal G_{\ell-1}\Bigr]
 \le e^{\mathsf{x}_\ell c_{\ge\ell}}\,\mathbb{E} e^{\mathsf{x}_\ell U^{(\ell)}}<\infty ,
\]
where $c_{\ge\ell}=c_\ell+c_{>\ell}$. Lemma~\ref{lem:poisson-shift} (with a one-point mark space),
applied conditionally on $\mathcal G_{\ell-1}$, shows that conditionally on $\mathcal G_{\ell-1}$
the supremum $R_v$ is attained and $R_v-\varkappa'_v$ has the law of the largest point $u_1$ of
that Poisson process, where
$\varkappa'_v=\mathsf{x}_\ell^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}[e^{\mathsf{x}_\ell Y_1}\mid\mathcal G_{\ell-1}]\le c_{\ge\ell}+\varkappa_\ell$
and $\varkappa_\ell=\mathsf{x}_\ell^{-1}\log\mathbb{E} e^{\mathsf{x}_\ell U^{(\ell)}}$. The same lemma, applied with i.i.d.\
copies of $U^{(\ell)}$ in place of the $Y_n$, gives $U^{(\ell-1)}\overset{d}{=}\varkappa_\ell+u_1$.
Since $\mathbb{P}(u_1>t)\le e^{-\mathsf{x}_\ell t}$, we have $\mathbb{E} e^{\lambda u_1}<\infty$, hence
$\mathbb{E} e^{\lambda U^{(\ell-1)}}<\infty$, for $\lambda<\mathsf{x}_\ell$, and then
\[
 \mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{\lambda R_v}\bigm|\mathcal G_{\ell-1}\bigr]=e^{\lambda\varkappa'_v}\,\mathbb{E} e^{\lambda u_1}
 \le e^{\lambda c_{\ge\ell}}e^{\lambda\varkappa_\ell}\,\mathbb{E} e^{\lambda u_1}
 =e^{\lambda c_{\ge\ell}}\,\mathbb{E} e^{\lambda U^{(\ell-1)}} .
\]
This is the statement at $\ell-1$. The case $\ell=0$, after taking expectations, is the lemma.
<!-- end proof-40 -->
<!-- remark-15: body_md -->
\label{rem:onsager-shift-scope}
The proof of Lemma~\ref{lem:onsager-shift} uses only $\mathsf{x}_\ell>0$ and $\vartheta'\ge0$ on $[0,r_L]$; it
needs no ordering of the parameters, no bound $\mathsf{x}_\ell\le1$ and no relation to a Parisi measure.
If $\mathsf{x}_1<\dots<\mathsf{x}_L$, then $U$ is almost surely finite and attained, so the supremum in
Lemma~\ref{lem:onsager-shift}\ref{lem:onsager-shift-a} is a maximum (for
\ref{lem:onsager-shift-b}--\ref{lem:onsager-shift-c} apply the argument of its Step~4 to the
indicator of attainment). By induction on $L$: for $L=1$, $U$ is the largest Poisson
point; for $L\ge2$, the subtree suprema $U^{[n]}$ are i.i.d., independent of the root labels, almost
surely finite and attained, and $\mathbb{E} e^{\mathsf{x}_1U^{[1]}}<\infty$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:cascade-domination}
for the subtree (parameters $\mathsf{x}_2<\dots<\mathsf{x}_L$, exponent $\mathsf{x}_1<\mathsf{x}_2$); so by
Lemma~\ref{lem:poisson-shift} with $\gamma_n=U^{[n]}$ only finitely many of the $u_n+U^{[n]}$ exceed
any level, and $U=\sup_n(u_n+U^{[n]})$ is attained.
<!-- end remark-15 -->
<!-- lemma-25: body_md -->
\label{lem:glued-terminal}
In the setting above, $\Psi_0=\Phi_\eta(Q,\cdot)$. For every $(s,g_0)$ as above, the function
$\Psi_s$ is convex and twice continuously differentiable, and
\[
 |\Psi_s'|<1,\qquad 0<\Psi_s''\le2\bigl(1-(\Psi_s')^2\bigr).
\]
Consequently Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class} applies to $W_s=W[\mathsf{x},\Psi_s]$ with $G=3$: for every
$t\in[0,Q]$, $W_s(t,\cdot)$ is convex, $|\partial_zW_s(t,\cdot)|<1$ and
$|W_s(t,z)-W_s(t,0)|\le|z|$.
<!-- end lemma-25 -->
<!-- proof-41: body_md -->
The first two assertions are Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-fenchel}\ref{lem:pde-fenchel-c}, since
$\mathcal T_2$ is the class of convex $C^2$ functions $\psi$ with $|\psi'|<1$ and
$\psi''\le2(1-\psi'^2)$. As $\mathcal T_2\subset\mathcal T_3$ and $\mathsf{x}$ takes values in $(0,3]$,
the last assertion is Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}\ref{lem:pde-class-a}
and~\ref{lem:pde-class-d}.
<!-- end proof-41 -->
<!-- proof-42: body_md -->
\emph{Step 0: deterministic reduction.}
Let $m\in\mathcal S$ and $Q'=q_m\in[Q,Q+\rho]$. The measure
$\operatorname{Shift}_{Q'}\eta=\eta|_{(Q',1]}+\eta([Q,Q'])\delta_{Q'}\in\mathcal{P}([Q',1])$ has distribution
function $\bar{\eta}$ on $[Q',1]$, so its solution of the Parisi equation coincides with
$\Phi_\eta$ on $[Q',1]$. Since $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$ is an infimum over $\mathcal{P}([q_m,1])$,
\[
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\le F_{\operatorname{Shift}_{Q'}\eta}(m)
 =H_N(m)+\sum_{i=1}^N\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q',m_i)-\frac N2\int_{Q'}^1t\xi''(t)\bar{\eta}(t)\,dt .
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}, on each step
$\partial_t\Phi_\eta=-\frac{\xi''}2(\partial_{xx}\Phi_\eta+\bar{\eta}\,(\partial_x\Phi_\eta)^2)\le0$,
so $\Phi_\eta(Q',\cdot)\le\Phi_\eta(Q,\cdot)$ and therefore
$\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q',\cdot)\le\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q,\cdot)$. Moreover
$\int_Q^{Q'}t\xi''\bar{\eta}\le\xi''(1)\rho$, since $\xi''$ is nondecreasing on $[0,1]$, and
$A(q_m)\ge A(Q)=\frac N2\int_0^Qt\xi''\mathsf{x}$, since $\bar\mathsf{x}\ge0$. Comparing with
\eqref{eq:glued-Ps} and \eqref{eq:glued-T},
\begin{equation}\label{eq:glued-step0}
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)+s\sum_{i=1}^Ng_0(m_i)-NP_s(\mathsf{x},\eta)\le T(m)+\frac N2\xi''(1)\rho\le\mathcal T,
\end{equation}
which is \eqref{eq:glued-pointwise}. The function $\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q,\cdot)$ is concave, hence
lower semicontinuous on the closed interval $[-1,1]$, and upper semicontinuous as an infimum of
affine functions, so it is continuous. Since $H_N$ has almost surely continuous paths under
\hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}, $T$ is almost surely continuous on $\mathcal S$. Given \eqref{eq:glued-goal},
\eqref{eq:glued-moment} follows from \eqref{eq:glued-majorant}, $\kappa_\rho\le\xi''(1)\rho$
and $y\le3$:
\[
 \frac1N\log\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T}\le\theta\Bigl[\frac12\xi''(1)\rho+\frac{d_N}N\Bigr]
 \le\theta\Bigl[\Bigl(\frac12+1+\frac y2\Bigl(1+\frac1N\Bigr)\Bigr)\xi''(1)\rho
 +\mathbf{1}_{\{\rho>0\}}\frac{\log(N+1)}{yN}\Bigr],
\]
and $\frac12+1+\frac y2(1+\frac1N)\le\frac92$. It remains to prove \eqref{eq:glued-goal}.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Step 1: the cascade.}
If $Q>0$, set $r_\ell=q_\ell$ for $0\le\ell<L$ and $r_L=Q+\rho$. Level $\ell$ is
$[r_{\ell-1},r_\ell]$ with parameter $\mathsf{x}_\ell$, so the top level $[q_{L-1},Q+\rho]$ has
parameter $y$. If $Q=0$, use a single level: $L=1$, $r_1=\rho$, with parameter $\mathsf{x}_1=y=1$. In
both cases $\theta<\mathsf{x}_1<\dots<\mathsf{x}_L\le3$, $\bar\mathsf{x}=\mathsf{x}_\ell$ on $[r_{\ell-1},r_\ell)$, and
$r_L\le1$. Let $(u_\alpha)_{\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^L}$ be the labels of the additive Ruelle probability
cascade with these levels and parameters, let $Y$ be the Onsager field, both as in
Appendix~\ref{app:pde-cascade} (they are the objects of \cite[Definitions~2.2
and~2.3]{Bou26b}), and let $U=\sup_\alpha u_\alpha$. Let $B^i_s(\alpha):=B^i(s,\alpha)$, $1\le i\le N$,
$s\in[0,r_L]$, be the cavity fields of Appendix~\ref{app:pde-cascade}
(\cite[Definition~2.3]{Bou26b}), and take the cascade and all fields independent of $H_N$. The
$B^i$ are centred Gaussian processes with continuous paths and
\[
 \mathbb{E} B^i_s(\alpha)B^j_t(\beta)=\delta_{ij}\,\xi'(s\wedge t\wedge r_{\alpha\wedge\beta}).
\]
They are built like $Y$, from independent Brownian motions attached to the vertices of the
tree, with $\vartheta$ replaced by $\xi'$ and one family for each $i$. Along a leaf, each
$B^i(\alpha)$ is a Gaussian martingale with $\langle B^i(\alpha)\rangle_t=\xi'(t)$, and two
leaves with $\alpha\wedge\beta\ge\ell$ have the same paths on $[0,r_\ell]$. Let $\mathcal G_\ell$
be the $\sigma$-field generated by the labels at levels at most $\ell$ and all paths on
$[0,r_\ell]$, as in Lemma~\ref{lem:cascade-domination}. Given $\mathcal G_{\ell-1}$, the
increments of the paths on $[r_{\ell-1},r_\ell]$ along the children of a vertex at level
$\ell-1$ are independent of each other and of $\mathcal G_{\ell-1}$, and the cavity-field
components of each are $N$ independent continuous Gaussian processes with independent increments and quadratic variation
$\xi'(t)-\xi'(r_{\ell-1})$.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Step 2: the outer level.}
Fix a finite set $D\subset\mathcal S$. Let $(w_b)_{b\ge1}$ be the points of a Poisson point
process on $\mathbb{R}$ with intensity $\theta e^{-\theta w}\,dw$, and let $(H_N^b,u^b,Y^b,B^b)$,
$b\ge1$, be independent copies of $(H_N,u,Y,B)$, independent of $(w_b)$. This outer level is
Boursier's device for exponential moments \cite[Proposition~2.7, Steps~1--2]{Bou26b}, the
mechanism of \cite{CGKLM}, as she notes. For $b\ge1$, $m\in D$ and $\alpha\in\mathbb{N}^L$ set
\begin{align*}
 X_b(m,\alpha)&=w_b+H_N^b(m)+Y^b(q_m,\alpha)+u^b_\alpha+\Upsilon(m),\\
 \widetilde X_b(m,\alpha)&=w_b+Z^b(m,\alpha)+u^b_\alpha+\Upsilon(m),
\end{align*}
where $\Upsilon(m)=\sum_{i}[\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q,m_i)+s\,g_0(m_i)]-NW_s(0,0)$ and
$Z^b(m,\alpha)=\sum_im_iB^{b,i}_{q_m}(\alpha)$. These are defined because $q_m\le Q+\rho=r_L$.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Step 3: Slepian's lemma.}
Condition on all labels $(w_b)$ and $(u^b)$. The two families are then Gaussian with the same
mean $w_b+u^b_\alpha+\Upsilon(m)$. Their variances agree:
$\mathbb{E}(H_N(m)+Y(q_m,\alpha))^2=N\xi(q_m)+N\vartheta(q_m)=Nq_m\xi'(q_m)=\mathbb{E} Z(m,\alpha)^2$. For two index
points in the same copy, with $R_{12}=R(m^1,m^2)\in[-1,1]$ and
$Q_{12}=q_{m^1}\wedge q_{m^2}\wedge r_{\alpha^1\wedge\alpha^2}\in[0,1]$, the covariance of the
first family exceeds that of the second by
\[
 N\bigl[\xi(R_{12})+\vartheta(Q_{12})-R_{12}\xi'(Q_{12})\bigr]
 =N\bigl[\xi(R_{12})-\xi(Q_{12})-\xi'(Q_{12})(R_{12}-Q_{12})\bigr]\ge0 .
\]
This is where convexity of $\xi$ enters; since $R_{12}$ may be negative, it is needed on all of
$[-1,1]$, and odd degrees are allowed. For index points in different copies both covariances
vanish. By Slepian's lemma, on every finite set of indices the maximum of the first family is
stochastically dominated by the maximum of the second. Take finite index sets increasing to
$\{(b,m,\alpha):b\ge1,\ m\in D,\ \alpha\in\mathbb{N}^L\}$ and use monotone convergence (the maxima are
bounded below by the value at one index point, which is integrable):
\begin{equation}\label{eq:glued-slepian}
 \mathbb{E}\sup_{b,\,m\in D,\,\alpha}X_b(m,\alpha)\le\mathbb{E}\sup_{b,\,m\in D,\,\alpha}\widetilde X_b(m,\alpha).
\end{equation}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Step 4: Fenchel's inequality.}
By \eqref{eq:glued-terminal}, $m_iz+\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q,m_i)+s\,g_0(m_i)\le\Psi_s(z)$ for every
$z\in\mathbb{R}$. Let
\[
 S_t(\alpha)=\sum_{i=1}^NW_s\bigl(t,B^i_t(\alpha)\bigr)\quad(0\le t\le Q),\qquad
 S_t(\alpha)=\sum_{i=1}^N\Psi_s\bigl(B^i_t(\alpha)\bigr)\quad(Q\le t\le Q+\rho).
\]
The two definitions agree at $t=Q$ because $W_s(Q,\cdot)=\Psi_s$, and $S_0=NW_s(0,0)$ because
$B_0=0$. Then $Z(m,\alpha)+\Upsilon(m)\le S_{q_m}(\alpha)-S_0$, and since
$q_m\in[Q,Q+\rho]$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:glued-fenchel}
 \widetilde X_b(m,\alpha)\le w_b+u^b_\alpha+\sup_{Q\le t\le Q+\rho}\bigl(S^b_t(\alpha)-S^b_0\bigr)
 =w_b+u^b_\alpha+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\delta^b_\ell(\alpha|\ell),
\end{equation}
where $\delta_\ell=S_{r_\ell}-S_{r_{\ell-1}}$ for $\ell<L$ and
$\delta_L=\sup_{Q\le t\le Q+\rho}S_t-S_{r_{L-1}}$. Leaves through the vertex $\alpha|\ell$ share
their paths on $[0,r_\ell]$, so $\delta_\ell$ is a measurable functional of the path of
$\alpha|\ell$ on $[0,r_\ell]$.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Step 5: the cascade side.}
We check the hypothesis of Lemma~\ref{lem:cascade-domination}: for every vertex $v$ at level
$\ell-1$ and every child $vn$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:glued-levels}
 \mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{\mathsf{x}_\ell\,\delta_\ell(vn)}\bigm|\mathcal G_{\ell-1}\bigr]\le e^{\mathsf{x}_\ell c_\ell},
 \qquad c_\ell=0\ \ (\ell<L),\qquad c_L=d_N .
\end{equation}

\emph{Exact levels.} Let $\ell<L$; or let $\ell=L$ and $Q>0$, with $r_L$ replaced by $Q$ in what
follows. Given $\mathcal G_{\ell-1}$, the starting points $B^i_{r_{\ell-1}}(vn)$ are known, and
the increments $B^i_{r_\ell}(vn)-B^i_{r_{\ell-1}}(vn)$, $1\le i\le N$, are independent
$N(0,\xi'(r_\ell)-\xi'(r_{\ell-1}))$ variables, independent of $\mathcal G_{\ell-1}$. On
$[r_{\ell-1},r_\ell)$ the coefficient $\mathsf{x}$ equals $\mathsf{x}_\ell$, so the definition
\eqref{eq:glued-colehopf} of $W_s$, applied coordinate by coordinate, gives
\begin{equation}\label{eq:glued-exact}
 \mathbb{E}\bigl[e^{\mathsf{x}_\ell(S_{r_\ell}-S_{r_{\ell-1}})(vn)}\bigm|\mathcal G_{\ell-1}\bigr]=1 ;
\end{equation}
the exponential moments are finite because $|W_s(t,z)-W_s(t,0)|\le|z|$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:glued-terminal}). This proves \eqref{eq:glued-levels} for $\ell<L$, and for
$\ell=L$ when $\rho=0$. Identity \eqref{eq:glued-exact} is the level-wise identity behind the
second identity of \cite[Remark~2.2]{Bou26b} (her martingale step, p.~9), here read off from the Cole--Hopf recursion with an arbitrary
terminal value at $Q$.

\emph{Doob's inequality on the shell.} Let $\rho>0$ and $\ell=L$; at this level $vn$ is a leaf
$\alpha$. Let $\mathcal G_Q$ be generated by $\mathcal G_{L-1}$ and all paths on $[0,Q]$, and
$\Delta=\sup_{Q\le t\le Q+\rho}(S_t-S_Q)$, so that $\delta_L=(S_Q-S_{r_{L-1}})+\Delta$. (If
$Q=0$, then $S_Q-S_{r_{L-1}}=0$ and $\mathcal G_Q$ is trivial.) By \eqref{eq:glued-exact} on
$[q_{L-1},Q]$, it suffices to show $\mathbb{E}[e^{y\Delta}\mid\mathcal G_Q]\le e^{yd_N}$. Given
$\mathcal G_Q$, the processes $(B^i_t-B^i_Q)_{t\in[Q,Q+\rho]}$ along $\alpha$ are independent
continuous Gaussian martingales with $d\langle B^i\rangle_t=\xi''(t)\,dt$. By It\^o's formula,
\[
 S_t-S_Q=M_t+\frac12\int_Q^t\xi''(r)\sum_{i=1}^N\Psi_s''(B^i_r)\,dr,\qquad
 M_t=\sum_{i=1}^N\int_Q^t\Psi_s'(B^i_r)\,dB^i_r .
\]
By Lemma~\ref{lem:glued-terminal}, $|\Psi_s'|<1$ and $0<\Psi_s''\le2$, so
$\langle M\rangle_t\le N\kappa_\rho$ and the drift term is at most $N\kappa_\rho$, where
$\kappa_\rho=\xi'(Q+\rho)-\xi'(Q)\le\xi''(1)\rho$. Let
$\mathcal E_t=\exp(yM_t-\frac{y^2}2\langle M\rangle_t)$, a martingale since $\langle M\rangle$
is bounded, and $p=1+\frac1N$. Then
$e^{y\Delta}\le e^{yN\kappa_\rho+y^2N\kappa_\rho/2}\sup_t\mathcal E_t$. Writing
$\mathcal E^p=\exp(pyM-\frac{p^2y^2}2\langle M\rangle)\exp(\frac{(p^2-p)y^2}2\langle M\rangle)$,
whose first factor has conditional expectation at most one, Doob's $L^p$ inequality gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}\Bigl[\sup_t\mathcal E_t\Bigm|\mathcal G_Q\Bigr]
 \le\frac p{p-1}\Bigl(\mathbb{E}\bigl[\mathcal E_{Q+\rho}^p\bigm|\mathcal G_Q\bigr]\Bigr)^{1/p}
 \le(N+1)\,e^{(p-1)y^2N\kappa_\rho/2}=(N+1)\,e^{y^2\kappa_\rho/2}.
\]
Hence $\mathbb{E}[e^{y\Delta}\mid\mathcal G_Q]\le(N+1)\exp\{yN\kappa_\rho+\frac{y^2(N+1)\kappa_\rho}2\}
=e^{yd_N}$, which is \eqref{eq:glued-levels} for $\ell=L$. This is the computation in the proof
of \cite[Lemma~2.5]{Bou26b}, performed on the shell only.

With \eqref{eq:glued-levels} and $\theta<\mathsf{x}_1$, Lemma~\ref{lem:cascade-domination} gives, for
$U''=\sup_\alpha\bigl(u_\alpha+\sum_{\ell=1}^L\delta_\ell(\alpha|\ell)\bigr)$,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:glued-cascade}
 \mathbb{E} e^{\theta U''}\le e^{\theta d_N}\,\mathbb{E} e^{\theta U}<\infty .
\end{equation}

\medskip\noindent\emph{Step 6: the lower side.}
By \eqref{eq:glued-T},
$X_b(m,\alpha)=w_b+T^b(m)+\bigl[u^b_\alpha+Y^b(q_m,\alpha)-A(q_m)\bigr]$, where $T^b$ is $T$
with $H_N$ replaced by $H_N^b$. Let $m^b_*$ be the first maximizer of $T^b$ over $D$ in a fixed
enumeration of $D$, and $q^b_*=q_{m^b_*}\in[Q,Q+\rho]\subset[0,r_L]$. Then
\[
 \sup_{m\in D,\,\alpha}X_b(m,\alpha)\ge w_b+\max_DT^b+V_b,\qquad
 V_b=\sup_\alpha\bigl(u^b_\alpha+Y^b(q^b_*,\alpha)-A(q^b_*)\bigr).
\]
The function $A$ is the shift of Lemma~\ref{lem:onsager-shift} for our cascade, because
$\bar\mathsf{x}=\mathsf{x}_\ell$ on $[r_{\ell-1},r_\ell)$. Apply part~(c) of that lemma with
$\mathcal G=\sigma\bigl((H_N^b)_{b\ge1},(w_b)_{b\ge1}\bigr)$, which is independent of the copies
$(u^b,Y^b)_{b\ge1}$, and with the $\mathcal G$-measurable radii $\mathsf q_b=q^b_*$: the
variables $V_b$ are i.i.d.\ with the law of $U$ and independent of $\mathcal G$. Since the
$H_N^b$ are i.i.d.\ and independent of $(w_b)$, the variables $\max_DT^b+V_b$, $b\ge1$, are
i.i.d., independent of $(w_b)$, and $\max_DT^b$ is independent of $V_b$.

\medskip\noindent\emph{Step 7: conclusion.}
We use the outer marking identity: if $(\chi_b)_{b\ge1}$ are i.i.d., independent of $(w_b)$,
and $\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\chi_1}<\infty$, then
\begin{equation}\label{eq:glued-outer}
 \mathbb{E}\sup_b(w_b+\chi_b)=\mathbb{E}\max_bw_b+\frac1\theta\log\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\chi_1},
\end{equation}
by Lemma~\ref{lem:poisson-shift} with $\mathsf{x}=\theta$ and a one-point mark space; this is
\cite[(2.11)]{Bou26b}, and $\mathbb{E}\max_bw_b$ is finite. On the upper side take $\chi_b=U''_b$, the
variable $U''$ of Step~5 for the $b$-th copy. The $U''_b$ are i.i.d.\ and independent of
$(w_b)$, so \eqref{eq:glued-fenchel}, \eqref{eq:glued-outer} and \eqref{eq:glued-cascade} give
\[
 \mathbb{E}\sup_{b,\,m\in D,\,\alpha}\widetilde X_b
 \le\mathbb{E}\max_bw_b+d_N+\frac1\theta\log\mathbb{E} e^{\theta U}.
\]
On the lower side take $\chi_b=\max_DT^b+V_b$. Here $\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\max_DT}<\infty$ because $D$ is
finite, and $\mathbb{E} e^{\theta U}<\infty$ by \eqref{eq:glued-cascade}; Step~6 and
\eqref{eq:glued-outer} give
\[
 \mathbb{E}\sup_{b,\,m\in D,\,\alpha}X_b
 \ge\mathbb{E}\max_bw_b+\frac1\theta\log\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\max_DT}+\frac1\theta\log\mathbb{E} e^{\theta U}.
\]
These two bounds and \eqref{eq:glued-slepian} form the chain \eqref{eq:glued-chain}. All its
terms are finite, so $\log\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\max_DT}\le\theta d_N$. Let $D$ increase along finite sets
to a countable dense subset of $\mathcal S$. By the continuity of $T$ (Step~0) and monotone
convergence, $\log\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\sup_{\mathcal S}T}\le\theta d_N$, which is
\eqref{eq:glued-goal}.
<!-- end proof-42 -->
<!-- lemma-26: body_md -->
\label{lem:pde-approx}
Let $\theta\in(0,1)$, $Q\in[0,1)$, $\mathsf{x}:[0,Q)\to[\theta,2]$ nondecreasing, $\eta\in\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$,
and $(s,g_0)$ as above. For $k\ge1$ let $\mathsf{x}_k(t)=\mathsf{x}(jQ/k)+1/k$ for $t\in[jQ/k,(j+1)Q/k)$,
$0\le j<k$, and let $\eta_k$ be the image of $\eta$ under
$t\mapsto Q+(1-Q)\lceil k(t-Q)/(1-Q)\rceil/k$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:pde-approx-a} $\mathsf{x}_k$ is a nondecreasing step function with values in
 $(\theta,3]$, and $\|\mathsf{x}_k-\mathsf{x}\|_{L^1}\le\frac Qk\bigl(\mathsf{x}(Q-)-\mathsf{x}(0)+1\bigr)$.
\item\label{lem:pde-approx-b} $\eta_k\in\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$ has a step distribution function, and
 $\|\bar{\eta_k}-\bar{\eta}\|_{L^1}=W_1(\eta_k,\eta)\le(1-Q)/k$.
\item\label{lem:pde-approx-c} For step data $(\mathsf{x}_1',\eta_1')$ and $(\mathsf{x}_2',\eta_2')$ with cascade
 coefficients taking values in $[0,3]$ (not necessarily monotone),
 \[
  |P_s(\mathsf{x}_1',\eta_1')-P_s(\mathsf{x}_2',\eta_2')|
  \le\xi''(1)\bigl(\|\mathsf{x}_1'-\mathsf{x}_2'\|_{L^1}+\|\bar{\eta_1'}-\bar{\eta_2'}\|_{L^1}\bigr),
 \]
 uniformly in $(s,g_0)$.
\end{thmlist}
Consequently $P_s$ extends uniquely to general data $(\mathsf{x},\eta)$ as a continuous function for the
$L^1$ distances, $|P_s(\mathsf{x}_k,\eta_k)-P_s(\mathsf{x},\eta)|\le\xi''(1)\bigl(\|\mathsf{x}_k-\mathsf{x}\|_{L^1}
+\|\bar{\eta_k}-\bar{\eta}\|_{L^1}\bigr)\le3\xi''(1)/k$, and
$P_0(\mathsf{x},\eta)=P(\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x},\eta))$ in the sense of Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}.
<!-- end lemma-26 -->
<!-- proof-43: body_md -->
(a) The values are $\mathsf{x}(jQ/k)+1/k\in(\theta,2+1/k]$, nondecreasing in $j$. On the $j$-th cell,
$|\mathsf{x}-\mathsf{x}_k|\le\mathsf{x}((j+1)Q/k-)-\mathsf{x}(jQ/k)+1/k$ by monotonicity, and summing over the cells
telescopes. (b) Each point moves by at most $(1-Q)/k$, and on the line the $W_1$ distance is the
$L^1$ distance of the distribution functions.

(c) For the cascade coefficient: $\Psi_s\in\mathcal T_2\subset\mathcal T_3$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-fenchel}, so Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-coef} with $G=3$ bounds the change of
$W[\cdot,\Psi_s](0,0)$ by $\frac12\xi''(1)\|\mathsf{x}_1'-\mathsf{x}_2'\|_{L^1}$, and the linear term changes by
at most as much. For the band measure: by Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-terminal},
$|W[\mathsf{x},\Psi^{(1)}_s]-W[\mathsf{x},\Psi^{(2)}_s]|\le\sup|\Psi^{(1)}_s-\Psi^{(2)}_s|$, where $\Psi^{(i)}_s$
is built from $\eta_i'$. The supremum defining $\Psi_s$ changes by at most
$\sup_m|\Phi^{*}_{\eta_1'}(Q,m)-\Phi^{*}_{\eta_2'}(Q,m)|\le\sup_y|\Phi_{\eta_1'}(Q,y)-\Phi_{\eta_2'}(Q,y)|$,
which is at most $\frac12\xi''(1)\|\bar{\eta_1'}-\bar{\eta_2'}\|_{L^1}$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-coef}
on $[Q,1]$; the linear term changes by at most as much. The consequences follow from density of
step data, from (a)--(b) with $\mathsf{x}(Q-)-\mathsf{x}(0)\le2$, and, for $s=0$, from
Corollary~\ref{cor:pde-step}\ref{cor:pde-step-c} and Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}, since
$\|\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x}_1',\eta_1')-\mathrm{glue}(\mathsf{x}_2',\eta_2')\|_{L^1}
=\|\mathsf{x}_1'-\mathsf{x}_2'\|_{L^1}+\|\bar{\eta_1'}-\bar{\eta_2'}\|_{L^1}$.
<!-- end proof-43 -->
<!-- corollary-4: body_md -->
\label{cor:pde-majorant}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}. Let $\rho\in[0,1-Q]$, with $\rho>0$ if $Q=0$, and let the other data be as in
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-approx}. For every $\varepsilon_A>0$ and $N\ge1$ there is a
random variable $\mathcal T'$ such that
\[
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)+s\sum_{i=1}^Ng_0(m_i)\le NP_s(\mathsf{x},\eta)+N\varepsilon_A+\mathcal T'
 \qquad\text{for every } m\in[-1,1]^N \text{ with } q_m\in[Q,Q+\rho],
\]
and $\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T'}\le(N+1)\,e^{N\theta C_R\rho}$.
The bound on $\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T'}$ depends neither on $Q$ nor on the data.
<!-- end corollary-4 -->
<!-- proof-44: body_md -->
Choose $k\ge3\xi''(1)/\varepsilon_A$, so that $P_s(\mathsf{x}_k,\eta_k)\le P_s(\mathsf{x},\eta)+\varepsilon_A$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-approx}. After merging equal neighbouring values, $\mathsf{x}_k$ is a step function with
strictly increasing values in $(\theta,3]$, so $(\mathsf{x}_k,\eta_k)$ are step data for
Proposition~\ref{prop:glued-comparison}, with top parameter $y_k=\mathsf{x}_k(Q-)>\theta$ (and $y=1>\theta$
if $Q=0$). Let $\mathcal T'$ be the random variable that the proposition provides for these data.
Then the pointwise bound holds, and
$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T'}\le(N+1)^{\theta/y_k}e^{N\theta C_R\rho}\le(N+1)e^{N\theta C_R\rho}$.
<!-- end proof-44 -->
<!-- lemma-27: body_md -->
\label{lem:var-net}
For every $\kappa>0$ there are $\tilde g_1,\dots,\tilde g_J\in C^\infty(\mathbb{R})$ with
$\|\tilde g_j'\|_\infty\le1$ and $\|\tilde g_j''\|_\infty<\infty$ such that, for all probability
measures $\mu,\mu'$ on $[-1,1]$,
\[
 W_1(\mu,\mu')\ge\kappa\quad\Longrightarrow\quad
 \int\tilde g_j\,d(\mu-\mu')\ge\frac\kappa2\ \text{ for some } j\le J .
\]
<!-- end lemma-27 -->
<!-- proof-45: body_md -->
The set $\mathcal L$ of $1$-Lipschitz functions on $[-1,1]$ that vanish at $0$ is compact for the
supremum norm, by the Arzel\`a--Ascoli theorem. Let $g_1,\dots,g_J$ be a $\kappa/16$-net of
$\mathcal L$. Extend each $g_j$ to a $1$-Lipschitz function on $\mathbb{R}$ and convolve it with a smooth
probability density supported in $[-\kappa/16,\kappa/16]$; the result $\tilde g_j$ is smooth, with
$\|\tilde g_j'\|_\infty\le1$, bounded second derivative, and $\sup_{[-1,1]}|\tilde g_j-g_j|\le\kappa/16$.
So every $g\in\mathcal L$ is within $\kappa/8$ of some $\tilde g_j$ on $[-1,1]$. By the
Kantorovich--Rubinstein duality, $W_1(\mu,\mu')=\sup_{g\in\mathcal L}\int g\,d(\mu-\mu')$. If
$W_1(\mu,\mu')\ge\kappa$, choose $g\in\mathcal L$ with $\int g\,d(\mu-\mu')\ge3\kappa/4$ and $j$
with $\sup_{[-1,1]}|g-\tilde g_j|\le\kappa/8$; then
$\int\tilde g_j\,d(\mu-\mu')\ge3\kappa/4-2\cdot\kappa/8=\kappa/2$.
<!-- end proof-45 -->
<!-- lemma-28: body_md -->
\label{lem:var-tangent}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}. Let $\theta\in(0,1)$ and $\zeta'\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ with $\zeta'(\{0\})\ge\theta$,
let $X'$ be the Auffinger--Chen process of $\zeta'$, and put
$L'_q=\operatorname{Law}(\Phi_{\zeta',x}(q,X'_q))$ for $q\in[0,1]$. Let $g\in C^2([-1,1])$ with
$\|g'\|_\infty\le1$, and let $|s|\le(2\|g''\|_\infty)^{-1}$. Put $C_2=1+L_\psi$, which depends
only on $\xi'(1)$ and $\xi''(1)$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:var-tangent-a} For every $Q\in[0,1)$,
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:var-tangent}
  P_s\bigl(\bar{\zeta'}|_{[0,Q)},\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta'\bigr)\le P_{\zeta'}+s\int g\,dL'_Q+C_2s^2 .
 \end{equation}
\item\label{lem:var-tangent-b} For every $Q\in[0,1)$, $\rho'\in(0,1-Q]$, $\varepsilon_A>0$ and
 $N\ge1$ there is a random variable $\mathcal T$ with
 $\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T}\le(N+1)e^{N\theta C_R\rho'}$ such that
 \begin{multline*}
  \sup\Bigl\{F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)+s\sum_{i=1}^Ng(m_i):\ m\in[-1,1]^N,\ q_m\in[Q,Q+\rho']\Bigr\}\\
  \le N\Bigl[P_{\zeta'}+s\int g\,dL'_Q+C_2s^2+\varepsilon_A\Bigr]+\mathcal T .
 \end{multline*}
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end lemma-28 -->
<!-- proof-46: body_md -->
\ref{lem:var-tangent-a} \emph{Step data.} Let $\mathsf{x}$ be a step function on $[0,Q)$ with values in
$[0,3]$ (none if $Q=0$), and let $\eta\in\mathcal{P}([Q,1])$ have a step distribution function. Let $c$ be their
glued coefficient~\eqref{eq:loc-glue}, $v_c=\partial_yW[c,\log\cosh]$, and $X^c$ the solution
of~\eqref{eq:pde-ac} for $(c,\log\cosh)$ from $(0,0)$. We claim that
\begin{equation}\label{eq:var-tangent-step}
 P_s(\mathsf{x},\eta)\le P_0(\mathsf{x},\eta)+s\,\mathbb{E} g\bigl(v_c(Q,X^c_Q)\bigr)+C_2s^2 .
\end{equation}
Let $\Psi_s$ and its maximizer $m^*_s$ be as in Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-fenchel}, and
$h=-\Phi^{*}_\eta(Q,\cdot)$, so that $h''\ge1$ and $\Psi_0'=m^*_0=\Phi_\eta'(Q,\cdot)$.

First, the perturbation of the terminal value. By the definition of $\Psi_s$ as a supremum,
$\Psi_s(z)\ge zm^*_0(z)-h(m^*_0(z))+s\,g(m^*_0(z))=\Psi_0(z)+s\,g(m^*_0(z))$. In the other
direction, the optimality conditions $h'(m^*_s(z))-s\,g'(m^*_s(z))=z=h'(m^*_0(z))$ and $h''\ge1$
give $|m^*_s(z)-m^*_0(z)|\le|s|\,\|g'\|_\infty\le|s|$, and therefore
\[
 \Psi_s(z)=zm^*_s-h(m^*_s)+s\,g(m^*_s)\le\Psi_0(z)+s\,g(m^*_s(z))
 \le\Psi_0(z)+s\,g(m^*_0(z))+s^2 .
\]
So $0\le\Psi_s-\Psi_0-s\,g\circ m^*_0\le s^2$, and $\|\Psi_s'-\Psi_0'\|_\infty=\sup|m^*_s-m^*_0|\le|s|$.

Next, the transport to the origin. If $Q=0$, then $P_s-P_0=\Psi_s(0)-\Psi_0(0)$, $m^*_0(0)=0$ and
$v_c(0,X^c_0)=0$, so~\eqref{eq:var-tangent-step} follows from the last display. Let $Q>0$. The
integral terms of $P_s$ and $P_0$ coincide, so $P_s-P_0=W[\mathsf{x},\Psi_s](0,0)-W[\mathsf{x},\Psi_0](0,0)$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-fenchel}, $\Psi_0,\Psi_s\in\mathcal T_2\subset\mathcal T_3$. Let $X^0$ and $X^s$
solve~\eqref{eq:pde-ac} on $[0,Q]$ for $(\mathsf{x},\Psi_0)$ and $(\mathsf{x},\Psi_s)$ from $(0,0)$, driven by
the same Brownian motion. The upper half of the terminal sandwich,
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-terminal}, gives
\[
 P_s-P_0\le\mathbb{E}\bigl[\Psi_s-\Psi_0\bigr](X^s_Q)\le s\,\mathbb{E} g\bigl(m^*_0(X^s_Q)\bigr)+s^2 .
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-stability} with equal coefficients gives
$\sup_r|X^s_r-X^0_r|\le L_\psi\|\Psi_s'-\Psi_0'\|_\infty\le L_\psi|s|$. The function $g\circ m^*_0$
is $1$-Lipschitz, because $g$ is and $(m^*_0)'=\Phi_\eta''(Q,\cdot)\le1$
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-fenchel}\ref{lem:pde-fenchel-a}); hence
$s\,\mathbb{E} g(m^*_0(X^s_Q))\le s\,\mathbb{E} g(m^*_0(X^0_Q))+L_\psi s^2$. Finally, the recursion
\eqref{eq:pde-colehopf} on $[0,Q]$ with terminal value $\Psi_0=\Phi_\eta(Q,\cdot)$ continues the one
on $[Q,1]$, so $W[\mathsf{x},\Psi_0]$ and $\Phi_\eta$ together form $W[c,\log\cosh]$; thus $X^0=X^c$ on
$[0,Q]$ and $m^*_0(X^0_Q)=v_c(Q,X^c_Q)$. This proves~\eqref{eq:var-tangent-step}.

\emph{General data.} Let $\mathsf{x}=\bar{\zeta'}|_{[0,Q)}$ and $\eta=\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta'$. These data are
admissible in Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-approx}, since $\mathsf{x}$ is nondecreasing with values in
$[\theta,1]$, and their glued coefficient is $\bar{\zeta'}$. Let $(\mathsf{x}_k,\eta_k)$ be the step data
of Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-approx}, with glued coefficients $c_k$. Then
$\|c_k-\bar{\zeta'}\|_{L^1}\le3/k$, and as $k\to\infty$:
$P_s(\mathsf{x}_k,\eta_k)\to P_s(\mathsf{x},\eta)$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-approx};
$P_0(\mathsf{x}_k,\eta_k)=P(c_k)\to P(\bar{\zeta'})=P_{\zeta'}$ by Corollary~\ref{cor:pde-step}\ref{cor:pde-step-c}
and Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-iv}; and, since $g$ is $1$-Lipschitz,
\[
 \bigl|\mathbb{E} g\bigl(v_{c_k}(Q,X^{c_k}_Q)\bigr)-\textstyle\int g\,dL'_Q\bigr|
 \le\mathbb{E}\bigl|v_{c_k}(Q,X^{c_k}_Q)-v_{\bar{\zeta'}}(Q,X^{\bar{\zeta'}}_Q)\bigr|
 \le L_M\|c_k-\bar{\zeta'}\|_{L^1}\to0
\]
by Corollary~\ref{cor:pde-step}\ref{cor:pde-step-d}, extended to measurable coefficients by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}, which also identifies $v_{\bar{\zeta'}}(Q,X^{\bar{\zeta'}}_Q)$ with
$\Phi_{\zeta',x}(Q,X'_Q)$. Applying~\eqref{eq:var-tangent-step} to $(\mathsf{x}_k,\eta_k)$ and letting
$k\to\infty$ gives~\eqref{eq:var-tangent}.

\ref{lem:var-tangent-b} The data $(\bar{\zeta'}|_{[0,Q)},\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta')$ and the perturbation
$(s,g)$ are admissible in Corollary~\ref{cor:pde-majorant}, which is~\eqref{eq:loc-glued-general};
it gives $\mathcal T$ with the stated moment bound and
$\sup[F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)+s\sum_ig(m_i)]\le NP_s(\bar{\zeta'}|_{[0,Q)},\operatorname{Shift}_Q\zeta')+N\varepsilon_A+\mathcal T$
over the shell. Insert~\eqref{eq:var-tangent}.
<!-- end proof-46 -->
<!-- proof-47: body_md -->
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}, fix $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ and $\kappa>0$, and write $\theta=\theta_f$, $\zeta=\zeta_f$ (any
constrained minimizer) and $X$ for the Auffinger--Chen process of $\zeta$, so that
$L_{q}=\operatorname{Law}(\Phi_{\zeta,x}(q,X_q))$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:loc-obstacle}, $\zeta(\{0\})=\theta$ and
$\Sigma(f)=\theta(P_\zeta-f)$.

\emph{Test functions and continuity in the radius.} Let $\tilde g_1,\dots,\tilde g_J$ be given by
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-net} for $\kappa$; they are the functions $g_j$ of
Section~\ref{sec:loc-field}. The map $q\mapsto\Phi_{\zeta,x}(q,X_q)$ is almost surely continuous on
$[0,1]$ and bounded by one (Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}), so by dominated convergence each
$q\mapsto\int\tilde g_j\,dL_{q}$ is continuous, hence uniformly continuous, on $[0,1]$. Let
$\omega$ be a common modulus of continuity for $j\le J$.

\emph{Parameters.} Choose, in this order,
\[
 s=\min\Bigl\{\frac{\kappa}{8C_2},\ \bigl(2\max_j\|\tilde g_j''\|_\infty\bigr)^{-1}\Bigr\},
 \qquad \rho\in(0,1]\ \text{with}\ C_R\rho\le\frac{s\kappa}{16}\ \text{and}\
 \omega(\rho)\le\frac\kappa{16},
\]
and put $\delta=s\kappa/16$ and $\varepsilon_A=s\kappa/32$. Then $C_2s^2\le s\kappa/8$, and
$(s,\tilde g_j)$ is admissible in Lemma~\ref{lem:var-tangent}.

\emph{One shell and one test function.} Let $Q_i=i\rho$ and $I_i=[Q_i,\min(Q_i+\rho,1)]$ for the
integers $i\ge0$ with $Q_i<1$. Fix $i$ and $j$. Suppose that $m\in[-1,1]^N$ has $q_m\in I_i$,
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\ge N(f-\delta)$ and $N^{-1}\sum_k\tilde g_j(m_k)\ge\int\tilde g_j\,dL_{q_m}+\kappa/2$.
Since $|\int\tilde g_j\,dL_{q_m}-\int\tilde g_j\,dL_{Q_i}|\le\omega(\rho)$,
\[
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)+s\sum_{k=1}^N\tilde g_j(m_k)\ge
 N\Bigl[f-\delta+s\Bigl(\int\tilde g_j\,dL_{Q_i}-\omega(\rho)+\frac\kappa2\Bigr)\Bigr].
\]
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-tangent}\ref{lem:var-tangent-b}, with $\zeta'=\zeta$, $Q=Q_i$,
$\rho'=\min(\rho,1-Q_i)$ and $g=\tilde g_j$, provides a random variable $\mathcal T_{ij}$ with
$\mathbb{E} e^{\theta\mathcal T_{ij}}\le(N+1)e^{N\theta C_R\rho}$ that bounds the left side by
$N[P_\zeta+s\int\tilde g_j\,dL_{Q_i}+C_2s^2+\varepsilon_A]+\mathcal T_{ij}$. The terms
$s\int\tilde g_j\,dL_{Q_i}$ cancel, so such an $m$ can exist only on the event
\[
 \Bigl\{\mathcal T_{ij}\ge N\Bigl[f-P_\zeta-\delta-s\,\omega(\rho)+\frac{s\kappa}2-C_2s^2
 -\varepsilon_A\Bigr]\Bigr\}.
\]
By Markov's inequality applied to $e^{\theta\mathcal T_{ij}}$, and $\Sigma(f)=\theta(P_\zeta-f)$,
this event has probability at most
\[
 (N+1)\exp N\Bigl\{\Sigma(f)+\theta\Bigl[C_2s^2+\varepsilon_A+C_R\rho+\delta+s\,\omega(\rho)
 -\frac{s\kappa}2\Bigr]\Bigr\}.
\]

\emph{The exponent budget.} By the choice of parameters, the bracket is at most
\begin{equation}\label{eq:var-budget}
 s\kappa\Bigl(\frac4{32}+\frac1{32}+\frac2{32}+\frac2{32}+\frac2{32}-\frac{16}{32}\Bigr)
 =-\frac5{32}\,s\kappa .
\end{equation}
The gain $s\kappa/2$ is linear in $s$, the cost $C_2s^2$ of the perturbation is quadratic, and the
remaining errors were chosen small compared with $s\kappa$.

\emph{Union bound.} If $W_1(\mu_m,L_{q_m})\ge\kappa$, then $q_m\in I_i$ for some $i$, and
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-net} gives a $j$ with $N^{-1}\sum_k\tilde g_j(m_k)\ge\int\tilde g_j\,dL_{q_m}
+\kappa/2$. So the event of~\ref{thm:struct-ii} is contained in the union of the events above over
the at most $(\lceil1/\rho\rceil+1)J$ pairs $(i,j)$, a finite union of measurable events. Its
outer probability is at most
$(\lceil1/\rho\rceil+1)J(N+1)e^{N(\Sigma(f)-5\theta s\kappa/32)}\le e^{N(\Sigma(f)-\theta s\kappa/8)}$
for all large $N$. This proves~\ref{thm:struct-ii} with $\delta=s\kappa/16$ and
$c=\theta_f s\kappa/8$.
<!-- end proof-47 -->
<!-- lemma-29: body_md -->
\label{lem:gauss-field}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}\ and fix $N$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:gauss-field-a} There is $r>1$, depending only on $\xi$, such that almost surely the
 series defining $H_N$ and the series of its first partial derivatives converge uniformly on
 $[-r,r]^N$. In particular $H_N$ is almost surely continuously differentiable on a neighbourhood
 of $[-1,1]^N$, and $\sup_{[-1,1]^N}|\partial_iH_N|<\infty$ for every $i$.
\item\label{lem:gauss-field-b} For $x,y\in[-1,1]^N$, $\mathbb{E}(H_N(x)-H_N(y))^2\le K_\xi|x-y|^2$, and
 \[
  \mathbb{E}\sup_{[-1,1]^N}H_N\le\sqrt{2K_\xi/\pi}\;N .
 \]
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end lemma-29 -->
<!-- proof-48: body_md -->
\emph{One degree.} Let $\rho\ge1$ and $x,y\in[-\rho,\rho]^N$, so that $|x|,|y|\le\rho\sqrt N$.
Writing $x^{\otimes p}-y^{\otimes p}=\sum_{k=0}^{p-1}x^{\otimes k}\otimes(x-y)\otimes
y^{\otimes(p-1-k)}$ gives $|x^{\otimes p}-y^{\otimes p}|\le p(\rho\sqrt N)^{p-1}|x-y|$, hence
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gauss-increment}
 \mathbb{E}\bigl(H_{N,p}(x)-H_{N,p}(y)\bigr)^2=N^{1-p}\,|x^{\otimes p}-y^{\otimes p}|^2
 \le p^2\rho^{2(p-1)}|x-y|^2 .
\end{equation}
Compare $H_{N,p}$ on $[-\rho,\rho]^N$ with the process $p\rho^{p-1}g\cdot x$, where $g$ is a
standard Gaussian vector of $\mathbb{R}^N$, and note that
\[
 \mathbb{E}\sup_{x\in[-\rho,\rho]^N}g\cdot x=\rho\,\mathbb{E}\sum_{i=1}^N|g_i|=\rho N\sqrt{2/\pi}.
\]
The Sudakov--Fernique inequality gives $\mathbb{E}\sup_{[-\rho,\rho]^N}H_{N,p}\le\sqrt{2/\pi}\,p\rho^pN$,
and the same bound for $-H_{N,p}$. Both suprema are nonnegative because $H_{N,p}(0)=0$, so
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gauss-sup-p}
 \mathbb{E}\sup_{[-\rho,\rho]^N}|H_{N,p}|\le2\sqrt{2/\pi}\;p\rho^pN .
\end{equation}

\ref{lem:gauss-field-a} Let $R_\xi>1$ be the radius of convergence of $\xi$ and fix
$r\in(1,R_\xi^{1/2})$. For fixed $i$ and fixed coordinates $x_j$, $j\ne i$, in $[-r,r]$, the map
$s\mapsto H_{N,p}(x_1,\dots,x_{i-1},s,x_{i+1},\dots,x_N)$ is a polynomial of degree at most $p$.
A.~A.~Markov's inequality for the derivative of a polynomial, $\max_{[-r,r]}|P'|\le
p^2r^{-1}\max_{[-r,r]}|P|$ for $\deg P\le p$, therefore gives
$\sup_{[-r,r]^N}|\partial_iH_{N,p}|\le p^2r^{-1}\sup_{[-r,r]^N}|H_{N,p}|$. With
\eqref{eq:gauss-sup-p},
\[
 \mathbb{E}\sum_{p\ge2}|\beta_p|\sup_{[-r,r]^N}\Bigl(|H_{N,p}|+\sum_{i=1}^N|\partial_iH_{N,p}|\Bigr)
 \le2\sqrt{2/\pi}\,N(1+N)\sum_{p\ge2}p^3|\beta_p|r^p<\infty,
\]
because $\limsup_p(|\beta_p|r^p)^{1/p}=rR_\xi^{-1/2}<1$. So almost surely both series converge
absolutely and uniformly on $[-r,r]^N$, and $H_N$ is continuously differentiable on $(-r,r)^N$.

\ref{lem:gauss-field-b} By independence of the $H_{N,p}$ and \eqref{eq:gauss-increment} with
$\rho=1$, $\mathbb{E}(H_N(x)-H_N(y))^2\le\sum_p\beta_p^2p^2|x-y|^2=K_\xi|x-y|^2$. By~\ref{lem:gauss-field-a}
the field is continuous on $[-1,1]^N$, and the Sudakov--Fernique inequality against $\sqrt{K_\xi}\,g\cdot x$
gives $\mathbb{E}\sup_{[-1,1]^N}H_N\le\sqrt{K_\xi}\,\mathbb{E}\sup_{[-1,1]^N}g\cdot x=\sqrt{2K_\xi/\pi}\,N$.
<!-- end proof-48 -->
<!-- lemma-30: body_md -->
\label{lem:gauss-bounds}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. Put $C^{\max}_\xi=\sqrt{2K_\xi/\pi}+\xi'(1)/2$ and, for $\theta>0$,
$C_\theta=\theta\sqrt{2K_\xi/\pi}+\theta^2\xi(1)$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:gauss-bounds-a} \textup{(Partition function.)} For $\theta>0$, $\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ge1$
 and $\mathbb{E}Z_N^{2\theta}\le e^{2C_\theta N}$; if moreover $\theta\le1$, then
 $\mathbb{E}Z_N^{2\theta}\le e^{2\theta N\xi(1)}$. For $\theta<0$,
 $\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ge e^{-|\theta|\sqrt{2K_\xi/\pi}\,N}$ and $\mathbb{E}Z_N^{2\theta}\le e^{2\theta^2N\xi(1)}$.
\item\label{lem:gauss-bounds-b} \textup{(Deterministic bounds.)} $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(0)=Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}$, and
 $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\leH_N(x)+N\xi'(1)/2$ for every $x\in[-1,1]^N$. Hence
 $Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}\leM_N\le\sup_{[-1,1]^N}H_N+N\xi'(1)/2$.
\item\label{lem:gauss-bounds-c} \textup{(The maximum.)} For $\lambda>0$,
 $\mathbb{E} e^{\lambdaM_N}\le\exp\{N[C^{\max}_\xi\lambda+\lambda^2\xi(1)/2]\}$; for $\lambda<0$,
 $\mathbb{E} e^{\lambdaM_N}\le e^{\lambda Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}}$.
\item\label{lem:gauss-bounds-d} \textup{(Truncation.)} Let $D$ be at least the smallest active
 degree.
 \begin{enumerate}[label=\textup{(d\arabic*)}, ref=(d\arabic*), leftmargin=*, topsep=2pt,
  itemsep=1pt, beginpenalty=10000]
 \item\label{lem:gauss-bounds-d1} For every $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$,
  $0\le\Phi_\zeta-\Phi^{(D)}_\zeta\le\xi'_{>D}(1)$ on $[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$ and
  $|P_\zeta-P^{(D)}_\zeta|\le\frac32\xi'_{>D}(1)$. Consequently
  $|f_{\mathrm{eq}}-f_{\mathrm{eq}}^{(D)}|\le\frac32\xi'_{>D}(1)$,
  $\sup_{\theta\in[0,1)}|\Lambda(\theta)-\Lambda^{(D)}(\theta)|\le\frac32\xi'_{>D}(1)$,
  $\sup_{\mu\in\mathcal{P}([-1,1])}|\mathrm{TAP}(\mu)-\mathrm{TAP}^{(D)}(\mu)|\le\frac32\xi'_{>D}(1)$, and
  \[
   |\logZ_N-\logZ_N^{(D)}|\le T_D,\qquad
   \sup_{[-1,1]^N}|F_{\mathrm{TAP}}-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}^{(D)}|\le T_D+\tfrac32N\xi'_{>D}(1),
  \]
  and the last bound also holds for $|M_N-M_N^{(D)}|$.
 \item\label{lem:gauss-bounds-d2} $\mathbb{E} T_D\le\varepsilon_DN$, and
  $\mathbb{P}\bigl(T_D>(\varepsilon_D+u)N\bigr)\le\exp\bigl(-u^2N/(2\xi_{>D}(1))\bigr)$ for $u>0$ if
  $\xi_{>D}\not\equiv0$ (otherwise $T_D=0$).
 \item\label{lem:gauss-bounds-d3} For $\theta>0$,
  $\bigl|N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta-N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}(Z_N^{(D)})^\theta\bigr|
  \le\theta\varepsilon_D+\theta^2\xi_{>D}(1)/2$.
 \end{enumerate}
\item\label{lem:gauss-bounds-e} \textup{(Tilts.)} For $\theta>0$ and every event $A$,
 $\mathbb{Q}_\theta(A)\le e^{C_\theta N}\mathbb{P}(A)^{1/2}$; for $\theta\in(0,1]$ also
 $\mathbb{Q}_\theta(A)\le e^{\theta N\xi(1)}\mathbb{P}(A)^{1/2}$.
\end{thmlist}
In particular, \eqref{eq:max-crude} holds for every $\theta\ne0$ and every $N$ with
$C(\xi,\theta)=2|\theta|(C^{\max}_\xi+|f_{\mathrm{eq}}|)+2\theta^2\xi(1)$.
<!-- end lemma-30 -->
<!-- proof-49: body_md -->
Write $S=\sup_{[-1,1]^N}H_N$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-field}, $S$ is finite and
$\mathbb{E} S\le\sqrt{2K_\xi/\pi}\,N$. Since $\operatorname{Var}H_N(x)=N\xi(q_x)\le N\xi(1)$, the bounds
\eqref{eq:gauss-conc} apply to $S$ with $\sigma^2=N\xi(1)$.

\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-a} By Jensen's inequality for the average over $\sigma$,
$\logZ_N\ge L:=2^{-N}\sum_{\sigma\in\{-1,1\}^N}H_N(\sigma)$, a centered Gaussian variable with
$\operatorname{Var} L=2^{-2N}\sum_{\sigma,\sigma'}N\xi(R(\sigma,\sigma'))\le N\xi(1)$, since
$|\xi(t)|\le\xi(1)$ on $[-1,1]$. Also $\logZ_N\le\max_{\{-1,1\}^N}H_N\le S$, so $\logZ_N$ is
integrable. For $\theta>0$, Jensen's inequality gives
$\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ge e^{\theta\mathbb{E}\logZ_N}\ge e^{\theta\mathbb{E} L}=1$, and \eqref{eq:gauss-conc} with
$\lambda=2\theta$ gives $\mathbb{E}Z_N^{2\theta}\le\mathbb{E} e^{2\theta S}\le e^{2\theta\mathbb{E} S+2\theta^2N\xi(1)}\le
e^{2C_\theta N}$. If $\theta\le1$, then $\mathbb{E}Z_N^{2\theta}\le(\mathbb{E}Z_N^2)^\theta$ and
$\mathbb{E}Z_N^2=2^{-2N}\sum_{\sigma,\sigma'}e^{N\xi(1)+N\xi(R(\sigma,\sigma'))}\le e^{2N\xi(1)}$. For
$\theta<0$, $\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ge e^{\theta\mathbb{E}\logZ_N}\ge e^{\theta\mathbb{E} S}\ge e^{-|\theta|\sqrt{2K_\xi/\pi}N}$,
and $Z_N^{2\theta}\le e^{2\theta L}$ gives $\mathbb{E}Z_N^{2\theta}\le e^{2\theta^2\operatorname{Var} L}\le
e^{2\theta^2N\xi(1)}$.

\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-b} Since $H_N(0)=0$ and $q_0=0$, $F_\zeta(0)=N\Phi^{*}_\zeta(0,0)-\frac
N2\int_0^1t\xi''(t)\bar{\zeta}(t)\,dt$. The function $\Phi_\zeta(0,\cdot)$ is even and convex
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-i}), so
$\Phi^{*}_\zeta(0,0)=\inf_b\Phi_\zeta(0,b)=\Phi_\zeta(0,0)$. Hence $F_\zeta(0)=NP_\zeta$ for every
$\zeta$, and $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(0)=Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}$ by \eqref{eq:intro-ftap}. For the upper bound, $\delta_1$ is
admissible in \eqref{eq:intro-ftap} at every $x$. Its distribution function vanishes on $[0,1)$, so
the integral term of $F_{\delta_1}$ vanishes and $\Phi_{\delta_1}$ solves the heat equation:
$\Phi_{\delta_1}(q,b)=\mathbb{E}\log\cosh\bigl(b+(\xi'(1)-\xi'(q))^{1/2}Z\bigr)$ with $Z$ standard
Gaussian, by \eqref{eq:pde-colehopf}. Taking $b=0$ in the infimum and using
$\log\cosh z\le z^2/2$ gives $\Phi^{*}_{\delta_1}(q,m)\le\Phi_{\delta_1}(q,0)\le\xi'(1)/2$ for
$|m|<1$, and for $m=\pm1$ by continuity. So $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\le F_{\delta_1}(x)\leH_N(x)+N\xi'(1)/2$.

\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-c} For $\lambda>0$, part~\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-b} and \eqref{eq:gauss-conc}
give $\mathbb{E} e^{\lambdaM_N}\le e^{\lambda N\xi'(1)/2}\mathbb{E} e^{\lambda S}\le
\exp\{\lambda N\xi'(1)/2+\lambda\sqrt{2K_\xi/\pi}N+\lambda^2N\xi(1)/2\}$. For $\lambda<0$ use
$M_N\ge Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}$.

\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-d1} First let $\zeta$ have finitely many atoms, and put $u=\Phi_\zeta$,
$w=\Phi^{(D)}_\zeta$ and $\delta=u-w$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}, applied with $\xi$ and with
$\xi_{\le D}$ and $G=1$, both functions are of class $C^{1,2}$ on each closed step of $\bar{\zeta}$,
with $|u_x|,|w_x|<1$ and $0\le u_{xx},w_{xx}\le1$. Subtracting the two Parisi equations and using
$u_x^2-w_x^2=(u_x+w_x)\delta_x$,
\[
 \partial_t\delta+\frac{\xi_{\le D}''}2\Bigl(\delta_{xx}+\bar{\zeta}\,(u_x+w_x)\,\delta_x\Bigr)
 =-\frac{\xi_{>D}''}2\bigl(u_{xx}+\bar{\zeta}\,u_x^2\bigr).
\]
Fix $(q,b)$ and let $X$ solve $dX_r=\frac12\xi_{\le D}''(r)\bar{\zeta}(r)(u_x+w_x)(r,X_r)\,dr+
\sqrt{\xi_{\le D}''(r)}\,dB_r$ on $[q,1]$ with $X_q=b$; the drift is bounded and Lipschitz in the
space variable. It\^o's formula on each closed step, chained over the steps as in the proof of
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-ac}, and $\delta(1,\cdot)=0$ give
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gauss-delta}
 \delta(q,b)=\frac12\,\mathbb{E}\int_q^1\xi_{>D}''(r)\bigl(u_{xx}+\bar{\zeta}\,u_x^2\bigr)(r,X_r)\,dr ;
\end{equation}
the stochastic integral is a martingale because $|\delta_x|\le2$. Since
$0\le u_{xx}+\bar{\zeta} u_x^2\le2$, we get $0\le\delta(q,b)\le\int_q^1\xi''_{>D}\le\xi'_{>D}(1)$.
For general $\zeta$, approximate $\bar{\zeta}$ in $L^1$ by distribution functions of measures with
finitely many atoms; $\Phi_\zeta$ and $\Phi^{(D)}_\zeta$ are the uniform limits
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-i}), and the bound passes to the limit.

The conjugates then satisfy $|\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q,m)-\Phi^{*,(D)}_\zeta(q,m)|\le\xi'_{>D}(1)$ for
$|m|<1$, and for $m=\pm1$ by continuity. The integral terms differ by
$\frac12\int_q^1t\xi''_{>D}(t)\bar{\zeta}(t)\,dt\le\frac12\vartheta_{>D}(1)\le\frac12\xi'_{>D}(1)$, where
$\vartheta_{>D}(1)=\xi'_{>D}(1)-\xi_{>D}(1)$. Hence, for every $\zeta$, $|P_\zeta-P^{(D)}_\zeta|$ and,
for every $x\in[-1,1]^N$, $N^{-1}\bigl|(F_\zeta(x)-H_N(x))-(F^{(D)}_\zeta(x)-H_N^{\le D}(x))\bigr|$
are at most $\frac32\xi'_{>D}(1)$. Taking infima over $\zeta$, over all of $\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ or over
$\{\zeta(\{0\})\ge\theta\}$, gives the bounds on $f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, on $\Lambda=\theta p(\theta)$ and, since
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)-H_N(x)=N(\mathrm{TAP}(\mu_x)-\log2)$, on $\mathrm{TAP}$ at every empirical law. The last
bound extends to every $\mu\in\mathcal{P}([-1,1])$, because the same computation applies to the
infimum over $\zeta$ in \cite[(2.24)--(2.25)]{CPS} at any $\mu$. Finally
$|H_N-H_N^{\le D}|\le T_D$ on $[-1,1]^N$ gives $e^{-T_D}Z_N^{(D)}\leZ_N\le e^{T_D}Z_N^{(D)}$ and the
bounds on $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$ and $M_N$.

\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-d2} If $\xi_{>D}\not\equiv0$, Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-field} applies to the
covariance $\xi_{>D}$, whose radius of convergence is at least that of $\xi$, and to the fields
$\pmH_N^{>D}$. Both suprema are nonnegative since $H_N^{>D}(0)=0$, so
$\mathbb{E} T_D\le\mathbb{E}\supH_N^{>D}+\mathbb{E}\sup(-H_N^{>D})\le\varepsilon_DN$. The variable $T_D$ is the supremum
of the process $(x,s)\mapsto sH_N^{>D}(x)$ on $[-1,1]^N\times\{-1,1\}$, whose variance is at most
$N\xi_{>D}(1)$, and \eqref{eq:gauss-conc} gives the tail bound.

\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-d3} By~\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-d1}, $Z_N^\theta\le(Z_N^{(D)})^\theta e^{\theta
T_D}$, and $T_D$ is independent of $Z_N^{(D)}$. So \eqref{eq:gauss-conc}
and~\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-d2} give $\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le\mathbb{E}(Z_N^{(D)})^\theta\,e^{\theta\varepsilon_DN
+\theta^2N\xi_{>D}(1)/2}$. Similarly $\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ge\mathbb{E}(Z_N^{(D)})^\theta\,\mathbb{E} e^{-\theta T_D}
\ge\mathbb{E}(Z_N^{(D)})^\theta\,e^{-\theta\varepsilon_DN}$ by Jensen's inequality.

\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-e} By the Cauchy--Schwarz inequality and~\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-a},
$\mathbb{Q}_\theta(A)=\mathbb{E}[Z_N^\theta\mathbf{1}_A]/\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le(\mathbb{E}Z_N^{2\theta})^{1/2}\mathbb{P}(A)^{1/2}$.

For the last assertion, compare the exponents in~\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-a}
and~\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-c} (with $\lambda=2\theta$) with $C(\xi,\theta)$, using
$C^{\max}_\xi\ge\sqrt{2K_\xi/\pi}$.
<!-- end proof-49 -->
<!-- proof-50: body_md -->
Fix $c,t>0$ and $L\ge1$.

\emph{Choice of $D$.} Choose $D$, at least the smallest active degree, with
\[
 2\varepsilon_D+\tfrac32\xi'_{>D}(1)\le t/4\qquad\text{and}\qquad
 (t/8)^2\ge2(c+1)\,\xi_{>D}(1).
\]
This is possible because $\varepsilon_D$, $\xi'_{>D}(1)$ and $\xi_{>D}(1)$ tend to zero. The
choice depends only on $\xi$, $c$ and $t$.

\emph{The truncated band theorem.} Apply the polynomial case to $\xi_{\le D}$, with rate $c+1$,
accuracy $t/2$ and the given $L$. This gives $\varepsilon,\delta>0$ and $n$ with $n\ge L$ and
$n\ge L/\min(\varepsilon,\delta)$ such that, for all large $N$, the event
\[
 \Omega^{(D)}=\Bigl\{\bigl|F^{\mathrm{band},(D)}_n(m;\varepsilon,\delta)-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}^{(D)}(m)\bigr|
 <tN/2\ \text{for every } m\in[-1,1]^N\Bigr\}
\]
has a complement of outer probability at most $e^{-(c+1)N}$. Here $F^{\mathrm{band},(D)}_n$ is
\eqref{eq:max-band} with $H_N^{\le D}$ in place of $H_N$.

\emph{The remainder.} Let $\Omega'=\{T_D\le(\varepsilon_D+t/8)N\}$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-bounds}\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-d2} with $u=t/8$ and the choice of $D$,
$\mathbb{P}((\Omega')^c)\le e^{-(c+1)N}$.

\emph{Comparison.} On $\Omega^{(D)}\cap\Omega'$, fix $m\in[-1,1]^N$. Since
$F^{\mathrm{band},(D)}_n(m)>F_{\mathrm{TAP}}^{(D)}(m)-tN/2>-\infty$, the band $B_n(m,\varepsilon,\delta)$ is nonempty. The band
does not depend on the field, and for every $(\sigma^1,\dots,\sigma^n)$ in it the exponents
$\sum_{i\le n}H_N(\sigma^i)$ and $\sum_{i\le n}H_N^{\le D}(\sigma^i)$ differ by at most $nT_D$; by
\eqref{eq:max-band}, $|F^{\mathrm{band}}_n(m)-F^{\mathrm{band},(D)}_n(m)|\le T_D$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-bounds}\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-d1},
$|F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}^{(D)}(m)|\le T_D+\frac32N\xi'_{>D}(1)$. Therefore
\[
 \bigl|F^{\mathrm{band}}_n(m)-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(m)\bigr|<\frac{tN}2+2T_D+\frac32N\xi'_{>D}(1)
 \le\frac{tN}2+\frac{tN}4+\Bigl(2\varepsilon_D+\frac32\xi'_{>D}(1)\Bigr)N\le tN .
\]
So the event in \eqref{eq:max-band-thm} is contained in $(\Omega^{(D)})^c\cup(\Omega')^c$, whose
outer probability is at most $2e^{-(c+1)N}\le e^{-cN}$ for $N\ge\log2$.
<!-- end proof-50 -->
<!-- lemma-31: body_md -->
\label{lem:gauss-interior}
\leavevmode
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:gauss-interior-a} Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. Almost surely, for every $N$, $H_N$ is continuously
 differentiable on a neighbourhood of $[-1,1]^N$, $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$ is continuous on $[-1,1]^N$, and $M_N$ is
 attained. In particular $M_N$ is a random variable.
\item\label{lem:gauss-interior-b} Assume $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$. Fix $N$ and a realization in which $H_N$ is
 continuously differentiable on a neighbourhood of $[-1,1]^N$. Let
 $\gamma(b)=\mathbb{E}\tanh(b+\sqrt{\xi'(1)}\,|Z|)$, with $Z$ standard Gaussian, which is an increasing
 bijection of $\mathbb{R}$ onto $(-1,1)$, and put $\psi_\xi(m)=\gamma^{-1}(m)-\xi''(1)$ for $m\in(-1,1)$,
 so that $\psi_\xi$ is increasing and $\psi_\xi(m)\to\infty$ as $m\uparrow1$. If $x\in[-1,1]^N$ has
 $x_i=1$ and $y=x-se_i$ with $s\in(0,1)$, then
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:gauss-push}
  F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(y)-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ \ge\ s\Bigl[\psi_\xi(1-s)-3\xi''(1)-\sup_{[-1,1]^N}|\partial_iH_N|\Bigr],
 \end{equation}
 and the same holds if $x_i=-1$ and $y=x+se_i$. Consequently every maximizer of $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$ lies in
 $(-1,1)^N$.
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end lemma-31 -->
<!-- proof-51: body_md -->
\ref{lem:gauss-interior-a} The first assertion is Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-field}\ref{lem:gauss-field-a},
for each $N$ outside a null set. By Section~\ref{sec:intro-setting},
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)=H_N(x)+N\mathrm{TAP}(\mu_x)-N\log2$. The functional $\mathrm{TAP}(\mu)$ depends on $\mu$ only
through the law of $|m|$ under $\mu$, because $\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q,\cdot)$ is even, and $m\mapsto|m|$
does not increase $W_1$. For a polynomial covariance, $\mathrm{TAP}$ is therefore $W_1$-continuous on
$\mathcal{P}([-1,1])$ by \cite[Theorem~12(ii)]{CPS}. Under \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}, $\mathrm{TAP}$ is the uniform limit of
$\mathrm{TAP}^{(D)}$ as $D\to\infty$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-bounds}\ref{lem:gauss-bounds-d1}, hence
continuous. Since $W_1(\mu_x,\mu_y)\le N^{-1}\sum_i|x_i-y_i|$, the map $x\mapstoF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)$ is
continuous on the compact set $[-1,1]^N$, so its maximum is attained and equals its supremum over a
countable dense subset.

\ref{lem:gauss-interior-b} \emph{Step 1: a lower bound on the inverse field.} Let
$\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$, $q\in[0,1]$ and $b\in\mathbb{R}$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-ac}\ref{lem:pde-ac-a} for measures with finitely many atoms, and by
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-measurable}\ref{lem:pde-measurable-i}--\ref{lem:pde-measurable-ii} in general,
$\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(q,b)=\mathbb{E}\tanh(X_1)$, where $X$ solves
$dX_r=\xi''(r)\bar{\zeta}(r)\,\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(r,X_r)\,dr+\sqrt{\xi''(r)}\,dB_r$ on $[q,1]$ with
$X_q=b$. Since $0\le\bar{\zeta}\le1$ and $|\partial_x\Phi_\zeta|\le1$, the drift is at most
$\xi''(r)\le\xi''(1)$ on an interval of length at most one, so $X_1\le b+\xi''(1)+W$ with
$W=\int_q^1\sqrt{\xi''(r)}\,dB_r$ centered Gaussian of variance $\xi'(1)-\xi'(q)\le\xi'(1)$. Since
$\tanh$ is increasing, $\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(q,b)\le\mathbb{E}\tanh(b+\xi''(1)+|W|)\le\gamma(b+\xi''(1))$.
Applied at $b=b_\zeta(q,m)$ this gives $m\le\gamma(b_\zeta(q,m)+\xi''(1))$, that is,
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gauss-inverse-lower}
 b_\zeta(q,m)\ge\psi_\xi(m)\qquad\text{for all } \zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1]),\ q\in[0,1],\ m\in(-1,1).
\end{equation}

\emph{Step 2: Lipschitz dependence on the self-overlap.} For $\zeta$ with finitely many atoms,
$\Phi_\zeta$ is continuous in $t$ and solves the Parisi equation on each closed step
(Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-class}\ref{lem:pde-class-b}), with
$|\partial_t\Phi_\zeta|=\frac{\xi''}2|\partial_x^2\Phi_\zeta+\bar{\zeta}(\partial_x\Phi_\zeta)^2|\le
\xi''(1)$. By uniform approximation, $|\Phi_\zeta(q,b)-\Phi_\zeta(q',b)|\le\xi''(1)|q-q'|$ for every
$\zeta$. Taking infima, $|\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q,m)-\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q',m)|\le\xi''(1)|q-q'|$ for
$|m|<1$, and for $m=\pm1$ by continuity.

\emph{Step 3: moving a coordinate inward.} Let $x_i=1$, $y=x-se_i$ and $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$.
The function $\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q,\cdot)$ is concave and continuous on $[-1,1]$, and for
$m,m'\in(-1,1)$,
$\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q,m')\le\Phi_\zeta(q,b_\zeta(q,m))-m'b_\zeta(q,m)=\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q,m)-(m'-m)\,
b_\zeta(q,m)$. So $-b_\zeta(q,m)$ is a supergradient at $m$, and since $b_\zeta(q,\cdot)$ is
continuous, $\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q,\cdot)$ is continuously differentiable on $(-1,1)$ with derivative
$-b_\zeta(q,\cdot)$ (compare \cite[(2.21)--(2.23)]{CPS}). By \eqref{eq:gauss-inverse-lower} and the
monotonicity of $\psi_\xi$, with an improper integral at $m=1$,
\[
 G_\zeta(q_y,y)-G_\zeta(q_y,x)=\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q_y,1-s)-\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q_y,1)
 =\int_{1-s}^1b_\zeta(q_y,m)\,dm\ge s\,\psi_\xi(1-s).
\]
Next, $|q_y-q_x|=(2s-s^2)/N\le2s/N$, and Step~2 together with $t\,\xi''(t)\bar{\zeta}(t)\le\xi''(1)$
gives $|G_\zeta(q_y,x)-G_\zeta(q_x,x)|\le\frac32N\xi''(1)|q_y-q_x|\le3\xi''(1)s$. Finally
$H_N(y)-H_N(x)\ge-s\sup_{[-1,1]^N}|\partial_iH_N|$. Adding the three bounds,
\[
 F_\zeta(y)-F_\zeta(x)\ge s\Bigl[\psi_\xi(1-s)-3\xi''(1)-\sup_{[-1,1]^N}|\partial_iH_N|\Bigr]
 \qquad\text{for every } \zeta .
\]
Since $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\le F_\zeta(x)$ for every $\zeta$, $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(y)-F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge\inf_\zeta(F_\zeta(y)-
F_\zeta(x))$, which proves \eqref{eq:gauss-push}. The case $x_i=-1$ is the same, because
$\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q,\cdot)$ is even. The supremum of $|\partial_iH_N|$ is finite and
$\psi_\xi(1-s)\to\infty$ as $s\downarrow0$, so the right side of \eqref{eq:gauss-push} is positive
for small $s$, and $x$ is not a maximizer.
<!-- end proof-51 -->
<!-- lemma-32: body_md -->
\label{lem:gauss-critical}
Assume $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$. Fix $N$ and a realization in which $H_N$ is continuously differentiable on a
neighbourhood of $[-1,1]^N$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:gauss-critical-a} For every $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ the function $F_\zeta$ is
 continuously differentiable on $(-1,1)^N$, with
 \begin{equation}\label{eq:gauss-gradient}
  \partial_iF_\zeta(y)=\partial_iH_N(y)-b_\zeta(q_y,y_i)
  -y_i\,\xi''(q_y)\,\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^Nu_\zeta(q_y,y_j),\qquad y\in(-1,1)^N .
 \end{equation}
\item\label{lem:gauss-critical-b} Let $x\in(-1,1)^N$, and let $\zeta_x$ be the unique minimizer of
 $\mu\mapsto F_\mu(x)$ over $\mathcal{P}([q_x,1])$ \cite[Theorem~12(iii) and Section~11]{CPS}. For every
 $v\in\mathbb{R}^N$, the function $t\mapstoF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x+tv)$ is differentiable at $t=0$, with derivative
 $\nabla F_{\zeta_x}(x)\cdot v$.
\item\label{lem:gauss-critical-c} If $x\in(-1,1)^N$ is a local maximizer of $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$, then
 $\nabla F_{\zeta_x}(x)=0$ and $F_{\zeta_x}(x)=F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)$.
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end lemma-32 -->
<!-- proof-52: body_md -->
\emph{Minimizers in $h$.} By Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-b}, for
$m\in(-1,1)$ the function $b\mapsto\Phi_\zeta(q,b)-mb$ is strictly convex with critical point
$b_\zeta(q,m)$. Hence, for fixed $\zeta$, the unique minimizer of $f_y(t;\zeta,\cdot)$ is
$h_t=(b_\zeta(q_t,y_i+tv_i))_{i\le N}$, which is continuous in $t$ because $b_\zeta$ is jointly
continuous on $[0,1]\times(-1,1)$.

\emph{One-sided derivatives.} For fixed $(\zeta,h)$, the right and left derivatives in $q$ of
$q\mapsto\sum_i\Phi_\zeta(q,h_i)-\frac N2\int_q^1s\xi''(s)\bar{\zeta}(s)\,ds$ are computed in
\cite[Section~11]{CPS} from the Parisi equation:
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gauss-qderiv}
 -\frac{\xi''(q)}2\sum_{i=1}^N\partial_x^2\Phi_\zeta(q,h_i)
 +\frac{\xi''(q)}2\,\bar{\zeta}^{\pm}(q)\Bigl(Nq-\sum_{i=1}^N\bigl(\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(q,h_i)\bigr)^2\Bigr),
\end{equation}
where $\bar{\zeta}^+(q)=\zeta([0,q])=\bar{\zeta}(q)$ and $\bar{\zeta}^-(q)=\zeta([0,q))$. Since
$t\mapsto q_t$ is smooth, with $\frac{d}{dt}q_t=2(y+tv)\cdot v/N$, and $q\mapsto\Phi_\zeta(q,b)$ is
Lipschitz (Step~2 of the previous proof), $f_y(\cdot;\zeta,h)$ has right and left derivatives in $t$: the chain rule applies
with the one-sided $q$-derivative \eqref{eq:gauss-qderiv} taken on the side toward which $q_t$
moves, and the term $-\sum_iv_ih_i$ is added. The only factor that may be discontinuous is
$\bar{\zeta}^{\pm}(q)$, and it multiplies $Nq-\sum_i(\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(q,h_i))^2$. At $(t,h)=(0,h_0)$,
where $h_{0,i}=b_\zeta(q_y,y_i)$ and hence $\partial_x\Phi_\zeta(q_y,h_{0,i})=y_i$, this factor
equals $Nq_y-|y|^2=0$ \cite[(11.9)]{CPS}. As $\partial_x\Phi_\zeta$ and $\partial_x^2\Phi_\zeta$ are
continuous on $[0,1]\times\mathbb{R}$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-a}), both
one-sided $t$-derivatives of $f_y(\cdot;\zeta,\cdot)$ are therefore continuous at $(0,h_0)$, as
functions of $(t,h)$, with the common value
\begin{equation}\label{eq:gauss-common}
 \sum_{i=1}^Nv_i\Bigl[-b_\zeta(q_y,y_i)-y_i\,\xi''(q_y)\,\frac1N\sum_{j=1}^Nu_\zeta(q_y,y_j)\Bigr].
\end{equation}

\ref{lem:gauss-critical-a} The envelope lemma \cite[Lemma~37]{CPS}, applied on the metric space
$\mathbb{R}^N$ to $f_y(\cdot;\zeta,\cdot)$ and its minimizers $h_t$, for right and for left derivatives,
shows that $t\mapsto\inf_hf_y(t;\zeta,h)$ is differentiable at $t=0$ with derivative
\eqref{eq:gauss-common}. Adding $\nablaH_N(y)\cdot v$, every directional derivative of $F_\zeta$
at $y$ exists and is the linear form in $v$ given by \eqref{eq:gauss-gradient}. The right side of
\eqref{eq:gauss-gradient} is continuous on $(-1,1)^N$, because $b_\zeta$ and $u_\zeta$ are jointly
continuous on $[0,1]\times(-1,1)$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing}\ref{lem:pde-standing-b}). A function
whose partial derivatives exist and are continuous on an open set is continuously differentiable
there.

\ref{lem:gauss-critical-b} Let $y=x$. In \cite[Section~11]{CPS} it is shown that the minimizer
$(\zeta_{x+tv},h_{x+tv})$ of $f_x(t;\cdot,\cdot)$ over $\mathcal{P}([0,1])\times\mathbb{R}^N$, normalized by
$\zeta([0,q_t))=0$, is unique and continuous at $t=0$, and that the one-sided $t$-derivatives of
$f_x$ are continuous at $(0,(\zeta_x,h_x))$ jointly in $(t,\zeta,h)$, by the cancellation just
described; here $h_{x,i}=b_{\zeta_x}(q_x,x_i)$. The envelope lemma \cite[Lemma~37]{CPS} on
$\mathcal{P}([0,1])\times\mathbb{R}^N$ then shows that $t\mapstoF_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x+tv)-H_N(x+tv)$ has right and left
derivatives at $t=0$ equal to those of $f_x(\cdot;\zeta_x,\cdot)$ at $(0,h_x)$. By the proof
of~\ref{lem:gauss-critical-a} with $\zeta=\zeta_x$, both equal \eqref{eq:gauss-common}, which is the
derivative of $F_{\zeta_x}(x+tv)-H_N(x+tv)$ at $t=0$.

\ref{lem:gauss-critical-c} At a local maximizer in the open cube, the derivative in~\ref{lem:gauss-critical-b}
vanishes for every $v$. So $\nabla F_{\zeta_x}(x)=0$, and $F_{\zeta_x}(x)=F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)$ by the choice of
$\zeta_x$.
<!-- end proof-52 -->
<!-- proof-53: body_md -->
Let $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-interior}\ref{lem:gauss-interior-a}, there is an event
of probability one on which, for every $N$, $H_N$ is continuously differentiable on a neighbourhood
of $[-1,1]^N$, $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$ is continuous and $M_N$ is attained. Fix a realization in this event and a
maximizer $x^*$. By Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-interior}\ref{lem:gauss-interior-b}, $x^*\in(-1,1)^N$. With
$\zeta^*=\zeta_{x^*}$, Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-critical} shows that $F_{\zeta^*}$ is continuously
differentiable on $(-1,1)^N$, that $\nabla F_{\zeta^*}(x^*)=0$, and that
$F_{\zeta^*}(x^*)=F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x^*)=M_N$.
<!-- end proof-53 -->
<!-- remark-16: body_md -->
\label{rem:gauss-tap}
By \cite[(11.12)]{CPS}, at the minimizing order parameter the factor
$\xi''(q_x)N^{-1}\sum_ju_{\zeta_x}(q_x,x_j)$ in the last term of \eqref{eq:gauss-gradient}
equals $\xi''(q_x)\int_{q_x}^1\zeta_x([0,s])\,ds$, so
\eqref{eq:gauss-gradient} at $(x,\zeta_x)$ is the gradient formula \cite[Theorem~5]{CPS} and
$\nabla F_{\zeta^*}(x^*)=0$ are the generalized TAP equations \cite[Remark~6]{CPS}.
Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-critical} does not use this: away from $x$, the gradient of $F_{\zeta_x}$
keeps the empirical average.
<!-- end remark-16 -->
<!-- proposition-11: body_md -->
\label{prop:var-tail}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ and $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$. Let $I(f)=-\Sigma(f)$ for $f\gef_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and $I(f)=+\infty$ for
$f<f_{\mathrm{eq}}$.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{prop:var-tail-a} For every $\theta\in[0,1]$,
 $\lim_N N^{-1}\log\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}=\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)$.
\item\label{prop:var-tail-b} For every $f\in\mathbb{R}$,
 $\limsup_N N^{-1}\log\mathbb{P}(M_N\ge Nf)\le\Sigma(f)$, and for every $f<f_1$,
 \[
  \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(M_N\ge Nf\bigr)=\Sigma(f).
 \]
\item\label{prop:var-tail-c} For every closed set $A\subset\mathbb{R}$ and every open set $U\subset\mathbb{R}$,
 \[
  \limsup_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(N^{-1}M_N\in A\bigr)\le-\inf_AI,\qquad
  \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(N^{-1}M_N\in U\bigr)\ge-\inf_{U\cap(-\infty,f_1)}I .
 \]
\item\label{prop:var-tail-d} $M_N\ge Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}$, and for every $\delta>0$ there is $c_\delta>0$ such
 that $\mathbb{P}(M_N\ge N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta))\le e^{-c_\delta N}$ for all large $N$.
\item\label{prop:var-tail-e} For every $N\ge1$ and $f\in\mathbb{R}$,
 $\mathbb{P}(\logZ_N\ge Nf)\le e^{N\Sigma(f)}$, and for every $f<f_1$,
 \[
  \lim_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(N^{-1}\logZ_N\ge f\bigr)=\Sigma(f).
 \]
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end proposition-11 -->
<!-- proof-54: body_md -->
\ref{prop:var-tail-a} For $\theta\in(0,1)$ this is Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-c}
and~\ref{thm:exist-e}, and for $\theta=1$ it is the last assertion of
Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-c}, since $\overline{\Lambda}(1)=\xi(1)/2$. For $\theta=0$ both sides
vanish.

\ref{prop:var-tail-b} Markov's inequality gives
$\mathbb{P}(M_N\ge Nf)\le e^{-\theta Nf}\mathbb{E} e^{\thetaM_N}$ for $\theta\in[0,1]$, so
by~\ref{prop:var-tail-a} the upper limit is at most $\overline{\Lambda}(\theta)-\theta f$; the infimum over
$\theta\in[0,1]$ is $\Sigma(f)$. For the lower bound, let $f<f_1$. If $f\lef_{\mathrm{eq}}$, then
$\mathbb{P}(M_N\ge Nf)=1$ by~\eqref{eq:max-crude-M} and $\Sigma(f)=0$. Let $f_{\mathrm{eq}}<f<f_1$ and
$0<\varepsilon<(f_1-f)/2$, and put $f'=f+\varepsilon\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$. Since
$\{|N^{-1}M_N-f'|\le\varepsilon\}\subset\{M_N\ge Nf\}$, and since the lower limit in
Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-d} is nondecreasing in the window and tends to $\Sigma(f')$
as the window shrinks,
\[
 \liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(M_N\ge Nf\bigr)
 \ge\liminf_{N\to\infty}\frac1N\log\mathbb{P}\bigl(|N^{-1}M_N-f'|\le\varepsilon\bigr)
 \ge\Sigma(f+\varepsilon).
\]
Let $\varepsilon\downarrow0$ and use the continuity of $\Sigma$.

\ref{prop:var-tail-c} By Proposition~\ref{prop:var-regular}\ref{prop:var-regular-c}, $I$ is
nondecreasing on $[f_{\mathrm{eq}},\infty)$ and infinite below $f_{\mathrm{eq}}$. Let $A$ be closed. If $A$ does not
meet $[f_{\mathrm{eq}},\infty)$, then $\mathbb{P}(N^{-1}M_N\in A)=0$ by~\eqref{eq:max-crude-M}. Otherwise let $a$
be the least point of $A\cap[f_{\mathrm{eq}},\infty)$. Then $\{N^{-1}M_N\in A\}\subset\{M_N\ge Na\}$ almost
surely, and~\ref{prop:var-tail-b} gives the upper limit $\Sigma(a)=-I(a)=-\inf_AI$. Let $U$ be
open and $f\in U\cap[f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$, and choose $\delta>0$ with $(f-\delta,f+\delta)\subset U$. Then
\[
 \mathbb{P}\bigl(N^{-1}M_N\in U\bigr)\ge\mathbb{P}\bigl(M_N\ge Nf\bigr)-\mathbb{P}\bigl(M_N\ge N(f+\delta)\bigr).
\]
By Proposition~\ref{prop:var-regular}\ref{prop:var-regular-c}, $\Sigma(f+\delta)<\Sigma(f)$; fix
$\gamma>0$ with $3\gamma<\Sigma(f)-\Sigma(f+\delta)$. By~\ref{prop:var-tail-b}, for all large $N$
the first probability is at least $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-\gamma)}$, and the second is at most
$e^{N(\Sigma(f+\delta)+\gamma)}\le\frac12e^{N(\Sigma(f)-\gamma)}$. So the lower limit is at least
$\Sigma(f)-\gamma=-I(f)-\gamma$. Let $\gamma\downarrow0$ and take the supremum over
$f\in U\cap[f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$; the points of $U$ below $f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ have $I=+\infty$.

\ref{prop:var-tail-d} The first claim is~\eqref{eq:max-crude-M}. By
Proposition~\ref{prop:var-regular}\ref{prop:var-regular-c}, $\Sigma(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)<0$, and
\ref{prop:var-tail-b} gives the claim with $c_\delta=-\Sigma(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+\delta)/2$.

\ref{prop:var-tail-e} Let $\theta\in(0,1)$ and $\alpha\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$ with
$\alpha(\{0\})\ge\theta$. Guerra's bound, $(N\theta)^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le P_\alpha$ for every
$N$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:moments-guerra}; \cite[Theorem~6.1]{Tal07}), and Markov's inequality give
$\mathbb{P}(\logZ_N\ge Nf)\le e^{-\theta Nf}\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le e^{N\theta(P_\alpha-f)}$. Taking the
infimum over $\alpha$ gives $e^{N(\Lambda(\theta)-\theta f)}$, and $\theta=0$ gives the trivial
bound $1$. The infimum of $\Lambda(\theta)-\theta f$ over $\theta\in[0,1)$ equals $\Sigma(f)$,
because $\Lambda(\theta)\to\overline{\Lambda}(1)$ as $\theta\uparrow1$ (Lemma~\ref{lem:var-dual}). This
proves the bound for every $N$, and hence the upper half of the limit. For the lower half, let
$f<f_1$, $0<t<f_1-f$ and $\gamma>0$. Then
\[
 \mathbb{P}\bigl(\logZ_N\ge Nf\bigr)\ge\mathbb{P}\bigl(M_N\ge N(f+t)\bigr)
 -\mathbb{P}\bigl(M_N-\logZ_N>tN\bigr).
\]
By~\ref{prop:var-tail-b} the first term is at least $e^{N(\Sigma(f+t)-\gamma)}$ for all large $N$,
and by Theorem~\ref{thm:max}\ref{thm:max-a} the second is at most $e^{N(\Sigma(f+t)-\gamma-1)}$
for all large $N$. Hence the lower limit is at least $\Sigma(f+t)-\gamma$. Let $\gamma\downarrow0$
and $t\downarrow0$.
<!-- end proof-54 -->
<!-- remark-17: body_md -->
\label{rem:var-tail}\label{rem:max-subsumed}
The limit in~\ref{prop:var-tail-e} follows from \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ and is not new where \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ is known;
the bound for every $N$ is Guerra's. For even $\xi$, \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\ is Talagrand's
\cite[Section~7]{Tal07}, and for $\xi$ finite on $\mathbb{R}$ it is stated in \cite[Theorem~2.1]{CGKLM};
Boursier notes that it makes $-\Sigma$ the upper-tail rate function of $N^{-1}\logZ_N$
\cite[Remark~1.3]{Bou26b} and, ``with a little more work'', gives a large deviation principle on
$[f_{\mathrm{eq}},\infty)$ with rate function $-\Sigma$, the Legendre transform of $\overline{\Lambda}$
\cite[Section~1.4]{Bou26a}. The upper bound in~\ref{prop:var-tail-b} is hers
\cite[Section~2.2]{Bou26b}; through TAP states she proves the lower half of~\ref{prop:var-tail-e}
at regular levels whose first positive contact is strictly Plefka stable \cite[Remark~1.4 and
Proposition~3.12]{Bou26b}. Here it holds at every level below $f_1$, whatever the stability of
the contacts; Theorem~\ref{thm:max} transfers every speed-$N$ statement about $N^{-1}\logZ_N$
to $N^{-1}M_N$ and, through Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-a}, its local rates at levels
of $(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$ to the existence event. We do not claim a full large deviation principle for the
free energy: the open-set lower bound in~\ref{prop:var-tail-c} stops at $f_1$, and \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}\
enters only through Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-e}.
<!-- end remark-17 -->
<!-- proposition-12: body_md -->
\label{rem:max-overlap}
\leavevmode
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{rem:max-overlap-a} Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. For every $f>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ and $c>0$ there is
 $\kappa\in(0,1]$ such that, for every $N$,
 \[
  \mathbb{P}\bigl(\exists x\in[-1,1]^N:\ q_x\le\kappa,\ F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge Nf\bigr)\le e^{-cN};
 \]
 any $\kappa$ with $\vartheta(\kappa)/2+\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}<(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})/2$ and $(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})^2\ge8c\,\xi(\kappa)$
 works.
\item\label{rem:max-overlap-b} Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}, and let $\theta,t>0$ with $f_{\mathrm{eq}}+t<\ell_\theta$.
 There are $\kappa,c'>0$ such that, for all large $N$,
 \[
  \mathbb{Q}_\theta\bigl(\exists x\in[-1,1]^N:\ q_x\le\kappa,\ F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge\logZ_N-tN\bigr)\le e^{-c'N}.
 \]
 Together with Corollary~\ref{cor:max-tilt}: with $\mathbb{Q}_\theta$-probability at least $1-2e^{-c'N}$, the
 set $\{x:F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge\logZ_N-tN\}$ contains every maximizer of $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}$ and lies in
 $\{q_x>\kappa\}$. If moreover $\theta\in(\theta_*,1)$ and $\mathrm{FM}^{\ge}(\xi,\theta)$ holds,
 then $\ell_\theta\ge p(\theta)>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$.
\item\label{rem:max-overlap-c} Assume $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$ and \hyperref[hyp:FM]{\textup{(FM)}}, and let $f\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}},f_1)$,
 $\varepsilon\in(0,(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})/4)$ and $c>0$. There is $\kappa>0$ such that, for all large $N$,
 \[
  \mathbb{P}\Bigl(\exists x\in[-1,1]^N:\ q_x\le\kappa,\ F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\geM_N-\varepsilon N\ \Bigm|\
  |N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon\Bigr)\le e^{-cN}.
 \]
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end proposition-12 -->
<!-- lemma-33: body_md -->
\label{lem:var-small}
Assume \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}.
\begin{thmlist}
\item\label{lem:var-small-a} For every $N$ and every $x\in[-1,1]^N$,
 \[
  F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\leH_N(x)+Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}+\frac N2\,\vartheta(q_x).
 \]
\item\label{lem:var-small-b} For every $\kappa\in(0,1]$ and $u>0$,
 \[
  \mathbb{P}\Bigl(\sup\bigl\{H_N(x):\ x\in[-1,1]^N,\ q_x\le\kappa\bigr\}>N\bigl(\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}+u\bigr)\Bigr)
  \le\exp\Bigl(-\frac{u^2N}{2\xi(\kappa)}\Bigr).
 \]
\end{thmlist}
<!-- end lemma-33 -->
<!-- proof-55: body_md -->
\ref{lem:var-small-a} Let $q=q_x$ and $\zeta\in\mathcal{P}([0,1])$. By~\eqref{eq:intro-ftap},
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\le F_\zeta(x)$. Three bounds compare $F_\zeta(x)$ with $NP_\zeta$.
\begin{steplist}
\item $\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q,a)\le\Phi_\zeta(q,0)$ for every $a\in[-1,1]$: take $b=0$ in the infimum
 that defines $\Phi^{*}_\zeta(q,a)$ for $|a|<1$, and pass to the continuous extension at $a=\pm1$.
\item $\Phi_\zeta(q,0)\le\Phi_\zeta(0,0)$. When $\zeta$ has finitely many atoms,
 $\Phi_\zeta(t,\cdot)$ is convex and
 $\partial_t\Phi_\zeta=-\frac{\xi''}2(\partial_x^2\Phi_\zeta+\zeta([0,t])(\partial_x\Phi_\zeta)^2)\le0$
 on each step of the Cole--Hopf recursion, so $t\mapsto\Phi_\zeta(t,0)$ is nonincreasing; this
 passes to general $\zeta$ by the uniform continuity of $\zeta\mapsto\Phi_\zeta$
 \cite[Lemma~14]{JT16}.
\item Since $\zeta([0,t])\le1$ and $\int_0^qt\xi''(t)\,dt=\vartheta(q)$,
 $\int_q^1t\xi''(t)\zeta([0,t])\,dt\ge\int_0^1t\xi''(t)\zeta([0,t])\,dt-\vartheta(q)$.
\end{steplist}
Together, $F_\zeta(x)\leH_N(x)+NP_\zeta+\frac N2\vartheta(q)$. Take the infimum over $\zeta$.

\ref{lem:var-small-b} The set $S_\kappa=\{x\in[-1,1]^N:q_x\le\kappa\}$ is compact and $H_N$ is
almost surely continuous, so the supremum is a supremum over a countable dense subset, and its law
depends only on the covariance of $H_N$. For $x,y\in[-1,1]^N$,
$\mathbb{E}(H_N(x)-H_N(y))^2\le K_\xi|x-y|^2$ by Lemma~\ref{lem:gauss-field}\ref{lem:gauss-field-b}. The
Sudakov--Fernique inequality, comparing with $\sqrt{K_\xi}\,g\cdot x$ for a standard Gaussian vector
$g$, gives
\[
 \mathbb{E}\sup_{S_\kappa}H_N\le\sqrt{K_\xi}\,\mathbb{E}\sup_{|x|\le\sqrt{\kappa N}}g\cdot x
 =\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa N}\,\mathbb{E}|g|\le\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}\,N .
\]
On $S_\kappa$ the variance of $H_N(x)$ is $N\xi(q_x)\le N\xi(\kappa)$, since $\xi$ is
nondecreasing on $[0,1]$. The Borell--TIS inequality~\eqref{eq:gauss-conc} with deviation $uN$
gives the claim.
<!-- end proof-55 -->
<!-- proof-56: body_md -->
\ref{rem:max-overlap-a} Let $u=(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})/2$ and let $\kappa\in(0,1]$ satisfy
$\vartheta(\kappa)/2+\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}<u$ and $u^2\ge2c\,\xi(\kappa)$; such $\kappa$ exist because
$\vartheta(\kappa)\le\kappa\xi'(1)$ and $\xi(\kappa)\le\kappa^2\xi(1)$. Outside the event of
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-small}\ref{lem:var-small-b}, which has probability at most
$e^{-u^2N/(2\xi(\kappa))}\le e^{-cN}$, every $x\in[-1,1]^N$ with $q_x\le\kappa$ satisfies, by
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-small}\ref{lem:var-small-a} and the monotonicity of $\vartheta$ on $[0,1]$,
\[
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\le N\bigl(\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}+u\bigr)+Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}+\frac N2\vartheta(\kappa)<N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+2u)=Nf .
\]
Both bounds hold for every $N$.

\ref{rem:max-overlap-b} Let $C=C(\xi,\theta)$ be the constant of~\eqref{eq:max-crude}, so that
$\mathbb{Q}_\theta(B)\le e^{2CN}\mathbb{P}(B)^{1/2}$ for every event $B$ (proof of Corollary~\ref{cor:max-tilt}). The
level $\ell_\theta$ is finite because $\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le(\mathbb{E}Z_N^{2\theta})^{1/2}\le e^{CN/2}$. Fix
$a\in(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+t,\ell_\theta)$, put $\gamma=(a-t-f_{\mathrm{eq}})/2>0$, and choose $\kappa\in(0,1]$ with
$\vartheta(\kappa)/2+\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}<\gamma$ and $\gamma^2\ge4(2C+1)\xi(\kappa)$. Consider
\[
 B_1=\{\logZ_N\ge Na\},\qquad
 B_2=\bigl\{\sup\{H_N(x):x\in[-1,1]^N,\ q_x\le\kappa\}\le N(\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}+\gamma)\bigr\}.
\]
For all large $N$, $(N\theta)^{-1}\log\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\ge(\ell_\theta+a)/2$, so
$\mathbb{Q}_\theta(B_1^c)\le e^{\theta Na}/\mathbb{E}Z_N^\theta\le e^{-\theta N(\ell_\theta-a)/2}$. By
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-small}\ref{lem:var-small-b},
$\mathbb{Q}_\theta(B_2^c)\le e^{2CN}e^{-\gamma^2N/(4\xi(\kappa))}\le e^{-N}$. On $B_1\cap B_2$, every $x$ with
$q_x\le\kappa$ satisfies, by Lemma~\ref{lem:var-small}\ref{lem:var-small-a},
\[
 F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\le N\bigl(\sqrt{K_\xi\kappa}+\gamma\bigr)+Nf_{\mathrm{eq}}+\frac N2\vartheta(\kappa)<N(f_{\mathrm{eq}}+2\gamma)
 =N(a-t)\le\logZ_N-tN .
\]
So the event of~\ref{rem:max-overlap-b} lies in $B_1^c\cup B_2^c$, whose $\mathbb{Q}_\theta$-probability is at
most $e^{-c'N}$ with $c'=\frac12\min\{\theta(\ell_\theta-a)/2,1\}$, for all large $N$. By
Corollary~\ref{cor:max-tilt}, $\mathbb{Q}_\theta(M_N<\logZ_N-tN)\le e^{-c'N}$ for all large $N$. Off both events,
the maximum $M_N$ is attained, every maximizer lies in $\{x:F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge\logZ_N-tN\}$, and this set
lies in $\{q_x>\kappa\}$. Finally, if $\theta\in(\theta_*,1)$ and $\mathrm{FM}^{\ge}(\xi,\theta)$
holds, then $\ell_\theta\ge\Lambda(\theta)/\theta=p(\theta)$; and $p(\theta)>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$, since
otherwise $\zeta_\theta$ would minimize $P$ and equal $\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}$ by
Lemma~\ref{lem:var-basic}\ref{lem:var-basic-a}, while
$\zeta_\theta(\{0\})\ge\theta>\theta_*=\zeta_{\mathrm{P}}(\{0\})$.

\ref{rem:max-overlap-c} The lower limit in Theorem~\ref{thm:exist}\ref{thm:exist-d} is
nondecreasing in $\varepsilon$ and tends to $\Sigma(f)$ as $\varepsilon\downarrow0$, so it is at
least $\Sigma(f)$ for each fixed $\varepsilon$. Hence, for all large $N$, the conditioning event
$\{|N^{-1}M_N-f|\le\varepsilon\}$ has probability at least $e^{N(\Sigma(f)-1)}$. On it, $F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\geM_N-\varepsilon N$ implies
$F_{\mathrm{TAP}}(x)\ge N(f-2\varepsilon)$, and $f-2\varepsilon>f_{\mathrm{eq}}$ because $\varepsilon<(f-f_{\mathrm{eq}})/4$.
Apply~\ref{rem:max-overlap-a} at the level $f-2\varepsilon$ with the rate $c+1-\Sigma(f)$, which
is positive because $\Sigma\le0$; it gives $\kappa$ such that the unconditional probability of the
event is at most $e^{-(c+1-\Sigma(f))N}$ for every $N$. Dividing gives the bound $e^{-cN}$.
<!-- end proof-56 -->
<!-- remark-18: body_md -->
\label{rem:rpde}
The class $\mathcal{C}$ enters our proofs only through facts on the Parisi equation and on the
functionals $\mathrm{TAP}(\mu,\zeta)$ that we cite from \cite{CPS} (Theorems~5 and~12, Lemma~37, and
Section~11 there), from \cite{AC15a,AC15b} and from \cite{Che17}. These papers state their models
under a summability condition such as $\sum_p2^p\beta_p^2<\infty$, which there serves to define the
Hamiltonian, while the cited statements involve $\xi$ only through $\xi'$ and $\xi''$ on $[0,1]$.
If they hold for every $\xi$ satisfying \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}, then every statement of this paper made for
$\xi\in\mathcal{C}$ holds under \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}\ (together with \hyperref[hyp:H]{\textup{(H)}}\ where it is assumed). We have not
checked their proofs in that generality, and we do not claim this extension. It would add the
covariances with $\sum_p2^p\beta_p^2=\infty$, all of which have radius of convergence at most two;
covariances of radius two with $\sum_p2^p\beta_p^2<\infty$ already lie in $\mathcal{C}$. The rest of
this subsection gives details.
<!-- end remark-18 -->
<!-- head-2: body_md -->
Appendix~\ref{app:matrix-gaussian} and Lemma~\ref{lem:matrix-uniform} use only \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}. Everywhere
else we assume $\xi\in\mathcal{C}$, which implies \hyperref[hyp:R]{\textup{(R)}}: the regularity of the Parisi equation in
Lemma~\ref{lem:pde-standing} is proved for this class. Wherever $\zeta_f$ and the objects defined from
it appear ($C_f$, $L_{Q}$, $U_Q$, $\chi_Q$, $\Delta$, $\rho_Q$, $\nu_Q$, $\lambda_+$), the standing
